suggestion.title: Unauthenticated database export via ALWAYS_PROTECTED bypass (CVE-2026-55500)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states '/api/settings/database endpoint allows full database export…without any authentication requirement beyond the ALWAYS_PROTECTED middleware check, which only validates JWT or CLI token.' Need detection for requests circumventing or spoofing this middleware.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP requests to /api/settings/database with GET method returning 200 OK + large payloads (>1MB). Correlate with missing/invalid JWT tokens, CLI tokens from unexpected sources, or requests from external IPs. Flag rapid sequences of export requests from same source.

suggestion.title: Malicious database import causing mass credential overwrite (CVE-2026-55500)
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'full database import (complete overwrite)' capability. Detection should identify when POST requests to /api/settings/database result in abnormal database mutations: mass password hash changes, OAuth token resets, settings overwrites detected in application logs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate POST requests to /api/settings/database with subsequent application logs showing database schema changes, mass credential updates, OAuth token resets, or unusual user account modifications. Flag when import occurs outside maintenance windows or without corresponding backup/restore tickets.

suggestion.title: Credential exfiltration and reuse post-database-export (CVE-2026-55500)
suggestion.rationale: Article notes exported database contains 'all credentials, API keys, OAuth tokens'. After export, attacker will use these credentials. Detection should identify authentication events using credentials sourced from 9routers instance (impossible-travel, new geographies, unusual user-agent combinations).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for successful authentications immediately following failed attempts using same credentials from different IP/user-agent. Correlate OAuth/API token usage patterns: legitimate tokens show stable geographic + device fingerprint; stolen tokens show sudden changes in source IP, user-agent, or service access patterns.

suggestion.title: Detection of ALWAYS_PROTECTED middleware bypass attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article states endpoint is 'protected' only by ALWAYS_PROTECTED middleware (JWT or CLI token validation). Attacker must either forge/steal valid tokens or bypass check. Detection should flag requests to /api/settings/database with malformed, expired, or missing auth headers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor requests to /api/settings/database with HTTP 401/403 status codes followed by 200 OK from same source within short window, indicating potential token-forging or bypass. Flag requests with malformed Authorization headers, bearer tokens with invalid signatures, or requests missing Authorization header entirely returning 200 OK.

suggestion.title: Bulk reconnaissance: CVE-2026-55500 scanning for /api/settings/database exposure
suggestion.rationale: Pre-exploitation phase. Attacker will scan for exposed 9routers instances or enumerate /api/settings/database endpoint availability before attempting export. Article establishes endpoint is the attack surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect scanning pattern: multiple HEAD/OPTIONS/GET requests to /api/settings/database from single source across multiple targets or repeated requests returning 401/403/404 before successful 200. Flag any single source making >5 requests to /api/settings/database endpoint in <1 hour.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable halo2_gadgets Installation Detected
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'variable-base scalar multiplication gadget of halo2_gadgets allowed a malicious prover'—software inventory must actively flag unpatched halo2_gadgets versions in running Zebra nodes or Rust projects importing the crate.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Cargo.lock or package.json entries referencing halo2_gadgets versions prior to the patched release. Cross-reference with running Zebra node processes to confirm active exploitation surface.

suggestion.title: Orchard Circuit Proof Verification Failure Spike
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'under-constrained base, breaking Orchard Action circuit soundness'—a malicious prover exploiting the gadget flaw will generate invalid proofs that pass local verification on the vulnerable node but fail downstream consensus checks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Zebra application logs for repeated proof-verification errors or divergence-to-network errors on Orchard transactions (valid locally but rejected by peers), which would indicate either the vulnerability being exploited or a node running the flawed gadget generating invalid proofs.

suggestion.title: Zebra Node Halo2_Gadgets Version Drift from Network Consensus
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies the bug 'allows a malicious prover to produce a valid proof' for Orchard transactions—a node with the vulnerable gadget may diverge from network consensus if it accepts proofs peers reject or vice versa.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag Zebra nodes exhibiting sudden consensus divergence or fork-reorg patterns coinciding with Orchard transaction processing, which would indicate the node's proof-verification logic is out of sync with the network (possibly due to the vulnerable gadget).

suggestion.title: Cypher query injection payload detection — suspicious APOC function calls
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'query text is influenceable by prompt injection' via APOC/dbms functions leading to 'config-conditional RCE'. Pipeline missed detection for the actual payload: Cypher queries containing dangerous APOC functions (apoc.cypher.run, apoc.load.json, dbms.executeSystemCommand, dbms.executionEngine). These are the weaponized query patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Neo4j network traffic or driver logs for Cypher queries containing APOC function calls outside of whitelist. Correlate with user-supplied input (HTTP params, file upload content, RAG sources) to detect prompt injection. Flag queries with string concatenation operators or comment-injection syntax (// -- /* */).

suggestion.title: LLM output stream anomaly — Cypher syntax injection patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'LLM-generated Cypher without validation, no statement-type allowlist'. The pipeline should detect when an LLM model outputs Cypher containing structural modifications (UNION, MATCH, DELETE, SET) that deviate from expected query templates. This is the generation point where injection occurs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Log all Cypher queries generated by Langroid ChatAgent. Baseline expected query structures (SELECT-only, parameterized). Flag queries with: unexpected keywords (DELETE, DROP, UNWIND), command separators, escaped quotes, or byte-order markers. Correlate with preceding LLM prompt to confirm injection vector.

suggestion.title: RAG source contamination — prompt injection via retrieval pipeline
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'indirect content the agent reads back via RAG' can influence query execution. The pipeline missed detection of poisoned data entering the RAG retrieval system before it reaches the LLM. External knowledge bases, APIs, or document stores could inject malicious Cypher fragments.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor external data sources feeding the RAG system for injection payloads (Cypher syntax, command patterns). Detect when retrieval results contain queries or code-like structures. Flag documents added to knowledge base containing APOC/dbms patterns. Correlate retrieved content with subsequent Neo4j queries.

suggestion.title: Missing input validation checkpoint — Neo4jChatAgent initialization without gating
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'no validation, no statement-type allowlist, and no opt-out gate'. Detection should focus on application configuration and runtime state: when Neo4jChatAgent is instantiated without security controls enabled. This is the precondition check.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan application code or startup logs for Neo4jChatAgent instantiation. Detect missing parameters: allow_statement_types whitelist, query_validation_func, use_apoc_disabled flag. Cross-reference with Neo4j server capabilities: check if APOC plugin is loaded and unrestricted. Alert if agent is active + APOC enabled + no input validation.

suggestion.title: Neo4j driver statement-type anomaly — execution of unexpected query classes
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'no statement-type allowlist' implies legitimate use should only execute READ queries. Any WRITE/DELETE/MODIFY operations from the ChatAgent connection are suspicious by design. This is a high-confidence divergence from expected behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enable Neo4j query audit logging. Filter for queries originating from the Langroid application user/connection. Baseline all legitimate query types (expected: MATCH, RETURN, optional: CREATE if building graph). Alert on DELETE, DROP, SET (data modification), CALL APOC, or dbms.* statements. Flag multi-statement queries or transactions. Correlate with LLM request logs to confirm injection occurred between prompt and execution.

suggestion.title: Privilege escalation via Neo4j user role mismatch — APOC function availability to unprivileged role
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'config-conditional RCE' suggests APOC functions are accessible based on Neo4j user privileges. If Langroid runs with admin or unrestricted role, APOC becomes available. Detection should check role-capability misalignment and detect when application context has unexpected permissions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Audit Neo4j user roles assigned to Langroid connections. Verify Langroid application user has minimal role (read-only, specific database). Alert if role includes APOC or administrative privileges. Cross-check Neo4j version: APOC in 4.0+ should be restricted via neo4j.conf settings (dbms.security.procedures.allowlist). Flag deployments missing restrictive ACL or with APOC globally enabled.

suggestion.title: Rapid endpoint scanning for 9router API paths
suggestion.rationale: Advisory states endpoints 'lack authentication entirely'; attackers would scan to discover them. Article explicitly lists /api/providers, /api/usage/stats, /api/usage/request-logs, /api/usage/request-details. Should detect reconnaissance: high cardinality URI-path requests or 404→200 pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Single source issuing 20+ distinct GET requests to /api/* paths from 9router instance within 5min, or sequence of 404 responses followed by 200 responses to same endpoint class. Correlate on source IP + host + time window.

suggestion.title: Suspicious bulk export of API keys / conversation records from /api/usage/request-details
suggestion.rationale: Advisory warns of 'full API key leak' and conversation data exposure. Article mentions /api/usage/request-details/* endpoint. Should flag exfiltration patterns: high-volume sequential reads to request-details variants or large cumulative response bodies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Unauthenticated source querying 50+ distinct /api/usage/request-details/* endpoints or cumulative HTTP response exceeding 50MB within 30min. Pair with outbound data-flow telemetry to external IPs.

suggestion.title: Provider configuration tampering post-authentication bypass
suggestion.rationale: Article warns of 'rogue provider / key swap' and DoS via provider CRUD. Should correlate unauthorized /api/providers mutations with downstream provider-config changes in application state or credential stores.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: POST/PUT to /api/providers from unauthenticated/anomalous source followed by provider configuration modifications in backend storage within 5min. Alert on provider state changes (endpoint, credentials, enabled-flag) without corresponding legitimate admin action.

suggestion.title: Stolen API keys from leaked /api/usage/stats used in external API calls
suggestion.rationale: Advisory emphasizes 'full API key leak.' Extracted keys would be exfiltrated or used by attacker. Should detect key material observed in /api/usage/stats response bodies appearing in subsequent outbound HTTPS or external API usage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Extract API key patterns (hex/JWT-like tokens) from successful /api/usage/stats GET responses; monitor for same key values in outbound Authorization headers, POST bodies, or query parameters to external domains. High-confidence indicator of key theft and abuse.

suggestion.title: Privilege escalation via provider-credential injection
suggestion.rationale: Unauthenticated provider CRUD allows attacker to inject provider credentials (e.g., attacker-controlled API keys, endpoints). This can enable lateral movement or privilege escalation if those credentials grant access to downstream systems.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: New provider created or modified via /api/providers POST/PUT with mismatched provider_name / endpoint / credentials. Correlate with subsequent successful authentication or API calls from 9router to that provider using those credentials, especially if provider is high-privilege (internal service, database, secret manager).

suggestion.title: Python eval()/exec() with LLM-generated code execution
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'When these agents evaluate LLM-generated tool messages with full_eval=True'—the core vulnerability is dynamic code evaluation. This is the exploitation phase; currently undetected. No hunt for eval(), exec(), compile(), or __import__() calls with untrusted input.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Python processes calling eval, exec, or compile with argument strings originating from network input, tool outputs, or LLM integration points. Correlate child process spawning immediately after eval/exec calls to identify post-exploitation activity.

suggestion.title: Exploit public-facing Langroid API with malicious tool messages (T1190)
suggestion.rationale: Article references T1190 but no UC hunts the initial exploitation. Vulnerability is triggered via 'LLM-generated tool messages' fed to TableChatAgent/VectorStore. Missing detection for malicious crafted messages or unusual agent input patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Langroid TableChatAgent and VectorStore query logs for messages containing eval(), exec(), subprocess keywords, or code syntax. Correlate with unusual Python process spawning or multi-stage eval patterns within seconds of tool message ingestion.

suggestion.title: Tool transfer and staging post-RCE (T1105 — Ingress Tool Transfer)
suggestion.rationale: Article lists T1105 as technique but no UC hunts for tool downloads. RCE payload typically stages secondary tools. Missing detection for curl/wget initiated by child shells to fetch payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag curl/wget/PowerShell downloads spawned from Python or shell children, especially to ephemeral paths (/tmp, %TEMP%), with executable or script extensions, or from suspicious domains.

suggestion.title: VectorStore eval() injection via malicious vector queries
suggestion.rationale: Article names VectorStore as vulnerable but no UC addresses vector query evaluation. Missing detection for eval() or filter operations on LLM-generated query strings within VectorStore operations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Python VectorStore query/filter/search calls that invoke eval() with untrusted query content. Monitor for code-injection patterns in vector filter expressions or query metadata parsed as code.

suggestion.title: Symlink/hardlink creation by archive-extraction processes targeting paths outside extraction root
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'A link (hardlink) or symlink entry is created without checking where its target points.' This is the core attack vector but no detection hunt addresses symlink/hardlink creation itself.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for symlink (ln -s) or hardlink (ln) creation by archive utilities (node, tar, unzip, 7z) where link target contains parent-directory traversal (..) or absolute paths (/etc, /root, /usr) outside declared extraction directory.

suggestion.title: Cron/systemd script execution following archive extraction to /etc/cron.* or /etc/systemd/system
suggestion.rationale: Article describes writing to cron and systemd paths (—these enable persistence, but pipeline detects only the write, not activation. Article: writes to '/etc/cron.d/*', '/etc/cron.hourly/*', '/etc/systemd/system/*' are escalation vectors.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate DeviceFileEvents (cron/systemd file creation by node) with DeviceProcessEvents showing execution of scripts in those paths within 5 minutes, with no legitimate package-manager parent process.

suggestion.title: Setuid/ld.so.preload-based privilege escalation following node-driven archive extraction
suggestion.rationale: Article lists T1548.001 and T1574.006 as techniques but provides no detection for the *exploitation* phase: pipeline detects file writes to /etc/ld.so.preload but not subsequent binary execution that loads it.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when process execution follows write to /etc/ld.so.preload or /usr/local/sbin (written by node) within 2 minutes, especially if the executed binary shows privilege escalation artifacts (UID change, capability gain).

suggestion.title: SSH authorized_keys or sudoers.d file injection via archive extraction by unprivileged node process
suggestion.rationale: UC_5_2 monitors these paths but doesn't distinguish between legitimate system updates and malicious injection. Article: attacker-controlled archives write to '/.ssh/authorized_keys', '/etc/sudoers.d/*'—these are direct-access persistence vectors.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect file modification to ~/.ssh/authorized_keys or /etc/sudoers.d/* by node/nodejs process running as unprivileged user (not root, not system service accounts). Baseline on approved SSH key management tools.

suggestion.title: Cavern C2 Command-and-Control Beacon Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly discusses 'new Cavern C2 Framework' as the attack vehicle. Pipeline extracted zero IOCs and no C2-phase kill-chain. Detecting beacon traffic to known C2 infrastructure is the primary defensive value from this article.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP/HTTPS outbound connections to known Cavern C2 domains and IP addresses, particularly on non-standard ports. Look for beaconing patterns: regular, small-payload requests to the same C2 host with consistent User-Agent strings and encrypted body content.

suggestion.title: Iran-Linked Spear Phishing and Credential Harvesting
suggestion.rationale: Iran-linked APT groups (APT33, APT34, etc.) invariably use spear-phishing for initial access; article references 'targeting Israeli organizations' implying targeted delivery. No initial-access detection logic generated by pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag emails with .exe, .scr, .lnk, or macro-enabled Office attachments sent to Israeli defense, government, or critical infrastructure sectors. Correlate sender domain reputation, domain age, and SPF/DKIM alignment. Watch for credential-harvesting landing pages spoofing Israeli organization portals.

suggestion.title: Cavern C2 Process Injection and Memory Persistence
suggestion.rationale: Typical Iran APT tradecraft involves process hollowing/injection (T1543, T1055) to evade EDR; no execution-phase detection or technique mapping by pipeline despite 'framework' language implying sophisticated post-exploitation capability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unsigned/anomalous child processes spawned by legitimate system processes (svchost.exe, lsass.exe, explorer.exe). Flag processes with parent-child mismatch (e.g., csrss.exe spawning cmd.exe or powershell.exe) and unusual DLL loads in System32 contexts.

suggestion.title: Registry Persistence: Run Key and Scheduled Task Injection
suggestion.rationale: Iran-linked APTs establish persistence via HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run and Scheduled Tasks; no persistence-phase kill-chain generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for creation of new Registry values in Run/RunOnce keys and HKCU startup folders, especially with randomized names or obfuscated paths. Alert on Scheduled Task creation with suspicious triggers (logon, system startup) or Task XML containing encoded/base64 payloads.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Kerberoasting and SMB Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Iran APTs enumerate domain trusts and exploit Kerberos; article states targeting 'Israeli organizations' (likely domain-joined networks) but pipeline reconstructed zero lateral-movement phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for TGS requests (Event ID 4769) with unusual service accounts and RC4 encryption. Alert on failed SMB authentication storms (4625 events) followed by successful logon (4624) on non-standard hours, indicating credential stuffing followed by lateral movement.

suggestion.title: Exfiltration Over Encrypted C2 Channel
suggestion.rationale: Article's focus on 'Israeli organizations' implies targeting of sensitive data; pipeline failed to generate exfiltration-phase detection despite T1041 being standard for C2 frameworks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline organizational network egress and alert on anomalous outbound data volumes to new external IPs/domains. Correlate file-open events (rare, large files) with network spike timing. Monitor for DNS exfiltration: unusually long or base64-encoded DNS queries to external nameservers.

suggestion.title: KVM Guest Memory Boundary Violation
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'guest VMs escape to host'—detection should trigger on memory access patterns crossing VM boundaries. Exploitation requires reading/writing host kernel memory from guest context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when QEMU/KVM processes attempt mmap() or madvise() syscalls with flags that cross EPT (Extended Page Table) boundaries, or when guest vCPU threads access host-owned memory regions. Correlate with abnormal page table walks or TLB flushing patterns not typical of legitimate VM operations.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation via KVM Architectural Flaw
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 16-year-old Linux KVM flaw on Intel and AMD; indicates exploitation path from guest kernel code to host kernel execution. 'x86 systems' suggests architecture-specific CPU feature abuse (e.g., TSX, EPT misconfiguration).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect processes running in guest context executing privileged CPU instructions or KVM-specific hypercalls not permitted from guest ring level. Flag repeated vmcall invocations with arguments attempting to modify host page tables or CPU registers.

suggestion.title: Host Kernel Module Load from Guest-Attributed Process
suggestion.rationale: Successful VM escape implies ability to inject code into host kernel; article's 'lets guest VMs escape to host' suggests eventual host kernel compromise. Detect anomalous module loading.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for insmod() or modprobe operations where parent process is qemu-system-* or within guest namespace, or where memory origin is guest-allocated regions. Flag any kernel module load lacking signed driver certificate when kernel module signing is enforced.

suggestion.title: Host Root Filesystem Access from KVM Guest Thread
suggestion.rationale: Article indicates host compromise once escape succeeds. Post-exploitation, attacker gains access to host /etc, /boot, /root directories. Detect suspicious FS traversal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file open/read operations targeting host root FS paths (/boot, /etc, /root, /var/log) from qemu or kvm-attributed processes, especially rapid directory enumeration or attempts to read sensitive files (shadow, sudoers, authorized_keys).

suggestion.title: Exploitation of x86 TSX or EPT Side-Channel in KVM
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'Intel and AMD x86 systems'; 16-year-old KVM flaw likely leverages hardware-specific CPU features (TSX transactional abort, EPT misconfiguration). Detect architectural exploitation patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for abnormal TSX_ABORT counts, excessive EPT misses, or patterns of speculative memory reads followed by privileged memory access in KVM vCPU contexts. Flag processes triggering repeated transactional aborts followed by successful privileged memory operations.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-45659 Detected on Exposed SharePoint Servers
suggestion.rationale: Article states CISA KEV implies active wild exploitation; 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' is explicitly recommended. Vulnerability scanner detection is the first gate for a public-facing application under active attack.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any vulnerability scan detection of CVE-2026-45659 on SharePoint Server instances. Correlate with network exposure scanning to confirm internet accessibility. Treat positive findings with federal-deadline urgency (due 2026-07-04).

suggestion.title: Deserialization Attack Exploitation Attempts Against SharePoint
suggestion.rationale: Article core vulnerability: 'deserialization of untrusted data.' Attackers will send malicious .NET serialized objects to trigger code execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to SharePoint for serialized object payloads (BinaryFormatter, DataContractSerializer markers, base64-encoded binary content) targeting deserialization endpoints. Flag requests with suspicious Content-Type or abnormally large payloads.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Process Execution from SharePoint Worker Processes
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'allows an authorized attacker to execute code over a network.' Post-exploitation phase: arbitrary code execution under w3wp.exe or owstimer.exe process context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unexpected child processes spawned from w3wp.exe (SharePoint worker) or owstimer.exe (timer service), especially cmd.exe, powershell.exe, rundll32.exe, or csc.exe without documented maintenance windows. Establish baseline of legitimate SharePoint spawned processes first.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized SharePoint Administration Activity Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article permits 'authorized attacker' code execution; threat actors will likely persist via SharePoint admin credentials or object model calls to add backdoor accounts or malicious features.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor SharePoint audit logs for unexpected user creation, permission elevation, or feature activation by non-admin service accounts. Flag brute-force attempts against SharePoint admin accounts correlating with exploitation attempt timestamps.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-45659 SharePoint Public-Facing Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'exploit...to execute code over a network' and explicitly maps T1190. Must detect inbound exploitation targeting exposed SharePoint instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for anomalous HTTP POST/PUT requests to SharePoint root web, _vti_bin/ paths, and known exploit endpoints. Flag requests with serialized .NET payloads, unusual Content-Encoding, or mismatched User-Agent patterns. Correlate with vulnerability scan results to find exposed SharePoint on external interfaces.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Process Execution from SharePoint Worker Process
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'execute code' via deserialization; successful exploitation spawns child processes from w3wp.exe/SharePoint services.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on cmd.exe, powershell.exe, certutil.exe, or rundll32.exe spawned by w3wp.exe or SharePoint-related service accounts with unusual command-line arguments, working directory, or network connections.

suggestion.title: Unpatched CVE-2026-45659 SharePoint Inventory Gap
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Federal patch due: 2026-07-04' and emphasizes 'patch lag is the silent killer'. Compliance requires confirmation even on systems reported as patched.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner for all SharePoint Server instances. Cross-check patch levels against Microsoft security bulletins. Flag gaps between scan date and patch date. Audit systems missing expected KB updates across the fleet.

suggestion.title: Network C2 from Compromised SharePoint Service Account
suggestion.rationale: Article indicates authorized remote code execution leads to post-compromise activity; compromised SharePoint services are strategic persistence/lateral-movement pivot points.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound connections from SharePoint app-pool and service accounts to external or suspicious internal IP ranges. Flag DNS lookups for known C2 domains, unusual ports (4444, 5555, 8888), or beaconing patterns. Correlate with file writes to temp/ProgramData for staged payloads.

suggestion.title: Asset inventory: Vulnerable SharePoint Server versions (CVE-2026-45659)
suggestion.rationale: Article states entry is in CISA KEV ('observed exploited in the wild') with mandatory federal remediation by 2026-07-04. Article phrase: 'Standard asset-exposure hunt — the canonical Splunk SPL and Defender KQL live once in [.../_TEMPLATES.md#asset-exposure].' Pipeline generated zero use cases despite this explicit template reference.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference organizational asset inventory against known-vulnerable SharePoint Server versions for CVE-2026-45659. Alert on any unpatched instances where remediation deadline (2026-07-04) has passed, particularly those reachable from untrusted networks.

suggestion.title: Exploitation detection: Suspicious deserialization payloads to SharePoint endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article describes core vector as 'deserialization of untrusted data vulnerability which allows authorized attacker to execute code over a network.' Pipeline failed to generate exploitation-phase detection despite this being the active attack mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor SharePoint Server w3wp.exe for anomalous HTTP POST requests containing serialized .NET objects targeting SOAP/REST endpoints. Correlate with external or low-reputation source IPs. Detect unusual gadget chains (ObjectDataProvider, WindowsIdentity, etc.) in request payloads before deserialization.

suggestion.title: Post-exploitation execution: Unexpected process spawning from SharePoint worker process
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability leads to code execution. No detection use case was generated for the execution phase despite RCE being the stated impact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect abnormal child processes spawned by w3wp.exe (SharePoint IIS worker) such as cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or rundll32.exe without corresponding application-level initialization events. Correlate timing with inbound network traffic from untrusted sources.

suggestion.title: Patch compliance: CVE-2026-45659 remediation status post-deadline
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes federal deadline 2026-07-04 and states 'patch lag is the silent killer.' No compliance or patch-status detection was generated despite patch verification being the primary mitigation strategy.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query patch management database to flag SharePoint Server instances still running unpatched versions as of deadline date. Escalate findings for environments with internet-facing instances or those serving high-criticality business functions.

suggestion.title: Patch Compliance Hunt: CVE-2026-45659 SharePoint Instances
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states CVE-2026-45659 is in CISA KEV (active exploitation) with federal patch due 2026-07-04; any unpatched instance is directly at-risk.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanners and patch-management systems to inventory all SharePoint Server instances and flag those not at a patched version for CVE-2026-45659. Prioritize instances with internet exposure.

suggestion.title: SharePoint Deserialization Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifically describes 'deserialization of untrusted data vulnerability'; exploitation payloads will contain binary serialization markers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor SharePoint HTTP endpoints for requests containing .NET BinaryFormatter headers (AQIDAA) or suspiciously large POST bodies to file handlers (.asmx, web service paths). Cross-correlate with failed authentication or unusual user-agents.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Code Execution from SharePoint Process
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'allows...execute code over a network'; successful exploitation manifests as child process creation under w3wp.exe or OWSTIMER.EXE with unexpected cmdline or network activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on child processes spawned by SharePoint worker processes (w3wp.exe, OWSTIMER.EXE) that have not been whitelisted, especially those executing scripts, spawning cmd.exe, or making outbound network connections.

suggestion.title: Internet-Exposed SharePoint Asset Inventory
suggestion.rationale: MITRE context notes 'KEV implies active exploitation against exposed assets'; CISA KEV entries target public-facing instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate all externally resolvable SharePoint server hostnames via DNS and test network reachability to ports 80, 443, and SharePoint management ports. Cross-correlate unpatched instances with public exposure to triage critical risk.

suggestion.title: SharePoint Diagnostic Log Anomalies During Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes active exploitation in the wild (CISA KEV); failed and successful deserialization attempts are logged in SharePoint diagnostic logs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor SharePoint ULS logs (Unified Logging System) for deserialization errors, cryptographic exceptions, or unexpected object instantiation failures that precede successful code execution or process spawning.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-45659 Vulnerability Scanner Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly directs: 'CVE-2026-45659 — match against your vulnerability scanner.' Pipeline extracted zero IOCs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query all vulnerability scanners for detections of CVE-2026-45659 on Microsoft SharePoint Server assets. CISA KEV status indicates active exploitation—prioritize unpatched instances and flag systems with detection status and patch-due date 2026-07-04.

suggestion.title: Microsoft SharePoint Server Asset-Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'Standard asset-exposure hunt — the canonical Splunk SPL and Defender KQL live once in ../_TEMPLATES.md#asset-exposure. Substitute this CVE wherever the template references <CVE>'. Pipeline generated zero UCs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate all internet-facing Microsoft SharePoint Server instances (standard ports 80, 443; SharePoint proprietary ports). Cross-reference against patch/vulnerability management for CVE-2026-45659 patch status. CISA KEV implies active scanning and exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: Deserialization Exploit Detection — SharePoint

Flag any unpatched SharePoint servers. Correlate with external threat-intel for active scanning/probing activity targeting SharePoint.

suggestion.title: Failed Authentication to Successful Exploitation Sequence
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'authorized attacker' implies credential compromise pathway. Pipeline missed initial access chain showing failed auth attempts preceding exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate sequences of HTTP 401/403 responses to SharePoint endpoints from external IP, followed by successful authenticated requests. Flag if credentials used belong to service account or disabled user—indicates takeover.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Lateral Movement from SharePoint
suggestion.rationale: Compromised public-facing SharePoint becomes network pivot; article states 'execute code over a network.' Pipeline missed lateral movement detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected outbound connections from SharePoint server to internal infrastructure (DC, file servers, SQL). Alert if spawned from non-standard service process. Correlate process creation events on same host with code execution timestamps.

suggestion.title: SharePoint Server Public Exposure Hunting
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker can exploit 'over a network' and CISA KEV status confirms active exploitation in the wild. Network-accessible SharePoint instances are the attack surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan for SharePoint services on standard ports (443, 80, 8080) and alternate HTTP/S ports. Correlate vulnerability scanner alerts for CVE-2026-45659 with network accessibility logs. Alert on unpatched instances after federal due date 2026-07-04.

suggestion.title: Deserialization Payload Detection in SharePoint Requests
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'deserialization of untrusted data' as the vulnerability mechanism. Exploitation requires sending malicious serialized objects; these appear as anomalous request bodies to SharePoint endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor POST/PUT requests to SharePoint webservices and _api endpoints for base64-encoded or binary serialized .NET object signatures (System.Runtime.Serialization markers, CLR payload indicators). Alert on abnormal request entropy or size to vulnerable SharePoint paths.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Child Process Execution from SharePoint
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'allows code execution'; successful exploitation manifests as command spawning. SharePoint processes (w3wp.exe, owstimer.exe) normally do not launch cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or non-system interpreters.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on cmd.exe, powershell.exe, csc.exe, or net.exe spawned as children of w3wp.exe or owstimer.exe without corresponding SharePoint administrative action. Monitor for unsigned or suspicious dlls loaded by SharePoint processes post-initial compromise.

suggestion.title: Outbound Network Connections from SharePoint Application
suggestion.rationale: Post-execution, attacker code running in SharePoint context may establish C2 or stage secondary payloads. Outbound network activity from SharePoint processes is anomalous outside normal replication/federation scenarios.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected outbound connections from w3wp.exe or owstimer.exe to non-internal hosts, especially on ports 443, 8080, or high-numbered ports. Alert on DNS queries initiated by SharePoint processes to external or recently-registered domains.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-45659 Patch Compliance Enforcement
suggestion.rationale: Federal civilian agencies required to patch by 2026-07-04. Any unpatched SharePoint instance post-deadline remains exposed to documented active exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Run vulnerability scans weekly post-due-date against all SharePoint Server instances. Generate daily alerts for non-compliant systems. Cross-reference unpatched, network-exposed instances for immediate remediation priority.

suggestion.title: Detect Exposed or Exploited SharePoint Deserialization (CVE-2026-45659)
suggestion.rationale: Article states CVE is 'actively exploited in the wild' and lists it in CISA KEV; recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt.' Pipeline produced no UC despite explicit guidance to hunt for this CVE.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect inbound requests to SharePoint Server on ports 80/443 with payloads indicative of deserialization exploit attempts (e.g., base64-encoded .NET objects, unusual binary content-type). Correlate with failed authentication or anomalous request patterns. Baseline normal SharePoint traffic and flag deviations.

suggestion.title: Monitor Abnormal Process Execution from SharePoint Service Accounts
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'authorized attacker to execute code over a network' — implies post-exploitation code execution. No UC for detecting unusual child processes, network connections, or file activity spawned by SharePoint services.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected process spawning from SharePoint worker processes (w3wp.exe, spoolsv.exe under SharePoint context) — particularly cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or net.exe. Monitor for outbound network connections from SharePoint PIDs. Establish baseline of legitimate SharePoint child processes and hunt deviations.

suggestion.title: Detect Suspicious .NET Deserialization Events
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability root cause is 'deserialization of untrusted data' — article emphasizes this as the attack vector. No UC for detecting abnormal deserialization, gadget chain loading, or unsafe reflection in SharePoint context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for .NET runtime warnings/errors related to deserialization, unsafe reflection, or serialization gadget chains in event logs (keywords: BinaryFormatter, ObjectInputStream, TypeConfusedDelegate). Cross-reference with SharePoint process context and unusual assembly loads.

suggestion.title: Track CVE-2026-45659 Patch Compliance Against Federal Deadline
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'Federal patch due: 2026-07-04' and notes 'patch lag is the silent killer.' Pipeline missed compliance/asset-inventory UC entirely despite explicit deadline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner output and patch management logs to inventory all SharePoint Server instances, flag unpatched hosts, and correlate against patch-deployment logs. Generate compliance report showing time-to-remediation vs. federal deadline; escalate any > 14 days past due.

suggestion.title: Detect Unauthorized SharePoint Administrative Activity Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'authorized attacker' but realistic scenario includes compromise of legitimate credentials, leading to administrative object manipulation. No UC for detecting anomalous SharePoint admin operations (site creation, user addition, permission changes).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor SharePoint ULS logs and audit trails for anomalous admin actions: new site collections, hidden sites, user group additions, permission escalations, content deployment. Baseline expected admin behavior and flag after-hours or unusual-account administrative activity.

suggestion.title: BeyondTrust Remote Support/PRA Unauthenticated Access Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes critical authentication bypass affecting Remote Support and PRA. Attackers can bypass auth controls entirely. No detection use case generated despite this being the primary attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests to BeyondTrust Remote Support/PRA endpoints (typically /api/auth*, /oauth*, /session endpoints) that originate from non-whitelisted sources or that lack valid authorization tokens. Flag attempts with 200/204 responses following authentication bypass patterns (e.g., missing or malformed credential headers followed by successful request).

suggestion.title: Successful Post-Auth-Bypass Remote Access Session
suggestion.rationale: Authentication bypass allows unauthorized session establishment. Article implies remote access capability post-bypass but pipeline did not map post-exploitation behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect new BeyondTrust remote session initiation from previously unauthenticated source IP/user context, or sessions that span unusual geographic regions within minutes. Correlate with suspicious process execution on target systems during these sessions.

suggestion.title: BeyondTrust Endpoint Reconnaissance Pre-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Auth bypass vulnerabilities are typically preceded by reconnaissance of target endpoints. Article does not detail pre-attack behavior, but detection pipeline should cover reconnaissance patterns against BeyondTrust infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect elevated HTTP request volume or unusual endpoint scanning against BeyondTrust Remote Support/PRA hosts, including 404/401 responses indicating fuzzing of authentication paths, SSL certificate enumeration, or version fingerprinting requests.

suggestion.title: BeyondTrust Vulnerability Exploitation Pattern (CVE-2026-XXXX)
suggestion.rationale: Article references specific critical flaws but pipeline extracted no CVE identifiers or patched-version signatures. Detection should key off known vulnerable version responses.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect requests to known vulnerable BeyondTrust endpoints (e.g., /api/Authentication/AuthenticateUser without proper token validation) or responses indicating vulnerable version headers (e.g., Server: BeyondTrust Remote Support < patched version). Flag requests with authentication bypass payloads (empty credentials, SQL injection patterns in auth parameters, JWT manipulation).

suggestion.title: Detect Creation of Hidden Admin Accounts on Tenda Routers
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes 'hidden admin backdoor' in firmware. Adversary would need to establish covert privileged access. Detection should monitor for unexpected admin account creation or modification via router configuration files or management interfaces.
log_sources: Web server access logs (router management UI)
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Tenda router admin account management for unauthorized account creation or credential modification. Track filesystem changes to /etc/passwd or equivalent router credential stores, and log all successful administrative web UI logins with unusual IP/geolocation pairing. Alert on account creation during off-hours or with credential patterns matching hardcoded defaults.

suggestion.title: Detect Firmware Modification or Unauthorized Downgrade on Tenda Routers
suggestion.rationale: Backdoor persistence requires firmware compromise. 'Hidden' implies pre-installation at supply-chain or post-compromise persistence. Detection must identify firmware tampering or rollback to vulnerable versions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline firmware integrity hashes (boot partition, kernel, root filesystem) for each Tenda router model. Alert on firmware version downgrades, unexpected rollbacks to older versions, or modifications to firmware signatures. Monitor for failed firmware verification events or bypass of firmware update validation.

suggestion.title: Detect Anomalous Outbound Connections from Tenda Router to Unknown C2
suggestion.rationale: Hidden backdoor implies remote activation capability. Article does not cite observed C2, but detection should target potential command-and-control communication originating from compromised router hardware.
log_sources: Layer 7 proxy logs (if router traffic inspected)
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound connections originating from Tenda router WAN interface for unknown IP destinations, especially to non-standard ports or with TLS/encryption indicators. Cross-reference router IP reputation feeds. Alert on DNS queries from router management VLAN to suspicious domains or newly registered registrant names.

suggestion.title: Detect Unauthorized Remote Access Sessions via Telnet/SSH on Tenda Router
suggestion.rationale: Admin backdoor enables remote access. Article specifies 'admin' access, implying remote management session capability. Detection should identify unexpected management protocol usage from external sources.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for successful SSH/Telnet sessions to Tenda router management interface from WAN-sourced IPs or IP ranges not matching known administrator geolocations. Alert on authentication attempts using default credentials or non-standard usernames. Correlate with failed login attempts preceding successful sessions (brute-force indicators).

suggestion.title: Detect Tenda Router Acting as MITM for Traffic Interception
suggestion.rationale: Hidden admin backdoor in router enables network interception. Router's central position in traffic path allows adversary to sniff credentials, inject payloads, or perform ARP/DNS spoofing. Detectable via anomalous traffic patterns.
log_sources: ARP spoofing indicators from network monitoring
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline NetFlow patterns for router traffic forwarding (expected symmetry between ingress and egress traffic types). Alert on NetFlow records showing router IP as source/destination for client-to-server traffic flows. Monitor for DNS responses originating from router IP where router is not authoritative. Track client-side SSL/TLS certificate errors referencing router IP as certificate issuer.

suggestion.title: Detect Supply-Chain Compromise via Tenda Firmware Distribution Channels
suggestion.rationale: Article cites CERT/CC warning, suggesting official Tenda distribution may be compromised or specific firmware versions contain embedded backdoor. Detection should identify widespread deployment of affected versions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate all deployed Tenda router firmware versions across organization. Cross-reference against CERT/CC advisory for affected version ranges. Correlate firmware versions with deployment source (OEM, reseller, direct download). Alert on presence of firmware versions identified as containing backdoor. Flag any firmware update attempts that fail or are blocked, suggesting manual patching resistance.

suggestion.title: 9router exploitation: unauthenticated API access from unexpected source IPs
suggestion.rationale: Article states '/api/providers endpoints lack authentication entirely' and '/api/usage/stats' leaks full API keys. Pipeline missed direct exploitation detection. Should flag successful 200 responses to sensitive endpoints from IPs with no prior authentication context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: 9router exposes critical API endpoints without authentication. Detect successful (HTTP 200/201) POST/PUT/DELETE to /api/providers or GET to /api/usage/stats from source IPs that have never authenticated to the application. Baseline should exclude known internal/monitoring IPs.

suggestion.title: 9router credential exfiltration: API key patterns in HTTP response bodies
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Full API Key Leak via /api/usage/stats'. Pipeline extracted no IOCs for leaked keys. Should hunt response body content for API key patterns (base64, JWT-like, provider token formats).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: When /api/usage/stats or /api/providers return HTTP 200, inspect response bodies for credential patterns: 'api_key', 'apiKey', 'token', or base64-encoded strings matching known LLM provider token formats (OpenAI, Anthropic, etc.). Flag any response >1KB containing these patterns to unauthenticated requesters.

suggestion.title: 9router rogue provider persistence: config file writes post-provider-create
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions provider CRUD mutations; attacker likely creates rogue providers for persistence/redirection. Should detect file system changes to application config after unauthorized provider creation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate HTTP POST to /api/providers with HTTP 201 response, then hunt for filesystem writes to 9router config/database files within 5 minutes. Indicates persistence attempt via rogue provider injection.

suggestion.title: 9router provider manipulation: PUT requests modifying routing or API keys
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attacker can 'create, read, update, and delete provider connections'. UC_6_3 hunts mutations but doesn't distinguish malicious modifications (key swaps, endpoint rewriting) from legitimate updates. Should track request body delta.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: For PUT requests to /api/providers/*, capture and baseline request body fields (api_key, endpoint_url, enabled). Alert on changes to critical fields from anomalous IPs or outside change-control windows.

suggestion.title: 9router software/version inventory for vulnerability scoping
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 9router ≤0.4.41 as vulnerable. Pipeline extracted zero IOCs. Should generate inventory detection for vulnerability management: running processes, listening ports, HTTP banners revealing 9router version.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt HTTP GET /api/version or /version endpoints (common in Next.js apps); correlate responses matching '9router' pattern with version field. Parse HTTP Server header for 'Next.js' strings. Inventory results against CVE-2026-XXXX affected version list.

suggestion.title: Archive extraction modifying SSH authorized_keys without subsequent login
suggestion.rationale: Article states links/files can be created 'outside that directory'—SSH key injection is explicit attack surface. UC_8_2 requires cron/systemd execution, but article describes arbitrary file write capability. Missing: detection for SSH key injection alone as persistence without immediate command execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when Node.js archive extraction writes to .ssh/authorized_keys or modifies its permissions without corresponding SSH login attempts within 1 hour. This detects key injection for later use.

suggestion.title: LD_SO_PRELOAD hijack via archive path traversal
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions /etc/ld.so.preload as write target. Article phrase: 'A link (hardlink) or symlink entry is created without checking where its target points.' This is the core primitive for dynamic linker hijacking.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Node.js processes or archive-extraction utilities writing to /etc/ld.so.preload or creating symlinks that resolve to it. Correlate with subsequent process execution—all child processes will load the injected library.

suggestion.title: Sudoers directory modification via archive extraction
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions /etc/sudoers.d/* as target. Writing crafted rules to sudoers.d grants command execution without password. Article describes link/symlink bypass: attacker can point a symlink in the archive to /etc/sudoers.d/99-pwned.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Node.js or archive extraction creating files in /etc/sudoers.d/ (should be rare). Combine with sudo execution rule changes or new sudoers entries that appeared at extraction time.

suggestion.title: Archive extraction creating hardlink to existing privileged executable
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies: 'A link (hardlink)...is created without checking where its target points.' Attacker can hardlink a new path to /bin/sh or other privileged tool, potentially changing permissions or creating suid copies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Node/archive processes creating hardlinks or symlinks to executables in /bin, /usr/bin, /usr/local/bin, especially to suid binaries or shell interpreters.

suggestion.title: Reply-To Domain Pivot in Spoofed Email Headers
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly documents the technique: 'Reply-To quietly redirects replies to an unrelated domain — a classic reply-pivot that keeps any victim response away from the spoofed organization.' This is the attacker's mechanism to evade detection while maintaining the impersonation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on emails where the Reply-To domain differs from the From domain, and the From domain claims to belong to a trusted external organization. Cross-correlate the reply-to domain against phishing infrastructure and vendor-impersonation campaigns. This pivot is the signature of vendor-spoofing attacks designed to collect responses out-of-band from the impersonated organization.

suggestion.title: SharePoint Tenant Lookalike URL Detection (Display vs. Href Mismatch)
suggestion.rationale: Article describes exact attack: visible anchor text shows 'https://mononapfp.sharepoint.com' (legitimate vendor) but the actual href points to 'https://mononapfpcom.sharepoint.com' (attacker-controlled tenant). The .com domain label is concatenated into the subdomain to bypass regex and string matching.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Parse email anchor tags and flag when the display text and href differ, especially when display mimics a vendor's legitimate sharepoint.com URL but href targets a lookalike with domain-name folding (e.g., vendorcom.sharepoint.com instead of vendor.sharepoint.com). Correlate display domain against SharePoint tenant inventory to confirm the href is attacker-controlled.

suggestion.title: Device Code Phishing API Sequence (POST /device/start with Broker Mode)
suggestion.rationale: Article details the exact API contract: 'POST /api/device/start with a JSON body containing userId, clientMode: "broker", login_hint, and redirect_url. The C2 responds with device_code, user_code, verification_uri, and expires_in.' The clientMode parameter is non-standard and specific to this MFA-bypass platform.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP POST requests to attacker-controlled endpoints that return device_code and user_code in the response, especially when paired with clientMode: 'broker' and unusual verification_uri pointing to phishing infrastructure. Correlate with sign-in logs showing authentication from the same user shortly after device code issuance, or impossible-travel/anomalous geo.

suggestion.title: Primary Refresh Token (PRT) Lifecycle API Chain Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies persistence via the specific endpoint sequence: '/prt/setup, /prt/refresh, /prt/renew, /prt/reacquire, and /prt/cookie, the same Primary Refresh Token persistence chain Sekoia documented as EvilTokens' core differentiator.' These are explicit named endpoints for persistent token management.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for sequences of token refresh operations against a single account that deviate from normal OAuth patterns—specifically, rapid /prt/refresh or /prt/renew calls without corresponding user interaction. Correlate with device registration events, impossible-travel logins, or sign-ins from known phishing infrastructure. PRT acquisition followed by refresh-token reuse is a signature of post-compromise persistence.

suggestion.title: Seven-Layer Anti-Bot Behavioral Verification in Phishing Page
suggestion.rationale: Article describes the evasion stack: 'User-Agent regex… navigator.webdriver check… Browser feature fingerprinting… Window dimension analysis… Interaction telemetry [3+ mouse moves or 1+ touch events]… Timing gate [minimum 800ms]… Movement pattern analysis.' This is more sophisticated than prior EvilTokens server-side anti-bot mechanisms.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inspect phishing page payloads for client-side bot-detection logic that combines User-Agent inspection, navigator.webdriver checks, window dimension validation, and interaction telemetry gating. Detect delayed payload execution (800ms+ timing gates) or script logic that monitors mouse coordinates for organic (non-linear) movement. This indicates malware-grade evasion infrastructure designed to block automated analysis and SOC investigation.

suggestion.title: Cloudflare Workers Phishing Infrastructure (UUID-Prefixed Subdomains)
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attack infrastructure: 'ARToken uses {uuid}-docviewer.workers.dev, {uuid}-onedrive.workers.dev, and {uuid}-adobe2.workers.dev.' Both ARToken and EvilTokens deploy phishing lures to Cloudflare Workers with UUID-prefixed naming patterns to abuse the platform's high reputation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for clicks, HTTP requests, or DNS queries to subdomains matching the pattern {UUID}-{service}.workers.dev where service names include 'docviewer', 'onedrive', 'adobe2', or similar cloud service impersonations. Track Cloudflare Workers subdomains provisioned by newly registered threat actors. The UUID prefix + service mimicry is a strong signal of this specific phishing-as-a-service platform.

suggestion.title: SharePoint Server Public-Facing Asset Exposure Baseline
suggestion.rationale: Article references asset-exposure template hunting and implies public-facing application. Pipeline generated zero use cases despite CISA KEV status (active exploitation now occurring).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of internal IPs/FQDNs hosting Microsoft SharePoint Server. Monitor external-to-internal HTTP/HTTPS traffic for requests to /_layouts, /sites, /_api, /admin paths. Alert on external IP enumeration of SharePoint endpoints or repeated unauthenticated access attempts.

suggestion.title: Suspicious HTTP POST with Serialized .NET Payload to SharePoint Admin Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'deserialization of untrusted data' as the vulnerability mechanism—the attack vector is HTTP POST requests with malicious serialized objects. Pipeline omitted this exploitation signature entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP POST to SharePoint admin and API endpoints for serialized .NET object signatures (BinaryFormatter magic bytes, TypeFilterLevel markers, ObjectStateFormatter patterns in request body). Correlate with HTTP 500 errors or application exceptions. Flag unexpected source IPs or deviations from baseline user behavior.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Child Process Spawned from w3wp.exe SharePoint Application Pool
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'execute code over a network'; successful deserialization RCE spawns child processes. Pipeline failed to generate execution-phase detection despite explicit code-execution capability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on cmd.exe, powershell.exe, certutil.exe, csc.exe, or rundll32.exe spawned from w3wp.exe. Exclude known SharePoint background processes (search crawler). Correlate timing with suspicious HTTP POSTs and IIS 500 errors from step 2.

suggestion.title: Compromised SharePoint User Attempting Admin Privilege Escalation or Sensitive Function Access
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'authorized attacker'—explicitly establishes compromised-credential or insider-threat attack model. Pipeline missed T1078 (Valid Accounts) correlation despite this being core to the stated threat model.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: For users with baseline SharePoint read-only access, detect attempts to modify admin settings, add/remove site collection admins, or access data-enrichment endpoints. Alert on same user authenticating from new geography then immediately accessing SharePoint admin functions within 15 minutes.

suggestion.title: SharePoint Application Log Deserialization Exception Spike (Pre-Exploitation Signal)
suggestion.rationale: Deserialization attacks typically fail multiple times during exploitation attempts, generating diagnostic exceptions. Pipeline ignored log-based early-warning detection despite vulnerability class providing clear IOC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Windows Application event logs and SharePoint ULS logs for SerializationException, DeserializationException, or TypeInitializationException. Establish baseline exception rate per server. Alert if exception count exceeds baseline by >200% within 5-minute window or same exception class recurs from multiple HTTP requests in rapid succession.

suggestion.title: CISA KEV: SharePoint Server Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Anything in CISA KEV is *currently* being exploited' and 'Even if your scanners say not vulnerable...worth one quick check across your fleet' — requires immediate asset inventory and exposure visibility for SharePoint instances vulnerable to CVE-2026-45659.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inventory all SharePoint Server instances (TCP 80, 443, 15292) and cross-reference against unpatched hosts. Identify public-facing SharePoint via external network scanners or passive DNS. Correlate with patch-management systems to flag systems still running unsupported versions or missing KBs released before 2026-07-04 federal deadline.

suggestion.title: SharePoint RCE: Anomalous Code Execution from IIS App Pool
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'execute code over a network' as the vulnerability impact — post-exploitation detection must capture child processes spawned from w3wp.exe (SharePoint application pool), which would indicate successful exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on w3wp.exe spawning cmd.exe, powershell.exe, cscript.exe, or regsvcs.exe. Establish baseline of legitimate SharePoint administrative activity; flag first-time spawns or execution chains leading to external command-and-control. Cross-correlate with network egress to identify exfiltration patterns.

suggestion.title: Deserialization Attack: Malicious Serialized Payload Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'deserialization of untrusted data vulnerability' as the attack vector — detection must capture serialized .NET objects with suspicious signatures before they reach vulnerable deserialization code paths.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor POST/PUT requests to SharePoint endpoints for serialized .NET object signatures: BinaryFormatter magic bytes (0xFB, 0xFE), TypedArray headers, or base64-encoded serialized data in request bodies. Alert on requests to known vulnerable SharePoint endpoints (e.g., /_api/, /sites/) containing binary payloads or object gadgets.

suggestion.title: SharePoint Authentication Bypass → Code Execution Chain
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'authorized attacker' but also 'actively exploited in the wild' — suggests attackers may bypass authorization or abuse valid credentials. Detection must capture the credential→execution correlation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate failed SharePoint authentication (401/403 responses to /_api/ or /_vti_bin endpoints) within 5 minutes of successful code execution (w3wp child processes, service account elevation, file writes to %WINDIR%). Flag patterns indicating credential stuffing followed by exploitation.

suggestion.title: CISA KEV Remediation Deadline Verification (Federal Compliance)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Federal patch due: 2026-07-04' and 'Federal civilian agencies are required to remediate by the published due date' — this CVE requires compliance tracking tied to a hard regulatory deadline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Automated daily query: For all Microsoft SharePoint Server systems in federal civilian agency scope, verify patches released 2026-06-11 or later (assumed patch Tuesday) are deployed. Flag any system still vulnerable on 2026-07-05; escalate unpatched federal assets as compliance violations.

suggestion.title: SharePoint Deserialization Exception Spike + Denial of Service
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation attempts may trigger deserialization exceptions in ULS logs before successful code execution. Spikes in format errors or ObjectDataFormat exceptions indicate attacker activity probing the vulnerability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor SharePoint ULS logs for spikes in BinaryFormatter exceptions, deserialization errors, or TypedArray parsing failures. Correlate with IIS W3WP worker process restarts, 503 errors, or unexpected W3WP memory growth — patterns consistent with malicious serialized-object delivery or fuzzing attempts.

suggestion.title: SharePoint Server Exposure & CVE-2026-45659 Asset Scan
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly directs 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' and provides template reference for Splunk SPL and Defender KQL. This is the primary detection need for a CISA KEV entry with active exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for exposed SharePoint Server instances listening on HTTP/HTTPS (ports 80, 443, 8080) and map against known-vulnerable versions. Cross-reference patch compliance data to identify unpatched assets. Monitor for deserialization-related exceptions or gadget-chain activity (ObjectInputStream, BinaryFormatter) in SharePoint process logs.

suggestion.title: SharePoint Deserialization Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability allows 'code execution over a network' via deserialization — this is the exploitation vector. No detection for the attack itself was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for SharePoint application pool processes (w3wp.exe) spawning child processes, loading suspicious assemblies, or writing to unexpected file paths. Watch for CLR/.NET deserialization failures in Application event log (EventID 1000) or suspicious ObjectInputStream usage patterns.

suggestion.title: Authorized User Exploitation of SharePoint (Lateral Escalation)
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'authorized attacker' — indicating the threat model includes legitimate credentials being used post-breach. No use case for post-auth exploitation detection was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate successful SharePoint authentication (EventID 4624, 4625) with subsequent RCE indicators (Process creation, file writes outside normal paths). Look for non-standard service accounts initiating SharePoint application pool restarts or accessing sensitive libraries.

suggestion.title: Exposed SharePoint Server Inventory — CVE-2026-45659
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability allows 'authorized attacker to execute code over a network,' implying SharePoint must be accessible. Template mandates asset-exposure hunt; pipeline generated none. Detect unpatched or exposed SharePoint Server instances before federal due date 2026-07-04.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset management and vulnerability scanners for SharePoint Server installations. Flag instances with missing patch for CVE-2026-45659. Cross-reference network exposure (port 80, 443, 15292 reachable from untrusted segments). Prioritize instances with admin/service account activity post-discovery.

suggestion.title: Deserialization Payload Detection — SharePoint RCE
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability explicitly identified as 'deserialization of untrusted data.' Article does not name specific payloads, but this is the attack vector. Detect serialized .NET objects or binary data in SharePoint requests.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP POST/PUT to SharePoint /_api/ and /Lists/ endpoints for Base64-encoded or binary serialized payloads (ObjectStateFormatter, BinaryFormatter patterns). Alert on abnormally large request bodies or ViewState manipulation in requests from non-authenticated or low-privilege sessions.

suggestion.title: RCE Child Process Spawning from w3wp.exe
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker can 'execute code over a network' post-exploitation. Successful deserialization leads to process execution. Detect unusual child processes from SharePoint application pool worker.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on child processes spawned by w3wp.exe (SharePoint service) running cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or encoded scripts. High-risk signals: w3wp.exe → powershell with -NoProfile or -EncodedCommand; w3wp.exe → csc.exe (C# compilation). Baseline normal SharePoint operations to reduce false positives on legitimate SharePoint extensions.

suggestion.title: Patch Compliance Verification — CVE-2026-45659 Deadline
