suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Ingest vulnerability scanner outputs and flag all systems running Microsoft SharePoint Server with CVE-2026-45659 unpatched. Cross-reference against network perimeter/exposure data to identify internet-facing instances. Track remediation lag to trigger incident investigations.

suggestion.title: Deserialization Payload Detection in SharePoint Requests
suggestion.rationale: Article describes vulnerability as 'deserialization of untrusted data vulnerability which allows an authorized attacker to execute code'. No detection for the attack delivery mechanism (malicious serialized object in HTTP request) was suggested.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor SharePoint Server HTTP logs and WAF telemetry for requests containing base64-encoded or binary serialized .NET objects (BinaryFormatter signatures). Alert on requests to known vulnerable endpoints paired with unusual content-encoding headers or oversized payloads.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Code Execution from SharePoint Process Context
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker can 'execute code over a network' but no detection use case covers process execution spawned post-deserialization. This is the exploitation outcome that needs monitoring.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on child processes spawned by w3wp.exe (SharePoint IIS worker) with high-confidence exploitation indicators: PowerShell with -noprofile/-enc flags, cmd.exe execution from temp directories, or net.exe/whoami.exe issued within 5 seconds of suspicious HTTP traffic. Establish baseline of legitimate SharePoint child processes first.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized SharePoint Server Network Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions federal agencies required to remediate and stresses externally exposed assets are at risk ('exploitation against exposed assets'). No network-layer detection for unexpected external access to SharePoint was suggested.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of expected inbound sources to SharePoint servers (internal networks, known VPNs). Alert on first-seen external IP addresses connecting to SharePoint ports (443, 80, 32771-32815 for admin). Flag spikes in connection attempts or HTTP 500/502 errors within exploitation time windows.

suggestion.title: SharePoint Server Unpatched Asset Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article targets exploitation of exposed SharePoint Server by 'authorized attacker'; asset discovery precedes exploitation. Explicit federal patch due-date (2026-07-04) supports timeline-driven inventory hunt. Template reference ('[`../_TEMPLATES.md#asset-exposure`]') directly prescribes this UC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference vulnerability scan results against asset inventory to identify SharePoint Server versions matching CVE-2026-45659 scope. Prioritize systems with patch dates older than 2026-07-04. Correlate with network exposure indicators (open ports 443, 80, or RPC).

suggestion.title: Suspicious Deserialization Payloads to SharePoint
suggestion.rationale: Article root cause is 'deserialization of untrusted data'; exploitation succeeds by sending malformed serialized objects. Detection should target unusual ObjectStateFormatter patterns, Base64 blobs in POST bodies, or deserialization exceptions in SharePoint/IIS logs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor inbound HTTP POST/GET to SharePoint paths for suspicious deserialization markers (e.g., ViewState parameters with unusual length, binary content, or unrecognized formats). Alert on IIS HTTP 500 errors containing ParseError or ObjectStateFormatter exceptions within seconds of suspicious requests.

suggestion.title: Process Execution from SharePoint Service Accounts
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'allows code execution over a network.' Post-exploitation, W3WP.exe (IIS Application Pool for SharePoint) should not spawn cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or other interpreters outside normal operations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on W3WP.exe or SPUCWorkerProcess.exe (SharePoint service processes) spawning cmd.exe, powershell.exe, rundll32.exe, net.exe, or wmic.exe. Baseline normal child processes and flag unexpected additions. Include parent-child execution chains to establish exploitation context.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement from Compromised SharePoint Host
suggestion.rationale: Once code-execution is achieved in SharePoint context, attacker uses it as a pivot. Monitor for outbound network connections and credential-access attempts initiated from SharePoint service accounts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag outbound network connections from W3WP.exe or SharePoint service accounts to non-whitelisted internal or external IPs, especially on unusual ports. Correlate with process-execution logs to identify post-exploitation reconnaissance (net group, nltest, BloodHound).

suggestion.title: Vulnerable SharePoint Server Asset Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'CVE-2026-45659 — match against your vulnerability scanner' and references standard asset-exposure hunt template. Pipeline should detect unpatched Microsoft SharePoint Server instances across the fleet.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Microsoft SharePoint Server instances (IIS w3wp.exe running SharePoint) that lack security patches for CVE-2026-45659. Cross-reference build numbers and cumulative updates against Microsoft bulletins. Federal due date was 2026-07-04; flag any unpatched instances after that date.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Code Execution on SharePoint Worker Process
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'authorized attacker to execute code over a network' via deserialization. Pipeline should detect unexpected process spawning from SharePoint application pools (w3wp.exe context).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for processes spawned by w3wp.exe (SharePoint worker process) with unusual command lines, especially PowerShell, cmd.exe, or encoded arguments. Deserialization exploits typically execute via runtime invocation without user-visible logon.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Deserialization Activity in SharePoint
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability is 'deserialization of untrusted data'; pipeline should detect indicators of exploitation during the deserialization phase itself.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: SharePoint ULS logs and IIS logs may show exceptions during object deserialization, unusual DLL loading by SharePoint processes, or module load events from non-standard locations. Look for TypeConfusionExceptions or SerializationException errors correlated with HTTP POST requests to SharePoint services.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement from Compromised SharePoint Server
suggestion.rationale: Once attacker executes code on SharePoint (network-facing service), subsequent reconnaissance and lateral movement is expected. Article implies active exploitation scenario requiring detection of post-compromise activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After successful code execution on SharePoint, detect secondary lateral-movement patterns: enumeration of network shares (T1135), credential dumping (T1110), or lateral RDP/SMB connections originating from the compromised SharePoint server.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-45659 Patch Compliance Check
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies federal patch due date of 2026-07-04. Pipeline should flag non-compliance as compliance violation for high-risk vulnerability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Audit all SharePoint Server instances for KB patches released in June 2026 addressing CVE-2026-45659. Flag any system past the federal deadline (2026-07-04) without documented patching or exception approval.

suggestion.title: Anomalous SharePoint Service Account Activity
suggestion.rationale: Deserialization exploits often execute in the context of the service account running SharePoint (e.g., SP_Admin pool identity). Unexpected actions by this account post-exploitation warrant detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual activity by SharePoint service accounts: lateral SMB connections, file shares accessed that are not part of farm topology, privilege escalation attempts, or interactive logons from the application server.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-45659 Vulnerability Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly recommends 'match against your vulnerability scanner' and substituting CVE-2026-45659 into asset-exposure templates. Pipeline generated zero use cases despite this direct detection call-out.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor vulnerability scanners and Defender for Vulnerability Management for detections of CVE-2026-45659 on Microsoft SharePoint Server instances. Flag any hit as confirmed active exploitation per CISA KEV catalog status.

suggestion.title: SharePoint Server Unauthorized Code Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'allows an authorized attacker to execute code over a network.' Pipeline missed behavioral detection of the execution phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious process execution, .NET assembly loading, or PowerShell invocations on SharePoint Server instances correlating with inbound network traffic. Key indicator: post-auth code execution from unexpected source IPs.

suggestion.title: Federal Patch Compliance for CVE-2026-45659
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies federal remediation deadline of 2026-07-04. Pipeline should generate patch-compliance hunts tied to regulatory deadlines for prioritization.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query patch management and endpoint inventory for all SharePoint Server instances missing patches for CVE-2026-45659 as of federal deadline. Cross-reference with external attack-surface discovery to flag internet-facing unpatched assets as critical.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure Detection for SharePoint Server
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly references 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' template and recommends Splunk and KQL baselines, yet pipeline returned empty use-case array.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify all internet-facing SharePoint Server instances via port 80/443 scanning, HTTPS certificate enumeration, and banner matching. Correlate with patch status and CISA KEV entry to surface confirmed exploitation risk.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-45659 Vulnerability Scan Match — Asset Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'CVE-2026-45659 — match against your vulnerability scanner.' CISA KEV designation means active exploitation; asset inventory scan is the canonical first hunt to identify exposed SharePoint instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability management systems for CVE-2026-45659 detection against Microsoft SharePoint Server assets. Alert on all matches; CISA KEV implies active bypass. Prioritize internet-facing or DMZ-exposed SharePoint servers and correlate with network exposure data.

suggestion.title: Suspicious .NET Deserialization Payload to SharePoint Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'deserialization of untrusted data vulnerability which allows...code execution over a network.' Target the exploit payload delivery mechanism — serialized .NET gadget chain in HTTP bodies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect POST requests to SharePoint web service endpoints containing Base64-encoded or binary-serialized .NET payloads. Look for ObjectDataProvider, DataSet, WindowsIdentity, or custom gadget patterns in request bodies. Correlate with IIS deserialization errors or w3wp.exe exceptions.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Child Process Spawning from SharePoint Worker (w3wp.exe)
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability permits 'code execution over a network.' Post-exploitation, expect cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or other tools spawned from w3wp.exe, the IIS worker process hosting SharePoint.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline legitimate child processes from SharePoint's w3wp.exe (typically limited to internal diagnostics). Alert on cmd.exe, powershell.exe, certutil.exe, net.exe, or system utilities spawned from w3wp.exe. Cross-check user context, time-of-day, and parent window title for anomalies.

suggestion.title: Authorized User Lateral Movement or Privilege Escalation via SharePoint Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'authorized attacker' — implies credential compromise or insider abuse precedes exploitation. Hunt for authenticated sessions pivoting to unexpected resources or executing administrative actions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate SharePoint successful authentication with subsequent anomalous activity: access to admin site collections, XML injection in lists, or deployment of custom solutions. Alert if auth originates from external IP or deviates from baseline (e.g., service account authenticating interactively, off-hours access).

suggestion.title: BeyondTrust Remote Support - Successful Access Without Prior Authentication
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'auth bypass flaws in Remote Support.' Core detection: access granted without valid credential submission. Citation: 'Critical Auth Bypass Flaws in Remote Support.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on sessions to BeyondTrust Remote Support endpoints that lack corresponding authentication events in the primary auth system, or that bypass MFA/OTP validation. Correlate successful connections with failed login attempts in the preceding 60 seconds.

suggestion.title: BeyondTrust PRA - Privilege Escalation via Authentication Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Privilege Remote Access (PRA) auth bypass grants direct privileged access without credential validation. Citation: 'Critical Auth Bypass Flaws in...PRA.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PRA sessions where the authenticated user identity does not match the system identity performing privileged operations. Alert on privilege escalation chains that occur without corresponding elevation consent or approval workflows in PRA logs.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Compromised BeyondTrust Remote Support Session
suggestion.rationale: Once auth bypass is exploited, attacker gains stable remote session into internal network. Remote support tools are canonical lateral movement pivots. Citation: 'Remote Support' as attack surface for critical bypass.
log_sources: Host-based endpoint logs on supported endpoints
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor BeyondTrust Remote Support sessions for command execution, file transfer, or process spawning activity. Alert on sessions originating from unexpected geographies, IP ranges, or outside business hours. Baseline normal supported-endpoint interaction patterns and flag anomalies.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Admin Account Creation on Tenda Devices
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'hidden admin backdoor'—detectable via admin user creation events outside maintenance windows. Phrase: 'Hidden Admin Backdoor' implies account manipulation as persistence vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on new admin-level user accounts created on Tenda devices without scheduled change requests. Correlate with firmware modification timestamps. Flag non-standard account naming patterns and accounts created via SSH/Telnet outside normal provisioning.

suggestion.title: Tenda Firmware Integrity Modification Detection
suggestion.rationale: Backdoor embedded 'in firmware' per title—implies firmware tampering or preinstallation. Monitor checksum failures and unexpected firmware version rollbacks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag firmware version mismatches between device declaration and official Tenda release manifests, failed firmware validation on boot, or unexpected version downgrades. Compare installed firmware hashes against known-good CVE-patched builds.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Tenda Management Interface Authentication
suggestion.rationale: Backdoor enables remote privileged access—detect via authentication to Tenda device management (HTTP/S 80/443, SSH 22, Telnet 23) from unexpected geographies, off-hours, or credential patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline Tenda admin login sources, times, and patterns. Alert on first-time logins from non-standard ASNs, administrative access during non-business hours, or rapid authentication attempts from rotating source IPs.

suggestion.title: Tenda Backdoor Command Execution via Management Port
suggestion.rationale: Hidden backdoor execution implies command channel—look for suspicious command sequences sent to device management interfaces or unexpected shell metacharacters in HTTP GET/POST payloads to router admin panels.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP POST bodies and GET query strings to Tenda device management URLs for command injection patterns (semicolons, pipes, backticks). Flag payloads containing shell commands or CGI parameter manipulation targeting common Tenda admin paths (/admin/, /cgi-bin/admin).

suggestion.title: Tenda Device Unexpected Outbound Command-and-Control
suggestion.rationale: Compromised firmware enables C2 callbacks—detect by establishing baseline of expected Tenda outbound destinations (firmware mirrors, NTP, DHCP) and alerting on new external connections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Whitelist known-legitimate Tenda firmware update and NTP sources. Alert on Tenda device initiating outbound TCP/UDP to new IPs outside these ranges, especially to high-numbered ports or non-RFC1918 private ranges that suggest external infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Orchard Action proof submission anomalies on nodes with vulnerable halo2_gadgets
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'Missing copy constraint...allows under-constrained base point...let a malicious prover produce a valid proof for an Orchard Action with an *under-constrained* base point.' Exploitation would manifest as high-frequency invalid Orchard proofs or transaction rejects from consensus nodes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect nodes with vulnerable zebrad/halo2_gadgets versions experiencing elevated Orchard proof validation failures, transaction rejections with zk-proof errors, or sudden spikes in proof submission attempts from anomalous sources. Correlate with network exfiltration or consensus rule violations.

suggestion.title: halo2_gadgets source repository anomalies (commit/release metadata)
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'Supply Chain Compromise: Compromise Software Dependencies'—if halo2_gadgets repository itself was compromised, detect unauthorized commits, unexpected release builds, or version bumps with malicious payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor halo2_gadgets GitHub repository for commits outside normal developer patterns, releases without corresponding signed tags, or version uploads to crates.io with unexpected hash mismatches. Alert on commits touching proof-validation logic from new or dormant accounts.

suggestion.title: Dependency pin audit: Projects embedding vulnerable halo2_gadgets versions
suggestion.rationale: Orchard and Zcash depend on halo2_gadgets; any project pinning a vulnerable version in Cargo.toml inherits the soundness flaw. Hunt for downstream consumers still locked to vulnerable releases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan accessible Cargo.lock files, package manifests, and container image layers for halo2_gadgets versions < patched release. Prioritize public/production deployments and cryptographic infrastructure projects.

suggestion.title: Consensus-layer rule violation: Orchard transactions passing invalid proofs
suggestion.rationale: The vulnerability breaks soundness of the proof itself. A successful exploit would submit Orchard Actions that the flawed gadget accepts but a correct verifier would reject. Monitor for transactions that achieve consensus finality despite failing external proof validation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-correlate Orchard transaction finalization with zero-knowledge proof validation results. Alert on finalized transactions with cryptographic proof validation failures or base-point integrity check failures from external verifiers.

suggestion.title: Prompt injection payloads in Neo4j query parameters
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'attacker who can influence the prompt' — prompts are influenceable by 'direct user input' and 'indirect content the agent reads back via RAG.' Pipeline missed detection of injection markers (Cypher keywords, APOC function names, escaped quotes) in user-controlled input logged before Neo4j execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for escaped Cypher keywords (MATCH, CALL, LOAD, DETACH, DELETE, DROP) appearing in user input or RAG-retrieved content that is then passed to Neo4jChatAgent. Detect injection marker sequences like `\'` + `MATCH` or `CALL dbms.` in unvalidated input fields. Correlate with subsequent Neo4j query logs to confirm execution.

suggestion.title: RAG-mediated Cypher injection — malicious strings in indexed documents
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'indirect content the agent reads back via RAG' as attack vector. An attacker can plant Cypher injection payloads in documents that Langroid's RAG retriever indexes (e.g., corpus files, uploaded PDFs, wiki content). When agent processes query, it retrieves poisoned content and feeds it to LLM, which generates malicious Cypher. Pipeline missed this reconnaissance + setup phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect when documents added to RAG corpus contain Cypher injection patterns (MATCH, CALL db., apoc.*, DETACH DELETE). Flag documents with suspicious frequency of DB control keywords. Correlate RAG retrieval of flagged documents with subsequent Neo4j query execution containing injected strings.

suggestion.title: Langroid Neo4jChatAgent LLM-to-Neo4j request pattern anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Article describes Cypher generation without validation — need to detect when LLM output is forwarded to Neo4j driver with unexpected complexity or dangerous functions. Behavioral detection: unusual Cypher structure, unexpected APOC calls, or parameter binding bypassed. Pipeline did not suggest hunting LLM-to-driver API call patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Cypher queries generated by Neo4jChatAgent that contain: (1) nested CALL statements, (2) apoc.* functions, (3) dbms.* calls, (4) LOAD CSV, (5) multiple MATCH clauses unusual for single-record lookups. Correlate request source IP/user with query complexity baseline—detect deviation indicating compromised/manipulated prompt.

suggestion.title: Langroid configuration files enabling unsafe Cypher execution
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'config-conditional RCE' — suggests configuration option that enables unvalidated Cypher. Pipeline should hunt for config files containing settings that disable validation or allowlist restrictions. No config-based detection suggested.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for Langroid config files (langroid.yaml, .env, config.json) being modified to set flags like `validate_cypher=false`, `allowlist_disabled=true`, or `unsafe_mode=true`. Detect config-reload triggers after suspicious modification. Correlate config changes with subsequent Cypher execution containing dangerous functions.

suggestion.title: Data exfiltration via Neo4j LOAD CSV to attacker-controlled host
suggestion.rationale: Article describes SSRF exfil via LOAD CSV — but UC_9_2 only hunts egress, not the SPECIFIC pattern of LOAD CSV pointing to external host. Need to detect Cypher containing LOAD CSV with attacker-controlled URL to send query results externally.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: In Neo4j query logs, detect LOAD CSV statements with external URLs (non-internal IPs, public hostnames). Cross-reference LOAD CSV target domain against known good data source allowlist. Detect novel external hosts in LOAD CSV clauses. Correlate with previous MATCH statements that select sensitive data (passwords, tokens, PII) to confirm exfil intent.

suggestion.title: LLM system prompt manipulation indicators in Langroid logs
suggestion.rationale: Pre-attack reconnaissance: attacker may test Langroid's prompt handling by submitting strings designed to escape LLM instructions and inject raw commands. Article doesn't mention this directly but it's the setup phase for prompt injection. Pipeline should hunt for unusual prompt/instruction sequences in agent logs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor LLM prompts for signs of jailbreak/escape attempts: phrases like 'ignore instructions', 'forget the context', 'execute this instead', raw Cypher commands in user input, escaped quotes, or repeated variations of similar payloads (fuzzing). Detect when same user submits multiple prompt variations in short timeframe (indication of testing/probing).

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated API requests to 9router (missing Authorization headers)
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'endpoints lack authentication entirely'—need explicit detection for requests missing Authorization headers or API tokens to /api/providers, /api/usage/stats. Current UCs assume successful exploitation; should also hunt the auth-bypass pattern itself.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP requests to 9router API endpoints (/api/providers*, /api/usage/stats, /api/v1/*) from non-localhost that lack Authorization, X-API-Key, or Bearer token headers. Baseline expected auth patterns and alert on deviation; early indicator of exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: Provider configuration persistence via /api/providers CRUD
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'create, read, update, and delete provider connections' via unauthenticated endpoint. Need to track *what* provider configs are being modified (e.g., API keys, model endpoints, credentials injected into provider records).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor response payloads or application logs for /api/providers POST/PUT operations. Look for creation of new provider entries with suspicious credentials (hardcoded API keys, external model endpoints, C2 server addresses). Correlate with credential access to identify harvested keys being re-injected.

suggestion.title: API authentication middleware bypass or disablement
suggestion.rationale: The vulnerability exists because auth middleware is absent or disabled on /api/providers and /api/usage/stats. Should hunt for code changes that comment-out, remove, or bypass auth guards in the routing logic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on commits, PRs, or file edits to Next.js middleware, route handlers, or API guards that remove/comment-out authentication checks, add public-facing skip-auth logic, or change middleware chain order. High-fidelity signal if auth removal coincides with provider CRUD abuse in logs.

suggestion.title: Sequential unauthenticated API enumeration and exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes both reconnaissance (UC_10_2 endpoint enum) followed by exploitation (provider CRUD, API key leak). A hunt correlating recon + exploitation from same source in short timeframe would catch chained attacks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate UC_10_2 (4+ distinct endpoint paths scanned) with UC_10_3 or UC_10_4 (successful POST/PUT/DELETE or GET returning data) from the same source IP within 5–60 minutes. Indicates recon-to-exploit progression.

suggestion.title: Internet-Facing SharePoint Server Inventory (CVE-2026-45659)
suggestion.rationale: Article describes exploitation of 'public-facing application' and CISA KEV implies active wild attacks. Must identify exposed SharePoint Server instances before compromise. Federal agencies required to remediate by 2026-07-04.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query for SharePoint Server (ports 80, 443, 15292, 8443) with internet-routable IP exposure. Cross-reference with CVE-2026-45659 patched version inventory. Flag any unpatched instances as critical.

suggestion.title: SharePoint Deserialization Exploit Pattern Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'deserialization of untrusted data vulnerability'; attackers send malformed serialized objects to trigger code execution. Requires detection of abnormal .NET deserialization gadget chains or exception floods.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for POST requests to SharePoint web service endpoints (_layouts, webservices, asmx) containing binary serialized payloads or .NET exception events (ObjectDisposedException, TargetInvocationException) in SharePoint diagnostic logs.

suggestion.title: Code Execution from SharePoint Service Identity
suggestion.rationale: Article states authorized attacker 'execute code over a network'—post-exploitation behavior indicator. Detect ProcessCreate events (PowerShell, cmd.exe, WMI) spawned from W3WP.exe or OWSTIMER.EXE (SharePoint service accounts).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on child processes (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, cscript.exe, wmic.exe, certutil.exe) with parent W3WP.exe, OWSTIMER.EXE, or SPUCWorkerProcess.exe. Baseline expected processes; flag anomalies.

suggestion.title: Suspicious File Write to SharePoint Binary / Layout Directories
suggestion.rationale: Successful exploitation followed by webshell or assembly deployment in _vti_bin, bin, or _layouts directories. Persistence indicator post-code-execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FileCreateTime events targeting SharePoint bin directories, _vti_bin, and _layouts paths for .aspx, .ashx, .asmx, .dll files—especially if correlates with suspicious process creation or deserialization log errors.

suggestion.title: Anomalous HTTP POST to SharePoint Web Service Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Deserialization attacks typically deliver payloads via POST to SharePoint ASMX web services. Article implies network-accessible attack surface; detect suspicious request patterns (high volume, unusual headers, binary payloads).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for POST requests to /_layouts/, /webservices/, /sharepoint/ endpoints with Content-Length > threshold or binary Content-Type from external/unexpected source IPs. Correlate with deserialization exceptions.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-45659 Patch Compliance Status Check
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entries carry Federal due-date remediation mandates (2026-07-04 stated in article). Critical to verify patch deployment and identify patch lag across enterprise SharePoint estate.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner and WSUS/SCCM data for SharePoint Server instances missing security updates tagged to CVE-2026-45659. Correlate missing patches with internet-facing status. Flag compliance violations relative to Federal due date.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure: Internet-Facing SharePoint Servers (CVE-2026-45659)
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'CISA KEV' + 'deserialization of untrusted data vulnerability...allows...execute code over a network.' Mandatory first hunt for any public-facing critical RCE.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate SharePoint servers (HTTPS/HTTP ports, SPAdministration ports 17012-17014, SOAP ports 32843-32846) reachable from external networks via netflow or firewall logs. Cross-reference with vulnerability scanner confirming CVE-2026-45659 exposure. Prioritize hosts with no patch confirmation before federal due date 2026-07-04.

suggestion.title: Exploitation Attempt: Abnormal Process Spawning from SharePoint IIS Worker
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'allows...execute code over a network.' Deserialization RCE typically manifests as w3wp.exe or OWSTimer.exe spawning cmd.exe, PowerShell, or network-outbound processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on w3wp.exe (SharePoint Application Pool), OWSTimer.exe, or associated child processes creating cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or spawning network connections following inbound HTTP POST to known-vulnerable SharePoint endpoints (.asmx, application paths). High fidelity if preceded by 4688 / ProcessCreate with parent=WWW Publishing Service.

suggestion.title: Deserialization Payload Detection: .NET Gadget Chain Markers in HTTP Traffic
suggestion.rationale: Article vulnerability vector: 'deserialization of untrusted data.' Exploit payloads contain base64 or hex-encoded .NET serialization markers (BinaryFormatter, ObjectStateFormatter, TypedReference streams).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect base64-encoded .NET serialization prefix (AAEAAAD==, AQAAA, or TypedReference magic bytes) in HTTP POST bodies targeting SharePoint application endpoints. Flag requests with encoded ObjectInputStream or serialized Exception/Type objects. Correlate with HTTP 500 errors or abnormal response times indicating gadget chain evaluation.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-45659 Patch Compliance Scan
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Federal patch due: 2026-07-04' and 'patch lag is the silent killer.' Required tracking against CISA deadline for compliance reporting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Compare vulnerability scanner results against Microsoft Security Update Guide for CVE-2026-45659; identify SharePoint Server versions pre-dating vendor patch. Cross-reference WSUS or patch-management logs for remediation confirmation. Alert on unpatched systems still bound to external-facing networks or WAF rules.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Persistence: SharePoint Timer Jobs / Scheduled Tasks
suggestion.rationale: Arbitrary code execution via deserialization enables persistence; attacker typically creates recurring timer jobs (SPTimer.exe) or Windows scheduled tasks for callback/data exfil.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor 4688/ProcessCreate for OWSTimer.exe or schtasks.exe execution with suspicious arguments following exploitation indicators (HTTP spike + process anomalies). Alert on timer job creation via SharePoint Central Admin or PowerShell cmdlets (Add-SPJobDefinition). Baseline and alert on deviations in timer job registration.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation: Token Impersonation / Kerberos Delegation Abuse Post-RCE
suggestion.rationale: SharePoint Application Pool identity often has delegation rights (SpnSetIdentity, constrained delegation). RCE → privilege escalation via S4U2Self/S4U2Proxy or token impersonation is standard attack chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect 4688 token impersonation (ImpersonationLevel > Delegation) by w3wp.exe child processes. Monitor for Kerberos events 4768/4769 (TGT/TGS requests) using S4U2Self (T2SVC) or S4U2Proxy flags with ServiceName=application service account post-exploitation window. Flag LSASS.exe memory access by non-system processes spawned from SharePoint.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure: Internet-Facing SharePoint Server Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' and requires vulnerability scan matching for CVE-2026-45659 against fleet; 'patch lag is the silent killer' establishes that even patched systems may show scanner lag.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify SharePoint Server instances with public IP exposure or DMZ placement. Cross-reference vulnerability scanner results for CVE-2026-45659 presence; prioritize systems reporting 'not vulnerable' due to lag between patch release (2026-07-01) and effective deployment.

suggestion.title: Patch Compliance: CVE-2026-45659 Remediation Tracking
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'Federal patch due: 2026-07-04' and establishes that 'Federal civilian agencies are required to remediate by the published due date'—compliance-driven detection for patch lag.

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor SharePoint Server logs for malformed or suspicious serialized payloads in request bodies. Alert on .NET deserialization exceptions followed by child process spawning or unusual code execution from w3wp.exe (SharePoint worker process).

suggestion.title: SharePoint Deserialization Exception Detection

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor SharePoint ULS logs and application event logs for deserialization exceptions, ObjectInputStream errors, and unexpected type-loading on externally-facing endpoints. Flag spikes in serialization-related warnings or errors from w3wp.exe.

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process creation from SharePoint w3wp.exe or application pool identities spawning cmd.exe, powershell.exe, cscript.exe, or other execution utilities. Also alert on unexpected .NET reflection, assembly loading, or remote code compilation in SharePoint processes.

suggestion.title: SharePoint Server Asset Exposure — Network Inventory

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-45659 Scanner Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'match against your vulnerability scanner' and includes federal patch due-date 2026-07-04. This is the foundational detection for this KEV entry.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any vulnerability scanner hit for CVE-2026-45659 against Microsoft SharePoint Server instances. Cross-reference patch status; flag unpatched systems for immediate remediation.

suggestion.title: SharePoint Instance Exposure (Internet-Facing)
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV indicates active exploitation 'in the wild' against public-facing applications. Attacker must reach SharePoint over network; exposure detection is prerequisite.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify SharePoint Server instances (port 443, 32843, custom ports) reachable from internet via shodan, certificate transparency logs, or cloud asset scanning. Flag all public-facing instances for immediate patching.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Deserialization Payload in SharePoint Requests
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability is 'deserialization of untrusted data.' Malicious payloads exploit this via crafted HTTP requests to SharePoint endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor POST/PUT requests to /_api/, /_vti_bin/, /sites endpoints containing binary serialized data, known gadget chains (ObjectDataProvider, WindowsIdentity), or abnormally large payloads.

suggestion.title: Code Execution via SharePoint Process
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability allows attacker to 'execute code over a network.' Detection of child processes spawned by w3wp.exe (SharePoint worker process) indicates post-exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag suspicious child processes from w3wp.exe (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, stsadm.exe with unusual args). Alert on network connections from SharePoint processes to external IPs.

suggestion.title: Authorized But Anomalous SharePoint Admin Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'authorized attacker'—once compromised, admin credentials may be abused. Post-exploitation activity differs from baseline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal SharePoint admin activity (hours, frequency, operations). Flag deviations: mass file downloads, unusual search queries, admin account usage outside business hours, credential dumps via _api/site/users.

suggestion.title: SharePoint RCE via Deserialization Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'authorized attacker to execute code over a network'—a direct exploitation path. Pipeline generated zero use cases for this execution phase despite it being the primary attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor SharePoint servers for abnormal .NET deserialization operations, sudden process spawning from W3WP.exe worker processes, or unexpected outbound connections from application pools. Correlate with scanner findings for unpatched CVE-2026-45659.

suggestion.title: Unpatched SharePoint Server Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'patch lag is the silent killer' and specifies federal due-date 2026-07-04. Pipeline missed inventory-based detection despite article explicitly recommending asset-exposure hunt template.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner for systems with CVE-2026-45659 still present post-deadline. Cross-reference network discovery logs to identify exposed SharePoint instances. Alert on systems vulnerable 7+ days after federal due-date to catch patch lag.

suggestion.title: SharePoint Web Log Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies exploitation occurs 'over a network' against public-facing application. Pipeline missed web-based exploitation detection despite this being the primary access vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor SharePoint web logs for POST requests with unusual serialized object patterns, oversized payloads to application endpoints, or external source IPs. Flag succeeded requests followed by unexpected child process creation or outbound network activity.

suggestion.title: SharePoint Server Asset Discovery and Patch Status
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly requires 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' and warns 'patch lag is the silent killer.' CISA KEV definition means actively exploited; without inventory, exposure remains unmeasurable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate all Microsoft SharePoint Server instances, query version numbers, and cross-reference against CVE-2026-45659 patch status. Prioritize instances accessible from internet-facing networks or with patch deployment lag >7 days past 2026-07-04 federal deadline.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-45659 Deserialization Payload Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'deserialization of untrusted data' as the exploit mechanism. This is the execution phase; need signature matching for malicious serialized payloads in SharePoint HTTP traffic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor SharePoint application logs and IIS access logs for POST/PUT requests containing Base64-encoded or binary serialized .NET gadget chains targeting vulnerable endpoints. Flag requests to non-standard SharePoint paths or with abnormal payload sizes.

suggestion.title: SharePoint Service Account Process Execution Anomaly
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability 'allows...execute code over a network' post-exploitation. Without process-level detection, successful exploitation goes undetected until lateral movement occurs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect new processes spawned by w3wp.exe (SharePoint worker) or SharePoint service accounts executing: PowerShell, cmd.exe, tasklist, net commands, or tools outside normal maintenance windows. Alert on first occurrence in environment.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Network Egress from SharePoint
suggestion.rationale: Code execution alone is insufficient; detection must span to impact phase. Exploited SharePoint instances will beacon for C2 or exfiltrate data, requiring network-layer monitoring.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound connections initiated from SharePoint service accounts to non-corporate IP ranges, especially on ports 443, 8080, or dynamic ports. Flag connections to known malware C2 domains, newly registered domains, or IP address scanning behavior.

suggestion.title: Microsoft SharePoint Server CVE-2026-45659 Asset Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Standard asset-exposure hunt… Substitute this CVE wherever the template references `<CVE>`: **CVE:** `CVE-2026-45659`'. Pipeline must surface exposed SharePoint instances. Also: 'U.S. federal "Known Exploited Vulnerabilities" catalog only adds CVEs that have been **observed exploited in the wild**. Federal civilian agencies are required to remediate by the published due date.'

Cross-reference with patch-inventory to flag unpatched instances as immediate remediation priority. CISA KEV status = active exploitation observed.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-45659 Vulnerability Scanner Hit
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Recommended hunts: Standard asset-exposure hunt… CVE: CVE-2026-45659.' Pipeline must map to scanner-based detection for any Tenable, Qualys, or similar integration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on vulnerability scan detections matching CVE-2026-45659 on any SharePoint Server. Severity: critical (CISA KEV status). Auto-escalate non-compliant systems for remediation within federal patch deadline (2026-07-04).

suggestion.title: Patch Compliance Tracking: CVE-2026-45659 Deadline
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Federal patch due: 2026-07-04.' Hard deadline for compliance tracking and regulatory reporting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query Microsoft SharePoint Server inventory for installed patches. Flag any unpatched instances or those with outdated patch levels for CVE-2026-45659 as non-compliant. Generate compliance report by 2026-07-04 deadline.

suggestion.title: Deserialization Attack: Unauthorized Code Execution on SharePoint
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'deserialization of untrusted data vulnerability which allows an authorized attacker to execute code over a network.' This describes the exploitation mechanism—detection must focus on anomalous code execution from SharePoint processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected child processes spawned by SharePoint application-pool workers (w3wp.exe, owstimer.exe) with suspicious command lines or file/registry modifications. Focus on processes launched from deserialization code paths (System.Runtime.Serialization, BinaryFormatter).

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation: Lateral Movement from Compromised SharePoint
suggestion.rationale: Article describes network code-execution capability; any compromise enables lateral movement and persistence attacks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on suspicious outbound network connections from SharePoint servers to internal systems, unexpected credential usage originating from SharePoint service accounts, or SMB/RDP activity initiated from SharePoint processes.

suggestion.title: SharePoint Server Network Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'authorized attacker to execute code over a network' on 'public-facing application'—requires asset inventory and exposure detection before exploitation can occur.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify all instances of Microsoft SharePoint Server (port 443/80 services, product banners, certificate metadata) exposed to untrusted networks or reachable from the internet. Cross-reference against vulnerability scanner data for CVE-2026-45659 status.

suggestion.title: Deserialization Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'deserialization of untrusted data vulnerability'—deserialization attacks generate characteristic HTTP POST patterns with binary/serialized payloads. Pipeline should hunt for exploitation attempts before code execution occurs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor SharePoint web tier for POST requests to sensitive endpoints (/_vti_bin, /sites/) with anomalous content-encoding (gzip, deflate) or binary-looking request bodies. Look for 400/500 errors followed by successful connections (sign of exploit iteration).

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Code Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article describes vulnerability 'allows...execute code'—successful exploitation generates child process creation or command execution under SharePoint worker process (w3wp.exe). Pipeline must detect execution phase after initial compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected child processes spawned by w3wp.exe (or OWSTIMER.EXE for timer jobs), particularly cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or network utilities. Correlate with preceding HTTP requests to /_vti_bin/ endpoints and unexpected outbound connections.

suggestion.title: Patch Compliance Against Federal Due Date
suggestion.rationale: Article cites 'Federal patch due: 2026-07-04'—pipeline should generate asset-based remediation tracking to enforce compliance deadline, distinguishing patched vs. vulnerable instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inventory all CVE-2026-45659-affected SharePoint Server versions (2013, 2016, 2019, Online) and enforce patch status tracking. Flag instances not remediated by 2026-07-04 for escalation.

suggestion.title: Vulnerability Scanner False Negatives
suggestion.rationale: Article warning: 'even if your scanners say not vulnerable because of patches, it's worth one quick check'—implies scanner lag or misconfiguration. Pipeline should validate scanner accuracy against network reachability and product versioning.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference vulnerability scanner 'not vulnerable' verdicts for CVE-2026-45659 against manual service enumeration of SharePoint farm. Alert when scanner reports 'patched' but network enumeration or build metadata contradicts (version mismatch, plugin signatures, listening service version).

suggestion.title: Abnormal Microsoft Device Code Flow Requests
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly names 'Device-Code Flow' as the abuse vector. Pipeline missed primary attack surface entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Microsoft Entra ID for rapid or repeated device code flow initiation events from non-standard clients or geographic anomalies. Flag cases where device code is requested but never redeemed (failed attack attempt), or where redemption occurs from geographically distant IP within seconds of request.

suggestion.title: DEBULL Malware / Tooling Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article title references 'DEBULL Tooling' as the attack tool; pipeline failed to surface process execution or file-based indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for process or file names containing 'DEBULL', 'debull', or known variants. Monitor for unsigned PowerShell/cmd execution patterns typical of device code flow exploitation frameworks launching after successful credential theft.

suggestion.title: M365 Bulk Data Access Following Device Code Authentication
suggestion.rationale: Title indicates 'M365 Accounts' as targets; pipeline did not generate exfiltration detection for post-credential-compromise data access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect anomalous bulk mail export, calendar export, or file download operations within 30 minutes of a device code flow authentication event. Correlate device code redemption IP, tenant, and user identity to subsequent M365 API calls (Search-Mailbox, Get-Mailbox, Export-Mailbox cmdlets in logs).

suggestion.title: Device Code Token Reuse or Long-Lived Refresh Token Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Device code flow vulnerability often leads to token theft; pipeline missed persistence and lateral movement use cases tied to token compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag refresh token or device code tokens used for authentication from multiple user agents, IP addresses, or countries in a single session. Detect tokens issued via device code flow being leveraged to add secondary credentials to compromised accounts.

suggestion.title: M365 Delegated Access Grants by Compromised User
suggestion.rationale: Device code flow often tricks users into consenting to high-privilege OAuth scopes; pipeline missed OAuth consent abuse detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for new OAuth application consents (especially Mail.ReadWrite, Files.ReadWrite.All, Directory.Read.All) granted during or shortly after a device code flow authentication spike. Correlate to third-party app registrations with suspicious metadata or lacking public publisher verification.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Device Code Flow from Non-Browser User Agents
suggestion.rationale: Device code flow is designed for device-constrained scenarios but can be abused by bots; pipeline did not generate user-agent-anomaly detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on device code flow initiation from user agents that lack typical web browser signatures (e.g., curl, Python requests, Go http clients). Detect device code redemption using a different user agent than the request, indicating token forwarding or bot-driven abuse.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Windows Device Hardware ID Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Article title references 'Windows Device ID Helped FBI Trace' — implies attacker discovery/exfiltration of HWID. Pipeline missed detection hypothesis for T1592.004 (Client Configurations) via WMI/registry queries for device identification.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Look for process execution of 'Get-WmiObject' or 'wmic' querying Win32_ComputerSystemProduct, Win32_BaseBoard for UUID/SerialNumber; registry access to HKLM\HARDWARE\DESCRIPTION\System; or PowerShell WMI queries for hardware identifiers. Legitimate endpoints rarely enumerate raw device IDs outside deployment contexts.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Device ID Cross-Reference
suggestion.rationale: Article implies device ID was forensic pivot for FBI attribution — suggests threat actor reused HWID across multiple accounts/systems. No UC for detecting reuse of hardcoded or cached device identifiers in lateral movement artifacts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate failed/successful logons with identical Windows Device IDs across unrelated user accounts or unusual source–destination pairs. Flag when a single device ID is associated with multiple user contexts within short time window, indicating potential credential reuse or token impersonation.

suggestion.title: Scattered Spider Credential Access Pattern (Social Engineering)
suggestion.rationale: Scattered Spider is known for social engineering and credential theft. Article references FBI court filing of attacker, but pipeline missed actor-specific TTPs. No UC for their typical phishing-to-shell workflow.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect high-volume failed VPN/RDP authentication attempts preceded by suspicious email opens (Office 365 logs) or unusual PowerShell credential prompt activity. Look for out-of-band authentication attempts after phishing indicators.

suggestion.title: Defense Evasion via Token Impersonation (Scattered Spider TTP)
suggestion.rationale: Scattered Spider is documented as using token impersonation and living-off-the-land binaries. Article context (criminal attribution) implies evasion techniques were core to their operations but completely absent from pipeline output.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious use of runas.exe, createprocessasuser API calls, or Mimikatz variants. Flag parent-child process chains where legitimate system binaries (whoami, net.exe) are launched from unusual parents or non-standard service accounts.

suggestion.title: JoomShaper SP Page Builder Unauthenticated File Upload
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'unauthenticated users to upload arbitrary files' — core attack surface for T1190 is public-facing app exploitation via upload handler.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor POST/file-upload endpoints to JoomShaper plugin paths (commonly /components/com_sppagebuilder/ or /plugins/joomshaper/) for requests without valid session tokens. Baseline upload frequency and file types; alert on suspicious extensions or polyglot uploads.

suggestion.title: PHP Code Execution from JoomShaper Uploads
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability results in 'upload and execution of PHP code' — execution phase detection required alongside initial access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for newly created .php files in web-accessible directories (e.g., /tmp, upload folders, media cache) followed by process execution spawning child processes (apache/php-fpm). Correlate file creation timestamps with prior suspicious uploads within the same session window.

suggestion.title: JoomShaper SP Page Builder Asset Inventory Validation
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entries mandate asset exposure checks; article states federal patch due 2026-07-10 — scan for unpatched installations regardless of reported patch status.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner data for CVE-2026-48908 and Joomla installations with SP Page Builder plugin active. Cross-reference with patch/component version records; prioritise assets where last scan is >7 days old (stale patch status). Validate with manual web fingerprinting (check Joomla /administrator path and plugin manifest files).

suggestion.title: Polyglot/Double-Extension File Upload Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Unrestricted upload vulnerabilities often bypass extension filters via double-extension (.php.jpg) or null-byte tricks; article describes 'dangerous type' but does not specify bypass technique — should hunt for common evasions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag POST uploads with Content-Type mismatch (e.g., application/octet-stream claimed as image/jpeg), filenames with double extensions (.php.png, .phtml.jpg), null bytes (%00), or HTaccess/web.config uploads to web-accessible paths.

suggestion.title: Detect JoomShaper SP Page Builder Installation via HTTP Fingerprinting
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes JoomShaper as the vulnerable product with unauthenticated upload capability — need to first identify exposed instances. Article: 'allows unauthenticated users to upload arbitrary files'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for HTTP GET/HEAD requests to known JoomShaper paths (e.g., /administrator/, /modules/mod_sppagebuilder, component.php?option=com_sppagebuilder) and HTTP 200 responses that fingerprint the product via response headers or HTML content matching JoomShaper signatures.

suggestion.title: Detect Arbitrary File Upload to SP Page Builder Upload Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Core attack vector explicitly described: 'unrestricted upload of file with dangerous type vulnerability that allows unauthenticated users to upload arbitrary files'. Need detection on the upload POST itself.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on POST requests to JoomShaper upload endpoints (e.g., /index.php?option=com_sppagebuilder&task=form_upload) containing file extensions commonly blocked by policy (.php, .phtml, .php5, .php7, .php8) or MIME type mismatches (e.g., Content-Type: image/jpeg but binary content is PHP).

suggestion.title: Detect PHP Execution from Web-Accessible Upload Directory
suggestion.rationale: Attack outcome explicitly stated: 'ultimately resulting in the upload and execution of PHP code'. Need post-exploitation process detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process creation events where the parent process is a web server (Apache, Nginx, IIS) or php-fpm and the command line references files located in common web-upload directories (e.g., /var/www/html/images, /home/*/public_html/uploads, C:\inetpub\wwwroot\uploads) with recent file access times.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure Scan for CVE-2026-48908 via Vulnerability Scanner
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entry explicitly requires vulnerability scanner correlation. Article: 'CVE-2026-48908 — match against your vulnerability scanner'. Article also mandates applying asset-exposure template.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate vulnerability scanner output for CVE-2026-48908 against asset inventory. Flag any JoomShaper SP Page Builder instances in the wild showing vulnerability status 'vulnerable' or older versions <2.x (if patch version is available). Cross-reference against network-facing asset lists to prioritize exposed instances.

suggestion.title: Detect Unusual Outbound Connections from Compromised Web Server
suggestion.rationale: PHP code execution on web server may lead to data exfiltration or C2 callbacks. Article establishes RCE as endpoint: 'resulting in...execution of PHP code' implies attacker control.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: For web servers running JoomShaper, alert on outbound DNS queries or TCP connections initiated from the web server process or PHP worker processes to non-whitelisted external IPs or domains, especially on ports 22, 443, 4444, 8080, or dynamic high ports indicative of reverse shells.

suggestion.title: Detect Suspicious PHP Code Patterns in Upload Directories
suggestion.rationale: Attack requires uploaded PHP payload. Article: 'unauthenticated users to upload arbitrary files, ultimately resulting in...PHP code' — need file content inspection on disk.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: File Integrity Monitoring (FIM) or EDR file scan alert on any .php, .phtml, .php5 file appearing in web-accessible upload directories after activity. Correlate file creation/modification time with preceding HTTP POST requests. Inspect file content for common webshell patterns: eval(), system(), exec(), shell_exec(), passthru(), function_exists().

suggestion.title: JoomShaper Asset Inventory + Exposure Check
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' and directs substitution of CVE into asset templates. Pipeline generated nothing. Article states: 'unauthenticated users to upload arbitrary files' — requires first identifying exposed instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate web assets running JoomShaper SP Page Builder via port scanning, banner grabbing, or web crawling. Cross-reference against patch status / vulnerability scanner results. Alert on any instances running known-vulnerable versions accessible from untrusted networks.

suggestion.title: PHP File Upload to Web Root (Exploitation)

suggestion.title: Web Server Process Spawning Post-Upload (Post-Exploitation)
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'execution of PHP code' — implies web server (Apache, Nginx) will spawn PHP-CGI or php-fpm child processes. Pipeline did not suggest monitoring for suspicious process lineage post-upload.

suggestion.title: Upload Endpoint Access Pattern Anomalies (Pre-Exploitation)
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'unauthenticated users' exploiting this. Pipeline did not suggest detection of unauthenticated access to upload endpoints. Reconnaissance or brute-force attempts should precede successful exploitation.

suggestion.title: Known-Vulnerable JoomShaper Version Detection in Web Headers
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies product 'JoomShaper SP Page Builder.' Version fingerprinting via HTTP response headers, HTML meta tags, or JavaScript file versions is standard Joomla reconnaissance. Pipeline did not surface signature detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search web proxy logs and WAF logs for HTTP responses containing JoomShaper-specific headers, script paths (/components/com_sppagebuilder/*), or HTML meta tags disclosing version. Alert on vulnerable version strings. Correlate with later POST attempts to upload endpoints.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized File Upload to JoomShaper SP Page Builder
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'allows unauthenticated users to upload arbitrary files' — core attack vector, no detection generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for POST/multipart requests to JoomShaper SP Page Builder upload endpoints (commonly /images/upload, /media/upload, or similar paths) from external sources with suspicious file extensions (php, phtml, php5, etc.). Baseline upload activity and flag repeated failed uploads or uploads of non-image files.

suggestion.title: PHP Code Execution Post-Upload

suggestion.title: Web Shell Indicators Post-Exploitation

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48908 Vulnerability Scan Hits
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly references CVE-2026-48908; IOCs should include this identifier for correlation with vulnerability scanners and web logs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference vulnerability scanner output for CVE-2026-48908 or JoomShaper SP Page Builder version detection. Correlate scanner hits with actual exploit attempts (file uploads) within 48 hours to identify active exploitation.

suggestion.title: Multipart Form Upload Abuse Detection

suggestion.title: Unrestricted File Upload Detection

suggestion.title: Dangerous File Type Upload to Web Root

suggestion.title: PHP Code Execution Post-Upload
suggestion.rationale: The article threat model ends with 'execution of PHP code' — detection must identify when newly uploaded files are executed by the web server process.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48908 Vulnerability Scanner Match
suggestion.rationale: Article is a CISA KEV entry — vulnerability scanners should flag instances; detection should correlate scanner findings with network traffic to the affected product.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on vulnerability scanner results for CVE-2026-48908 on JoomShaper SP Page Builder installations. Cross-reference with network traffic logs to identify if scanned instances are receiving suspicious POST requests to upload endpoints.

suggestion.title: Web Shell Persistence Detection

suggestion.title: JoomShaper SP Page Builder – Unauthenticated file upload
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'allows unauthenticated users to upload arbitrary files.' Pipeline generated zero use cases despite this being the vulnerability entry point.

suggestion.title: PHP code execution post-upload

suggestion.title: Web shell persistence via JoomShaper upload
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation likely proceeds to persistence via uploaded web shell. Article describes execution but not persistence implications.

suggestion.title: Asset inventory – JoomShaper SP Page Builder exposure
