suggestion.title: ColdFusion Arbitrary Code Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article impact states 'arbitrary code execution in the context of the current user.' Detect post-exploitation execution spawned from ColdFusion process context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for child processes spawned by ColdFusion runtime (cfusion.exe, java.exe under CF context) with unusual parent-child chains, command-line obfuscation, or execution from temp directories.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Suspicious File System Access
suggestion.rationale: Path traversal inherently involves accessing files outside normal application scope. Article describes traversal leading to code execution, implying file discovery and access (T1083).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect ColdFusion service account accessing system files, config directories, or paths inconsistent with application baseline. Correlate filesystem access with preceding HTTP path-traversal requests for exploitation confirmation.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable ColdFusion Patch Compliance
suggestion.rationale: Article warns 'patch lag is the silent killer' and sets Federal due date 2026-07-10. Must verify ColdFusion instances running unpatched versions vulnerable to CVE-2026-48282.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanners and asset inventory for ColdFusion versions matching CVE-2026-48282 affected range. Flag unpatched instances and raise compliance violation for breach of Federal remediation deadline.

suggestion.title: Ghost cache-layer XSS payload in cached response bodies
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'allowing [XSS injection] to be served to subsequent visitors requesting the same page' but pipeline detects only header presence, not actual malicious payloads. Cached responses with script tags/JavaScript URLs must be detected.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for HTTP 200/304 responses from Ghost endpoints that contain injected script tags, event handlers, or JavaScript URLs in the response body AND were preceded by a request with x-ghost-preview header. Correlate by URL and timestamp to identify when poisoned content was cached.

suggestion.title: Cache-layer distribution of poisoned content (multi-victim XSS)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'that response could be stored and served to subsequent visitors requesting the same page'—this is the impact phase. Detection requires correlating identical responses served from cache to multiple distinct clients after a poisoning attempt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify sequences where: (1) a single source sends x-ghost-preview header to Ghost, (2) the response contains XSS payload and carries cache-hit indicators (X-Cache: HIT, Age header > 0, Cache-Status: hit), (3) subsequent requests from different sources to the same URL receive identical cached response within short timeframe.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated access to Ghost preview header on caching proxies
suggestion.rationale: Attack precondition: 'unauthenticated user could send an x-ghost-preview header.' Detection must flag any x-ghost-preview header injection from sessions lacking authentication tokens or authorized preview access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for x-ghost-preview header in HTTP requests where: no session cookie is present, Authorization header is missing, and target Ghost instance is behind known CDN/proxy (Fastly, Cloudflare, nginx). Flag any POST/PUT/PATCH with this header as higher-risk.

suggestion.title: Cache-key collision or normalization bypass via x-ghost-preview
suggestion.rationale: Core vulnerability: 'altered the rendered frontend response' suggests the header modifies cached content while sharing the same cache key. Detection should identify when response varies by header but isn't being cache-separated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Compare HTTP responses to identical Ghost URLs with and without x-ghost-preview header. If response bodies differ but X-Cache headers show both were served from cache with same cache-key, the vulnerability is confirmed. Track for patterns of deliberate header injection to trigger cache variation.

suggestion.title: Anomalous caching proxy response times after x-ghost-preview injection
suggestion.rationale: Successful cache poisoning will show measurably different response behavior: first request (miss, 100+ ms) followed by rapid cached hits (< 10ms). Detect this timing signature.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate requests to Ghost with x-ghost-preview header. Baseline normal response times; flag sequences where response time drops sharply (cache hit) immediately after header injection, especially if Cache-Status headers confirm HIT and downstream requests show identical fast responses.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Path Traversal Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states CVE-2026-48282 is 'currently being exploited in the wild' and describes 'path traversal vulnerability.' Web access logs containing path traversal sequences (../, encoding variants) directed at ColdFusion endpoints are the primary exploitation signal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt web server logs for HTTP requests to ColdFusion application URIs containing path traversal payloads (../, %2e%2e, unicode variants). Correlate against scanner alerts identifying CVE-2026-48282 to confirm exploitation attempts versus probing.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Process Spawning Unexpected Child - Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability 'could lead to arbitrary code execution in the context of the current user.' Post-exploitation code execution manifests as ColdFusion JVM or native process spawning cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or scripting interpreters.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal ColdFusion (coldfusion.exe, cfusion.exe, java.exe child) process behavior. Alert on rare or anomalous child processes, especially command shells or interpreters executing encoded scripts, indicating successful exploitation and code execution.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48282 Exposed ColdFusion Instance Correlation
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'anything in CISA KEV is currently being exploited' with Federal remediation deadline 2026-07-10. Standard asset-exposure hunt correlates vulnerability scan results identifying unpatched ColdFusion with network reachability from untrusted sources.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Join vuln-scan output identifying CVE-2026-48282 in ColdFusion against network telemetry. Alert if affected instances show inbound connections from internet-facing sources, DMZ, or suspicious source IPs. Prioritize systems past Federal due date (2026-07-10) without evidence of patching.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Outbound C2 Communication - Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Successful arbitrary code execution will typically result in reverse shell or callback behavior. Article's emphasis on 'currently exploited' implies active post-breach command-and-control infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor egress traffic originating from ColdFusion processes or servers. Alert on rare/unusual outbound connections to external IPs or domains on non-standard ports, especially to known C2 infrastructure or unusual geographic regions for business application.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48282 Exploitation Attempts (Request Anomalies)
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'path traversal vulnerability that could lead to arbitrary code execution' — pipeline should detect malicious path traversal payloads in requests to ColdFusion endpoints. Canonical pattern: `../../../` sequences in HTTP parameters or URI paths targeting ColdFusion app roots.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for HTTP requests containing path traversal sequences (../, %2e%2e%2f, etc.) targeting ColdFusion web paths (/CFIDE, /cfusion, etc.). Pair with 200/404 response codes and unusual file requests. ColdFusion CVE-2026-48282 typically exploits misconfigured admin interfaces.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Code Execution After CVE-2026-48282
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states the vulnerability 'could lead to arbitrary code execution in the context of the current user' — pipeline must correlate successful path traversal with subsequent execution indicators (process spawning, shell activity, etc.).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After a path traversal request succeeds, monitor for child process creation from ColdFusion worker processes (cfusion.exe, java.exe running ColdFusion). Watch for cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or script interpreter spawns with unusual parent-child relationships or low event volume.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion CVE-2026-48282 Asset Exposure (Fingerprinting)
suggestion.rationale: Article recommends 'standard asset-exposure hunt' and states KEV implies 'active exploitation against exposed assets' — pipeline should prioritize identifying publicly-reachable ColdFusion instances vulnerable to this CVE (patch verification).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify ColdFusion web servers via banner grabbing or /CFIDE endpoint enumeration. Cross-reference against vulnerability scanner output for version < patch level (date cutoff 2026-07-10). Flag any public-facing instances without WAF/IPS rules for CVE-2026-48282 path traversal patterns.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Configuration File Access (Path Traversal Indicator)
suggestion.rationale: Path traversal attacks typically target WEB-INF or application config directories containing database credentials and API keys. Article mentions 'path traversal' as attack vector; this is the likely target of exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor ColdFusion process file I/O for reads of config files (web.xml, neo-query.xml, datasources.xml) following suspicious web requests. Watch for directory traversal patterns in filesystem calls originating from the ColdFusion application server.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48282 Vulnerability Scanner Detection (Asset Exposure)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Standard asset-exposure hunt...Substitute this CVE wherever the template references <CVE>: CVE: CVE-2026-48282'. Pipeline ignored directive to generate templated hunt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner outputs for CVE-2026-48282 detections. Cross-reference with patch management to identify gap between detection and remediation. Alert on unpatched instances; prioritize by federal due date 2026-07-10.

suggestion.title: HTTP Path Traversal Attempts Against ColdFusion
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'path traversal vulnerability' as attack vector; no UC maps this exploitation pattern despite it being the named attack mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP access logs for requests containing path traversal sequences ('../', '..%2f', '..%5c') combined with ColdFusion paths (/CFIDE/, /cf_scripts/, /administrator/) or .cfm/.cfml file extensions. Alert on 5+ attempts in 60s window against same host.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Process Execution from ColdFusion
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'arbitrary code execution in the context of the current user'—requires detection of exploitation aftermath. No UC captures post-exploitation process spawning.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on child processes spawned by ColdFusion processes (cfusion.exe, java.exe with ColdFusion classloaders) executing cmd.exe, powershell.exe, cscript.exe, or other shells. Baseline legitimate child processes first to reduce false positives.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion File Write/Read Abuse from Path Traversal
suggestion.rationale: Path traversal → code execution implies file-system interactions outside normal directories. Article omits file-access detection despite 'arbitrary code execution' being the end-state impact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect file access patterns from ColdFusion process (cfusion.exe, w3wp.exe) outside standard ColdFusion web root—especially writes to system directories, temp folders, or unexpected locations. Correlate with HTTP access logs showing path traversal attempts 1-5 minutes prior.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable ColdFusion Scanner Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies CVE-2026-48282 and implies active exploitation ('observed exploited in the wild'). Vulnerability scanner match is the canonical first-line detection for CISA KEV entries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag all ColdFusion instances flagged as vulnerable to CVE-2026-48282 in vulnerability scanner. Cross-reference against patch install dates. Alert on any instance without evidence of patching prior to federal due-date 2026-07-10.

suggestion.title: Path Traversal Attack Patterns in Web Logs
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'path traversal vulnerability.' ColdFusion-exposed web logs will contain ../ or %2e%2e/ sequences in HTTP requests targeting filesystem-sensitive paths.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search ColdFusion web server logs for requests containing path traversal sequences (../, ..\, %2e%2e/) or attempts to access /WEB-INF, /cfusion, or ../../../etc/passwd. Baseline legitimate ColdFusion admin access and alert on outliers.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Arbitrary Code Execution Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'could lead to arbitrary code execution in the context of the current user.' Post-exploitation detection should monitor for process spawning and command execution artifacts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor ColdFusion process (cfusion.exe or java.exe with ColdFusion context) for spawning cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or other shells. Alert on unexpected child processes. Check ColdFusion logs for unusual code evaluation or dynamic compilation events.

suggestion.title: Unpatched ColdFusion Asset Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article provides explicit federal patch due-date (2026-07-10) and recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt.' Asset management and configuration audit logs should enumerate all exposed ColdFusion instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inventory all ColdFusion instances accessible on network (port 8500, 8501, or custom CF ports via banner grabbing). Flag instances with version < fixed version or without patch evidence. Prioritize systems internet-facing or in DMZ.

suggestion.title: Post-Traversal File System Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Path traversal implies navigation outside intended directories. File system audit logs will show ColdFusion process accessing files outside /webroot or /cfusion directories (e.g., /etc/passwd, Windows registry, web.config).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect ColdFusion process reading files with suspicious paths: /etc/passwd, /etc/shadow, Windows registry, cfusion.ini, WEB-INF/web.xml, or parent-directory traversals. Correlate with concurrent web access logs showing ../ patterns within same minute.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Path Traversal Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'path traversal vulnerability that could lead to arbitrary code execution' — pipeline must surface detection for inbound exploitation attempts against ColdFusion endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP requests to ColdFusion application paths containing path traversal sequences (../, ..\ alternations, URL encoding variants). Correlate with ColdFusion access logs for requests to vulnerable endpoints returning 200/302 after traversal payload.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Post-Exploitation Process Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'arbitrary code execution in the context of the current user' — must detect process spawning from ColdFusion service account following successful path traversal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on child processes spawned by ColdFusion worker threads (cfusion.exe, jvm.exe child procs) with command lines containing shell interpreters or script execution, especially if triggered shortly after HTTP 200 responses to ColdFusion paths.

suggestion.title: Public-Facing ColdFusion Asset Inventory and Risk Scoring
suggestion.rationale: Article references 'KEV implies active exploitation against exposed assets' and 'public-facing application' — inventory Internet-facing ColdFusion instances before exploitation window closes (federal due date 2026-07-10).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Network service discovery hunt for ColdFusion default ports (8500, 8501, HTTP/HTTPS on 80/443 serving CF-specific headers). Cross-reference with Internet exposure scanning and vulnerability scanner results for CVE-2026-48282 to prioritize patch.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48282 Vulnerability Scanner Match and Alert
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly directs: 'CVE: CVE-2026-48282 — match against your vulnerability scanner' — baseline detection must flag any scanner-detected instances of this CVE.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any vulnerability scanner results (Nessus, Qualys, Tenable, Rapid7) reporting CVE-2026-48282 discovery. Escalate findings for ColdFusion instances exposed on public IPs or accessible from untrusted networks.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion File System Access Anomalies from Path Traversal
suggestion.rationale: Path traversal attack vector inherently involves 'file and directory discovery' — detect unusual filesystem paths accessed by ColdFusion following exploitation attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for ColdFusion process accessing files outside its configured webroot or application directories, especially system files (config, registry hives, password stores). Baseline normal ColdFusion read patterns and alert on deviations post-HTTP-200 from suspicious requests.

suggestion.title: Pod Security Admission Label Modification by Project Owner
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability allows users to 'modify Pod Security Admission (PSA) labels on namespaces within their projects.' This is the core exploitation step and should be detectable via namespace/PSA audit logs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for modification of pod-security.kubernetes.io/* labels on namespaces by principals holding Project Owner role in Rancher. Detect changes to PSA enforcement levels (restricted→baseline/privileged) that differ from organizational baseline policies.

suggestion.title: Cluster Member to Project Owner Role Assumption
suggestion.rationale: Article states attack requires 'Cluster Member access' followed by assignment to or creation of 'Project Owner' role. Detect lateral movement or privilege escalation within Rancher RBAC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on creation of new Project Owner role bindings or assumption of existing Project Owner roles by Cluster Member-level accounts. Flag role grant requests that differ from standard onboarding patterns.

suggestion.title: Rancher Host Escape via Namespace Manipulation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'escalation from Project Owner to Host.' Detect final privilege escalation achieving host/node-level access following PSA label tampering.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate PSA label modifications with subsequent host-level code execution or node access. Look for privileged container launches or host filesystem mounts immediately following namespace security policy downgrades.

suggestion.title: Rancher Default RBAC Configuration Weakness Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'default role configuration' is the vulnerability vector. Detect exploitation of overly permissive default Rancher or Kubernetes role bindings.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate Project Owner and Cluster Member role bindings to identify accounts with PSA label modification permissions. Detect queries or enumeration of role capabilities that precede exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-41052 Asset Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Standard vulnerability-asset correlation hunt. Article is indexed under this CVE and provides no other mitigating indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Rancher deployments vulnerable to CVE-2026-41052. Correlate against observed Cluster Member or Project Owner account creation/elevation within 7 days of vulnerability publication.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48282 Vulnerability Inventory Match
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly directs: 'CVE-2026-48282 — match against your vulnerability scanner'. CISA KEV designation means active exploitation; scanner and patch management correlation is the primary detection vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference vulnerability scanner and patch management systems for CVE-2026-48282 matches. Alert if vulnerable instance found and externally facing. Track remediation against federal due date 2026-07-10.

suggestion.title: Internet-Facing ColdFusion Service Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'public-facing application' as attack surface. Canonical OSINT hunt for exposed ColdFusion administrative and application interfaces.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan for externally accessible ColdFusion on admin ports (8500, 8501) and common web ports serving /cfusion, /CFIDE, /admin, /cf_scripts. Any HTTP request from external IP to these paths signals exposure.

suggestion.title: Path Traversal Exploitation Attempts Against ColdFusion
suggestion.rationale: Core vulnerability identified: 'Adobe ColdFusion contains a path traversal vulnerability'. Exploitation payload will contain ../, .../, or URL-encoded variants targeting application and configuration paths.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt ColdFusion web logs for path traversal patterns: ../, %2e%2e, ..\, unicode-encoded sequences in URI. Correlate with HTTP 200/302 responses and paths containing WEB-INF or cfusion. Single hit warrants incident investigation.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Child Process Spawning from ColdFusion Runtime
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability impact: 'could lead to arbitrary code execution in the context of the current user'. Post-exploitation indicators include process spawning from ColdFusion application server.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash spawned as children of cfusion.exe or java.exe. Establish baseline of legitimate ColdFusion child processes; deviations indicate post-exploitation code execution.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Configuration and Credential File Access via Path Traversal
suggestion.rationale: Path traversal typically enables access to WEB-INF/cfusion directory containing datasource credentials, encryption keys, and admin configuration files—secondary objective following initial access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt application logs for file read attempts on WEB-INF/cfusion.ini, datasources.xml via directory traversal patterns. High confidence if remote client receives non-error file content (size > 0). Correlate timeline with vulnerability scanner CVE-2026-48282 alerts.

suggestion.title: Outbound Network Connections Originating from ColdFusion Process
suggestion.rationale: Arbitrary code execution outcome enables reverse shells and C2 callbacks; unexpected network egress from ColdFusion process is direct post-exploitation signal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag DNS queries and TCP/UDP connections from cfusion.exe or java.exe processes to non-whitelisted external IPs/domains. Elevated confidence if correlated with cmd.exe/powershell.exe process creation in same timeframe.

suggestion.title: CVE-2024-42009 XSS Exploitation in Roundcube Webmail
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Opening the email in a vulnerable Roundcube webmail client triggers exploitation of a cross-site scripting flaw tracked as CVE-2024-42009, which executes JavaScript code inside the victim's browser, loading a payload called IceCube.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on JavaScript execution patterns in Roundcube webmail processes, especially payloads fetching external resources or establishing network connections. Detect obfuscated script tags in email bodies combined with anomalous JavaScript eval() or dynamic code execution post-email-rendering.

suggestion.title: IceCube In-Memory Credential Harvesting
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'IceCube is a fully-featured Roundcube stealer that can harvest usernames, passwords, cookies, two-factor authentication (2FA) data, and browser information.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for credential-access patterns from mail-server processes: unusual browser credential store access, 2FA token exfiltration, or outbound network traffic containing Base64-encoded credentials. Correlate process spawn hierarchy with email-client execution context.

suggestion.title: SquareShell PHP Webshell Installation (CVE-2025-49113 Escalation)
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'IceCube uses helpers to exploit a Roundcube deserialization flaw tracked as CVE-2025-49113 and attempts to install SquareShell, a PHP webshell that includes remote code execution capabilities.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PHP file uploads to Roundcube document roots or temp directories immediately following deserialization exceptions. Flag PHP files containing system(), exec(), shell_exec(), or other command-execution functions. Monitor for POST/PUT to .php endpoints from internal scripts.

suggestion.title: VShell Go-Based Backdoor Deployment & C2
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'VShell is a commodity Go-based backdoor that supports interactive shell access and port forwarding, which is commonly used by Chinese threat actors. The malware downloads a shell script that loads another payload, VShell, directly in memory.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify unexpected Go binaries or in-memory payloads spawned on mail servers with outbound network tunneling or reverse-shell patterns. Alert on port-forwarding activity or SOCKS proxy setup from mail-server context. Monitor for DNS queries or C2 beacons following failed webshell installation.

suggestion.title: Spear-Phishing of Academic & National Security Researchers
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'The campaign has been observed since May and focuses on physics and engineering departments, administrators and professors, as well as organizations involved in astrophysics, particle physics, or national security-related research. The attack begins with a malicious email sent from compromised accounts or spoofed domains.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect phishing emails targeting academic research institutions (physics, astrophysics, engineering, national-security sectors) from spoofed university domains or compromised external accounts. Flag emails with no legitimate business purpose sent during off-hours or to admin/faculty distribution lists.

suggestion.title: Roundcube Deserialization RCE Escalation (CVE-2025-49113)
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'IceCube uses helpers to exploit a Roundcube deserialization flaw tracked as CVE-2025-49113' to transition from in-browser stealer to server-side RCE via SquareShell or VShell.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Roundcube PHP error logs for unserialize() exceptions or Type Juggling warnings. Correlate deserialization failures with subsequent child-process spawning or web-shell instantiation. Alert on PHP unserialize() calls receiving untrusted input (POST/GET parameters, session data).

suggestion.title: Ubiquiti UniFi Service Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Article states critical flaws across five UniFi products (Connect, Talk, Access, Protect, OS); detections must cover reconnaissance probes against exposed UniFi management interfaces.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP/HTTPS connections to known Ubiquiti UniFi management ports (8443, 8080, 443) from external networks or anomalous internal subnets. Flag repeated connection attempts, rapid port scans, or User-Agent strings consistent with vulnerability scanners.

suggestion.title: Ubiquiti UniFi Exploit Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Title indicates critical flaws; article does not specify vectors but 'critical' typically implies RCE or auth bypass exploitable without user interaction.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect command execution or file write anomalies on UniFi controller hosts immediately after receiving HTTP requests with suspicious payloads (encoded shells, parameter manipulation) to known vulnerable UniFi endpoints.

suggestion.title: Ubiquiti UniFi Version Mismatch or Patch Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Article title emphasizes patches released; detection must verify patched versions are deployed and identify systems still running vulnerable builds.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query UniFi application version strings via API or log parsing; flag systems reporting version numbers below patch cutoff. Cross-reference deployment inventory against security advisory release notes to identify gaps in patch coverage.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via UniFi Connect Service
suggestion.rationale: UniFi Connect is listed as affected; this component typically handles device communication within mesh/federation architectures, enabling lateral pivots if compromised.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for anomalous inter-device communication initiated from a single compromised UniFi node (e.g., unusual source IPs, ports, or protocol anomalies on UniFi cluster ports 6789, 27017).

suggestion.title: Ubiquiti UniFi Privilege Escalation via Access or OS Flaw
suggestion.rationale: UniFi Access and OS products are listed; these typically run with elevated privileges and control network appliances; escalation tactics would follow initial foothold.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect privilege elevation attempts targeting UniFi service processes (unifi, unifi-os); flag spawning of shells or utilities with SYSTEM/root context from UniFi daemon accounts or inherited token impersonation.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Administrative Access to Patched UniFi Systems
suggestion.rationale: Post-patch, systems must still validate no persistence was established during pre-patch window; admin access logs are critical.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for newly created local admin accounts, SSH keys, or API credentials created on UniFi controllers during pre-patch vulnerability window; correlate login timestamps with exploit attempt logs.

suggestion.title: Phishing Email Campaign Detection by Volume and Sender Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article title 'New Ghost Phishing Wave' explicitly signals coordinated campaign. Pipeline must map characteristic mass-phishing indicators: multiple emails from external senders, shared URLs/attachments, temporal clustering.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on sudden spike in emails (>50 in 1hr window) from new external senders containing shared suspicious links, sender-spoofing attempts, or urgency-based social engineering language (account verification, urgent action needed).

suggestion.title: Email Security Control Bypass Indicators
suggestion.rationale: 'Breaking Traditional Email Security' indicates evasion of SPF/DKIM/DMARC, email filters, or sandboxes. Pipeline should surface defense-evasion techniques specific to email gateway bypass.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect emails authenticated as legitimate (bypassed DMARC checks), obfuscated URL encodings, lookalike domains differing by 1-2 characters from targets, or messages marked phishing/malicious yet successfully delivered to user inbox.

suggestion.title: Credential Submission Post-Phishing Click
suggestion.rationale: Phishing campaigns succeed through credential harvesting. Phrase 'wave' establishes coordinated credential-access objective requiring post-click detection of fake login pages.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate phishing email receipt with user visits to newly-registered credential-harvesting domains (generic login templates, brand-name-impersonating landing pages) followed within 2 hours by failed or anomalous sign-in attempts to legitimate cloud services.

suggestion.title: Account Takeover Post-Phishing Success
suggestion.rationale: Article implies 'breaking' email security leads to account compromise. Pipeline must detect post-breach account abuse: inbox rules, forwarding, unauthorized access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor phishing-targeted accounts for inbox rule creation (especially forwarding), suspicious mail folder access from new IPs/geographies, calendar/delegate additions, or bulk file downloads within 4 hours of credential compromise.

suggestion.title: Phishing Infrastructure Assembly Detection
suggestion.rationale: Coordinated 'wave' requires prepared domains and payloads. Pipeline should detect registration of look-alike domains, WHOIS privacy masking, or bulk domain registrations preceding campaign.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag DNS queries to newly-registered or recently-modified domains with typosquatting patterns (homoglyph substitution, subdomain spoofing) matching legitimate targets; correlate with email sender IPs or WHOIS registration timestamps within 7 days of phishing campaign launch.

suggestion.title: Unusual Email Forwarding and Delegation Post-Delivery
suggestion.rationale: Successful phishing often leads to email account takeover and forwarding setup to exfiltrate future emails. Article 'breaking security' suggests post-access control of compromised accounts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect creation of inbox forwarding rules or delegate access grants on previously-phished user accounts, especially forwarding to external domains or newly-added delegates with no prior access history.

suggestion.title: ClickFix Fake Tech-Support Payload Delivery
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly uses 'ClickFix Lures' in title—this is social-engineering delivery via fake browser notifications pretending to offer tech support. Pipeline missed the initial-access vector entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for downloads of executable/script files from ClickFix infrastructure domains or suspicious CDNs hosting fake tech-support popups. Correlate with user clicks on fake browser notifications and subsequent process spawning from browser temp folders.

suggestion.title: SCMBANKER Banking Malware Process Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article names 'SCMBANKER Malware'—a banking trojan family. No detection for post-delivery malware execution patterns (command shells, script interpreters launching from temp directories after ClickFix).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect suspicious child processes spawned by browsers or scripts (powershell.exe, cmd.exe, cscript.exe) following ClickFix artifact staging. Monitor for unusual DLL loads indicating banking-credential-grabber modules.

suggestion.title: Banking Credential Harvesting Post-SCMBANKER Infection
suggestion.rationale: Malware targets 'Mexican Banking Users'—implies credential theft as primary objective. Pipeline missed detection for keylogging, form-grabbing, or browser-credential-vault access post-infection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious handle opens to browser credential stores, LSASS process access, or WinAPI keylogging hooks. Correlate with banking-application-window-focus events and unusual clipboard/form-field interactions.

suggestion.title: Banking Malware Persistence via Registry Run Keys
suggestion.rationale: Banking trojans require persistent reinfection. Article does not detail persistence, but pipeline should generate standing detection for registry-based persistence common to SCMBANKER-family malware.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on modifications to HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run and Startup folders for banking-malware-signature values. Cross-reference with file writes to AppData/Temp and scheduled task creation for persistence.

suggestion.title: SCMBANKER C2 Exfiltration of Banking Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Stolen credentials and session tokens must be exfiltrated to attacker C2. Pipeline has no detection for outbound connections to SCMBANKER C2 infrastructure or encrypted credential-theft payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for persistent outbound HTTPS connections to known SCMBANKER C2 domains on non-standard ports. Correlate with in-memory credential-harvester module signatures and unusual banking-app behavior contemporaneous with connection bursts.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Access to Mexican Banking Systems Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Ultimate objective: fraud against Mexican banks. Pipeline should surface detections for lateral movement into banking VPNs, session-hijacking, or unauthorized fund transfers using stolen credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag logins to banking applications from non-expected geographies or times post-SCMBANKER infection. Monitor for unusual fund-transfer requests, ACH/wire originations, or account-balance queries from compromised user sessions.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Path Traversal in HTTP Requests
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'path traversal vulnerability' leading to 'arbitrary code execution.' Pipeline must detect exploitation attempts: requests containing traversal patterns (`../`, `%2e%2e%2e%2f`, encoded dots) targeting ColdFusion endpoints. Article phrase: 'contains a path traversal vulnerability.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP request logs (WAF, proxy, IIS) for requests to ColdFusion administrative or dynamic endpoints containing path traversal sequences. Flag requests with double-encoded dots, absolute path references, or attempts to read system files (web.config, cfusion.ini, system32). ColdFusion apps typically expose `/cfusion/`, `/CFIDE/`, or custom CFM routes.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Process Spawning from ColdFusion Runtime
suggestion.rationale: Article states the vulnerability 'could lead to arbitrary code execution in the context of the current user.' Pipeline must detect post-exploitation code execution. Phrase: 'arbitrary code execution.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect processes spawned by CFML engine processes (ColdFusion.exe, cfusion.exe, or jrun.exe on Windows; java process with ColdFusion config on Linux). New child processes with unusual parents, encoded/obfuscated command lines, or network communication immediately after spawning indicate post-exploitation activity. Baseline expected children: cfusion processes spawning logging utilities only.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion File Read Outside Webroot
suggestion.rationale: Path traversal implies reading arbitrary files outside intended directories. Article: 'path traversal vulnerability that could lead to arbitrary code execution.' Attacker accesses sensitive config or source files.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor file-access events on ColdFusion application directories. Flag reads of system-sensitive files (SAM, LSASS dumps, windows/system32), parent directory traversal (ColdFusion reads ../../../), or access to configuration files outside designated paths. Correlate with HTTP requests received in the same timeframe for path-traversal patterns.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48282 Scanner Reconnaissance
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV implies active scanning by threat actors. Pipeline should detect probing for vulnerable ColdFusion instances. Article: 'CISA KEV entry...only adds CVEs that have been observed exploited in the wild.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect scanning behavior: multiple requests to known ColdFusion paths (e.g., `/CFIDE/`, `/cfusion/`) from external IPs within short time windows. Flag attempts to access version-identification endpoints or CVE-2026-48282 proof-of-concept payloads. Correlate with IPS/WAF logs for CVE-2026-48282 exploit signatures.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Web-Accessible Configuration Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Path traversal may expose ColdFusion config files (datasource credentials, admin settings). Article: 'arbitrary code execution in the context of the current user' implies data access as well.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for access to .cfm config files, cfusion.ini, server.xml, or datasource definition files. Flag HTTP GET requests to CF admin interfaces (/CFIDE/administrator) or unusual direct file-serve attempts (path traversal fetches config as static content). Correlate timing with network exfiltration to unknown hosts.

suggestion.title: Adobe ColdFusion CVE-2026-48282 Asset Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' and references template substitution with CVE-2026-48282. Exposed ColdFusion instances are the initial-access vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan for exposed Adobe ColdFusion instances on standard ports (8500, 8501, 80, 443). Enumerate vulnerable versions by fingerprinting admin endpoints (/CFIDE, /cfusion) and comparing against affected build ranges. Cross-correlate with external-IP inbound HTTP/HTTPS traffic to ColdFusion application paths.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Path Traversal Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'path traversal vulnerability' as the exploitation technique. Detection must cover directory-traversal payload variants in HTTP requests targeting ColdFusion.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor ColdFusion access logs and web proxy logs for HTTP requests containing path-traversal patterns (../, %2e%2e, URL-encoded variants) in query strings, POST data, or HTTP headers. Alert on 4xx response codes clustering with traversal attempts or anomalous file-read operations in ColdFusion application directories.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Post-Exploitation Remote Code Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability 'could lead to arbitrary code execution in the context of the current user.' Execution follows successful path traversal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Post-exploitation: monitor for child processes spawned by cfusion.exe or java.exe (ColdFusion JVM) with non-standard command lines (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, curl, wget). Detect suspicious file writes to web-accessible directories (webroot, /CFIDE) for webshell staging. Correlate filesystem and process events within seconds of logged path-traversal attempts.

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect repeated HTTP requests with incrementally increasing traversal depth (../, ../../, ../../../) or requests to system paths (/etc/passwd, /windows/win.ini, ../../../apache/conf/httpd.conf). Alert on 200 responses indicating readable files; correlate timing with subsequent exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: HTTP Path Traversal Against ColdFusion
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'path traversal vulnerability' as the attack mechanism. Must detect inbound HTTP requests containing path traversal payloads (../ sequences) targeting ColdFusion application paths and file handlers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP access logs for requests containing path traversal sequences (../ or ..\) targeting ColdFusion application directories, CFML file extensions (.cfm, .cfc), or common traversal targets (/etc/passwd, /windows/system32). Correlate with 400-series HTTP responses and WAF blocks. Alert on repeated attempts from same source.

suggestion.title: Code Execution from ColdFusion Service

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process creation events where ParentImage is ColdFusion runtime (cfml.exe, jrun.exe, or coldfusion.exe) spawning cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or other command shells, especially with suspicious arguments (encoding, Base64 detection, obfuscation markers). Baseline normal CF processes and alert on outliers.

suggestion.title: File Access Anomalies from ColdFusion Context

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor file-access events where the source process is ColdFusion runtime and the target file path is outside expected application and CF installation directories (/coldfusion/, /jrun/, app root paths). Flag access to sensitive directories (/windows/, /etc/, /var/www outside app root, /home). Establish baseline of legitimate directory access per environment.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Network Connections from ColdFusion
suggestion.rationale: Post-exploitation, the attacker may use the code-execution primitive to establish command-and-control or lateral-movement connections. Must detect unexpected outbound network connections from ColdFusion services.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on outbound connections from ColdFusion processes (cfml.exe, coldfusion.exe) to non-whitelisted destinations, especially high ports (>10000), known C2 CIDR ranges, or recently-registered domains. Correlate with process-creation events showing suspicious spawns from the same CF process. Use baseline-deviation detection for CF network behavior.

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag all assets reporting CVE-2026-48282 in scanner inventory. Prioritize Internet-facing ColdFusion instances. Track remediation against federal due-date 2026-07-10. Cross-correlate scanning timestamp with exploitation indicators to assess patch lag vulnerability.

suggestion.title: HTTP Path Traversal Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'path traversal vulnerability' as primary attack vector but pipeline created no web-layer detection rule despite path-traversal patterns being detectable in access logs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests to ColdFusion endpoints containing `../`, `..\`, `%2e%2e`, or Unicode-encoded traversal sequences. Alert on requests attempting to escape wwwroot or accessing sensitive directories (/windows/, /etc/, etc.).

suggestion.title: ColdFusion-Spawned Code Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'arbitrary code execution in the context of the current user.' Pipeline missed process-creation detection from ColdFusion service accounts executing unexpected child processes (shells, utilities).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when ColdFusion process (cfusion.exe, jrun.exe) spawns cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or other shell interpreters with unexpected arguments. Flag parent-child relationships anomalous to normal ColdFusion operation.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Filesystem Escape Detection
suggestion.rationale: Path traversal attacks require accessing files outside the application root. Article describes filesystem-based attack but pipeline generated no file-access anomaly detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor ColdFusion process file-access events for rapid enumeration or access to directories outside wwwroot (System32, Program Files, Windows registry hives). Baseline normal ColdFusion file patterns first.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Application Log Exception Analysis
suggestion.rationale: ColdFusion logs contain path-resolution errors preceding successful traversal. Article points to exploitation but pipeline omitted application-log-source detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Parse ColdFusion logs for access-denied, path-not-found, or traversal-triggered security exceptions. Correlate exception timestamps with web-server 400/403 HTTP responses to prioritize investigation.

suggestion.title: Web Application Firewall Path Traversal Blocking
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies public-facing ColdFusion as attack surface ('Exploit Public-Facing Application'). Network-layer WAF rules are standard mitigation but pipeline proposed no WAF-native detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enable ColdFusion-specific path-traversal rules in WAF. Alert on WAF blocks matching CVE-2026-48282 exploitation signatures. Correlate WAF blocks with application logs to measure evasion attempts.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48282 Vulnerability Presence Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies CVE-2026-48282 in Adobe ColdFusion as the vulnerability. Pipeline generated zero use cases despite this being the core detection target.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner exports and patch-compliance databases for ColdFusion instances reporting CVE-2026-48282 or running unpatched ColdFusion versions released before 2026-07-10 federal remediation deadline. Cross-reference with asset inventory to identify exposed instances.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Public-Facing Application Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article states T1190 'exploit public-facing application' and describes vulnerability as actionable against exposed ColdFusion. Pipeline failed to generate asset-exposure baseline despite template references.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate ColdFusion instances (default ports 8500, 80, 443 with ColdFusion headers) accessible from untrusted networks. Log source could be firewall ACL reviews, web server headers in proxy logs, or port-scanning data. Flag any public-facing instances as T1190 targets.

suggestion.title: Path Traversal Attempt Detection in ColdFusion Logs
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability type is explicitly 'path traversal' (article: 'path traversal vulnerability that could lead to arbitrary code execution'). Pipeline failed to surface log-based path traversal patterns (.., ../, encoded variants).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search ColdFusion HTTP access logs for suspicious path traversal payloads: sequences containing ../, ..\, %2e%2e, or encoded backslash/dot combinations in query strings and POST bodies. High specificity: match file:// or directory traversal request patterns against known ColdFusion URI handlers.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Process Execution Anomalies Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'arbitrary code execution in the context of the current user.' Pipeline missed execution-phase detection despite explicit mention of code execution outcome.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for abnormal child processes spawned by ColdFusion JVM process (java.exe or cfusion.exe). Baseline includes legitimate scheduled tasks; flag cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or unexpected script interpreters as post-exploitation indicators, especially if preceded by HTTP request pattern matches from path-traversal hunt.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Patch Compliance Audit (Federal Deadline)
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'Federal patch due: 2026-07-10' and emphasizes CISA KEV remediation deadline. Pipeline should have included compliance-tracking use case for regulated entities.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Pull ColdFusion version inventory from patch-management system and cross-reference against Adobe security bulletins for CVE-2026-48282 patched versions. Flag any instances running unpatched builds; generate management report with asset owner, patch deadline (2026-07-10), and business justification (if any) for non-compliance.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48282 Vulnerability Scanner Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states CVE-2026-48282 is the vulnerability indicator and source data opens with 'only adds CVEs that have been observed exploited in the wild.' Pipeline failed to generate scanner-baseline detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag all hosts running Adobe ColdFusion versions affected by CVE-2026-48282. Cross-reference patch status against 2026-07-10 federal due date. High-priority because CISA KEV implies active exploitation.

suggestion.title: HTTP Path Traversal Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'path traversal vulnerability' and 'arbitrary code execution.' Pipeline ignored the attack vector despite it being the mechanism of initial access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP requests to Adobe ColdFusion endpoints containing path traversal sequences (../, ..\ , %2e%2e, etc.) or file-system escape patterns. Focus on publicly-exposed ColdFusion instances.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Process Execution Anomalies Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'could lead to arbitrary code execution in the context of the current user.' Pipeline failed to map execution phase despite explicit description of post-exploitation code execution capability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal child processes spawned by Adobe ColdFusion service account (cfusion.exe, jrun.exe, etc.). Alert on unexpected process launches, script interpreters (powershell.exe, cmd.exe, cscript.exe), or binary downloads from ColdFusion runtime context.

suggestion.title: Adobe ColdFusion File System Access Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Path traversal implies attacker can read/write arbitrary files. Article states impact is 'arbitrary code execution' — requires file write capability that pipeline failed to model as detection scenario.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Adobe ColdFusion service account accessing files outside normal application directories (esp. system/windows dirs, web roots beyond deployed app). Flag reads of config files (cfusion.ini, registry) or writes to executable paths.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement from Compromised ColdFusion Host
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV threat context implies attacker gains code execution on exposed ColdFusion instance; natural next step is lateral movement. Pipeline generated no post-exploitation detection scenarios.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on ColdFusion-compromised host establishing outbound connections to internal assets, spawning network scanning utilities (nmap, psexec, wmic), or accessing SMB shares / named pipes outside normal operational baseline.

suggestion.title: BlueHammer Ransomware Service Termination & File Encryption
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly names 'BlueHammer Ransomware' but pipeline extracted zero detections. No use case for mass encryption or defense-disabling service stops.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate sequential service stop attempts (net stop, wmic) against backup and antivirus services with rapid file encryption operations (bulk .encrypted/.locked extensions) or VSS deletion.

suggestion.title: Apple Mail Client Vulnerability Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Headline flags 'Apple Email Flaw' but pipeline generated no initial-access detection. Should cover email-based code execution or privilege escalation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Mail.app for unexpected child processes, memory-corruption footprints, or unusual file/network activity following vulnerability disclosure date.

suggestion.title: Cloud Compute Resource Hijacking via Credential Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Title emphasizes 'AI Compute Hijacking' but no detection logic for unauthorized GPU provisioning, cloud-resource theft, or compromised API credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on API calls launching GPU-intensive compute instances (p3, p4, A100 nodes) from anomalous principals, geolocations, or after failed authentication spikes.

suggestion.title: Ransomware Pre-Execution Defense Evasion Chain
suggestion.rationale: BlueHammer implies coordinated defense disabling before encryption but no detection for the evasion kill-chain phase (AV/backup service termination).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect kill-chain sequence: service-stop commands → driver/service deletion → VSS removal → followed by file encryption within 5-min window.

suggestion.title: Vulnerability Scanner Detection for CVE-2026-48282
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly directs: 'CVE-2026-48282 — match against your vulnerability scanner'. This is the minimum detection baseline for any CISA KEV entry.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scan results for CVE-2026-48282 detections. Cross-reference with patch management to identify systems that remain vulnerable post-patching-due-date (2026-07-10). Flag externally-exposed systems that remain unpatched.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Path Traversal Web Request Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'path traversal vulnerability' as the attack vector. Web and application logs should capture attempted exploitation via malformed requests.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor ColdFusion HTTP access logs for path traversal patterns: consecutive '../' or '..\\'  sequences, URL-encoded variants (%2e%2e/), or double-encoded attempts. Alert on requests to sensitive paths (admin, config, WEB-INF) or non-200 responses followed by 200s suggesting successful bypass.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Code Execution Following Path Traversal
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'could lead to arbitrary code execution in the context of the current user', requiring execution-phase detection to catch RCE following successful traversal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when ColdFusion service processes (cfusion.exe, coldfusion.jar, java.exe) spawn child processes like cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash, or sh. Correlate process creation timestamps with web access logs showing prior path traversal requests.

suggestion.title: Exposed ColdFusion Service Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' and emphasizes 'patch lag is the silent killer', requiring discovery of all internet-facing ColdFusion instances regardless of stated patch status.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan for exposed ColdFusion services on ports 8500, 8501, 8502, and standard web ports with ColdFusion fingerprints (HTTP headers, login page banners). Compare against approved asset registry to identify rogue or forgotten instances.

suggestion.title: Patch Compliance Audit: CVE-2026-48282 Federal Due Date Miss
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'Federal patch due: 2026-07-10' and 'auditors will ask about compliance timing'. Any system still vulnerable after this date represents a compliance and exploitation risk.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Generate a report of all systems still bearing CVE-2026-48282 vulnerability flags after 2026-07-10. Calculate days-past-due and prioritize by network exposure. Flag systems in compliance-sensitive environments (gov't, finance, healthcare) for escalation.

suggestion.title: Suspicious File Access Outside ColdFusion Web Root
suggestion.rationale: Path traversal attacks read or write files outside intended application directories. Article notes 'arbitrary code execution in the context of the current user' implies lateral file access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file open/read/write/execute events by ColdFusion processes accessing system directories (/etc, /Windows/System32), web server config files, or credential stores. Alert on access patterns inconsistent with normal ColdFusion operation.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48282 Vulnerability Scanner Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'CVE: CVE-2026-48282' and recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt — Substitute this CVE wherever the template references <CVE>.' Pipeline generated zero hunts despite this directive.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search vulnerability scanner output for CVE-2026-48282 matches against any ColdFusion instance. Even patched systems warrant review given 'patch lag is the silent killer' warning and federal due date urgency (2026-07-10).

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Path Traversal Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'path traversal vulnerability' as root attack vector. Article body states 'Adobe ColdFusion contains a path traversal vulnerability.' No detection logic provided for traversal patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for path traversal patterns in HTTP requests to ColdFusion instances (../../../, ..%2F..%2F, etc.). Monitor for abnormal directory access attempts in ColdFusion access logs, especially against sensitive paths (/CFIDE, /administrator, /cfadmin).

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Code Execution from ColdFusion Process
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'could lead to arbitrary code execution in the context of the current user.' No process-level detection hypothesis provided for resulting execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected child processes spawned from ColdFusion service (cfusion.exe, java.exe running coldfusion). Monitor for powershell.exe, cmd.exe, or bash spawned from ColdFusion context with unusual command-line arguments or execution timing correlated with anomalous HTTP traffic.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Admin Panel Access from External Networks
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies this as 'public-facing application' exploit (T1190). Admin panel exposure (ports 8500, 8501) is prerequisite for exploitation. Article warns 'Patch lag is the silent killer' implying unpatched exposed systems are prime targets.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect external-source traffic to ColdFusion default admin ports (8500, 8501, 8502, 8503) or /CFIDE paths from untrusted networks. Correlate with failed authentication attempts or unusual request patterns that indicate reconnaissance or exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48282 Federal Remediation Deadline Alert
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Federal patch due: 2026-07-10' and 'Federal civilian agencies are required to remediate by the published due date.' Imminent deadline (1 day from article date) is compliance-critical and auditor-relevant.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag all unpatched ColdFusion instances as critical before 2026-07-10 federal deadline. Cross-reference asset inventory against patch management system. Create mandatory incident for any ColdFusion host still missing CVE-2026-48282 fixes by deadline.

suggestion.title: Abnormal ColdFusion HTTP Request Patterns Indicating Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes 'observed exploited in the wild' status (CISA KEV designation). Exploitation attempts will manifest in HTTP logs before code execution. No specific exploitation signature provided despite active wild exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for HTTP requests with path traversal payloads, null-byte injection (%00), unicode encoding (%252e), or double-encoding patterns targeting ColdFusion application paths. Correlate request-response pairs showing unexpected file access or error patterns indicating successful traversal.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48282 Adobe ColdFusion Path Traversal Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'CVE-2026-48282 — match against your vulnerability scanner' and describes path traversal leading to arbitrary code execution. Asset-exposure hunt canonically covers this vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests to Adobe ColdFusion endpoints containing path traversal sequences (../, ..\ , encoded variants %2e%2e%2f) or suspicious file-path parameters. Correlate with subsequent process execution or file access outside ColdFusion's intended directories to confirm exploitation.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary Code Execution Post-ColdFusion Path Traversal
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'could lead to arbitrary code execution in the context of the current user.' RCE is the impact; need post-exploitation behavioral detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unexpected child processes spawned by ColdFusion process (java.exe / cfusion processes on Windows, cfusion on Linux) following HTTP requests containing path traversal payloads. Flag shell spawns (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, /bin/bash, /bin/sh) or system utilities (whoami, ipconfig, curl, wget).

suggestion.title: Sensitive File Access via ColdFusion Path Traversal
suggestion.rationale: Path traversal aims to access files outside application root. Article describes traversal leading to RCE; intermediate step is unauthorized file read (web.config, system files, credentials).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor ColdFusion process (java.exe, cfusion) accessing files outside its application directory: Windows system files (System32, SAM, NTDS.dit), configuration files (web.config, cf*.ini), or credential stores. Correlate file-read access with preceding HTTP requests containing ../ sequences.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Process with Elevated Token / Privilege Escalation
suggestion.rationale: Article notes RCE executes 'in the context of the current user'; ColdFusion often runs privileged (SYSTEM, root). Privilege boundaries crossed post-exploitation should alert.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag child processes spawned from ColdFusion that run with elevated integrity level, SYSTEM user, or root account (especially if parent ColdFusion runs under limited-privilege service account). Indicates successful RCE abuse.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48282 Inventory: Adobe ColdFusion Exposed Instances
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV implies active in-the-wild exploitation. Article emphasizes 'asset-exposure hunt' and federal patch due 2026-07-10. Prerequisite is asset discovery.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanners (Nessus, Qualys, Tenable) and asset-inventory systems for Adobe ColdFusion instances with version <X (affected versions per Adobe advisory). Cross-reference with network topology to identify public-facing exposures. Prioritize hosts not patched by federal due-date 2026-07-10.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Instance Exposure Scan
suggestion.rationale: Article states T1190 'implies active exploitation against exposed assets'—requires external-facing ColdFusion discovery. Article explicitly directs: 'Standard asset-exposure hunt.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify ColdFusion instances (standard ports 8500, 8501; HTTP Server headers) accessible from untrusted networks. Cross-correlate with scanner detections for CVE-2026-48282. Flag any unpatched instances as of federal remediation deadline 2026-07-10.

suggestion.title: Path Traversal Attack Detection on ColdFusion
suggestion.rationale: Article defines core vulnerability as 'path traversal.' Exploitation requires directory traversal payloads in HTTP requests to ColdFusion endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests to ColdFusion paths (/CFIDE/*, /cfusion/*, /cf/*) containing traversal patterns ('../', '..\', '%2e%2e') or encoded variants. Correlate with 403/401 responses or ColdFusion error logs for access control bypass attempts.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Arbitrary Code Execution by ColdFusion User
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'could lead to arbitrary code execution in the context of the current user'—detection required for execution phase following successful path traversal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor ColdFusion service account (typically 'coldfusion', 'cfusion', 'www-data') for spawned command shells (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash, sh). Baseline normal behavior; flag child processes with network activity or file write patterns inconsistent with legitimate ColdFusion operations.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48282 Patch Deployment Compliance
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies federal remediation deadline 2026-07-10. Audit control required for government mandate tracking and gap reporting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query inventory for all ColdFusion instances; extract versions and compare against Adobe security bulletins for CVE-2026-48282 patch status. Flag unpatched systems post-deadline by classification level. Report remediation gaps to compliance/risk teams.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Error Log Analysis for Exploitation Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Path traversal attempts would generate access-control or file-not-found errors in ColdFusion logs. Article confirms active exploitation; logs would contain attack signatures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Parse ColdFusion application logs for spikes in 'Access Denied', 'File not found', or 'Path does not exist' errors from external sources. Correlate timestamp and source IP with WAF logs for path traversal patterns. Baseline volume to distinguish from legitimate errors.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion CVE-2026-48282 Vulnerability Match
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'CVE-2026-48282 — match against your vulnerability scanner' as the canonical detection. Pipeline returned empty IOCs and no scan-based UC despite CISA KEV status indicating active exploitation in the wild.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt vulnerability scanner alerts and patch-compliance reports for CVE-2026-48282 or Adobe ColdFusion versions prior to patch release. Prioritize instances marked as publicly accessible or internet-facing. Verify scanner coverage includes all ColdFusion deployments (CFIDE, web roots, scheduled tasks).

suggestion.title: Exposed ColdFusion Instance Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article references T1190 (exploit public-facing application) and explicitly cites 'asset-exposure hunt' template guidance. Pipeline missed the foundational asset-discovery UC required before exploitation can occur.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate ColdFusion instances accessible from internet via port scanning, DNS resolution of *.cfusion.* or *.coldfusion.* subdomains, JARM fingerprinting, or certificate transparency logs. Cross-reference with internal asset inventory to identify unexpected public exposure. Correlate with patch status baseline.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Path Traversal Request Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'path traversal vulnerability' as attack mechanism. Pipeline generated no HTTP-signature or WAF-based UC to catch exploitation attempts at the gate.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to ColdFusion endpoints (.cfm, .cfc files, /cfusion, /CFIDE URIs) for path-traversal indicators: '../', '..\', URL-encoded variants (%2e%2e/), null-byte injection, or double-encoding. Alert on requests returning HTTP 200 to traversal payloads. Baseline normal ColdFusion traffic first.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Arbitrary Code Execution Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'could lead to arbitrary code execution in the context of the current user.' Pipeline generated no execution-phase behavioral UC despite this being the exploitability requirement for CISA KEV status.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for child processes spawned under ColdFusion service account (e.g., cfusion_service, wwwroot_service): cmd.exe, powershell.exe, java.exe with interactive shells. Watch for file writes to web-root or temp directories, outbound network connections from ColdFusion process, and unusual registry/service modifications. Correlate with recent traversal attempts.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Patch Status Compliance by Deadline
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'patch lag is the silent killer' and specifies federal patch due date 2026-07-10. Pipeline ignored the time-critical compliance tracking UC that SOCs must operationalize for federal/regulatory audits.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track Adobe ColdFusion version inventory across all systems. Identify any instances running versions prior to the patched release for CVE-2026-48282. Flag non-compliant systems and validate patch application by deadline 2026-07-10. Report exemptions and compensating controls to compliance/risk.

suggestion.title: Vulnerability Scanner Alert: CVE-2026-48282 Detected
suggestion.rationale: Article is CISA KEV—standard practice mandate. Phrase: 'CVE-2026-48282' with 'Federal patch due: 2026-07-10' establishes temporal urgency for detection logic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert whenever CVE-2026-48282 is detected in vulnerability scan results on any host. Escalate to critical if host runs ColdFusion and is externally accessible. Escalate to incident if detection occurs after federal patch deadline (2026-07-10).

suggestion.title: Exposed ColdFusion Instance Reconnaissance
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'exploit public-facing application' — need inventory of exposed ColdFusion instances. Prerequisite for attack surface validation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for publicly accessible ColdFusion instances on ports 8500, 8501, or standard HTTP/HTTPS with characteristic ColdFusion headers (X-Powered-By, Server: Adobe ColdFusion) or URI patterns (/cfide/, /cf_scripts/). Cross-reference against internal asset inventory; flag any external-facing ColdFusion deployment.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Path Traversal Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'path traversal vulnerability' is the attack vector. Direct log signature for exploitation attempts in request stream.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor web access logs and ColdFusion application logs for path traversal payload patterns in URL query/path/POST body: ../, %2e%2e%2f, ..\, %5c, file://, java.lang, ProcessBuilder, or similar. Correlate against known ColdFusion-exploitable endpoints. Flag as exploitation attempt if paired with 200/302 response (successful traversal).

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Arbitrary Code Execution Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'arbitrary code execution in the context of the current user' — success indicator. Execution phase detection for post-exploitation behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for anomalous child process spawning from ColdFusion JVM process (java.exe/javaw.exe on Windows, java on Linux), especially cmd.exe, powershell.exe, /bin/bash with suspicious arguments. Correlate timing with ColdFusion application access. Alert on unexpected OS command invocation from within ColdFusion context (CFML evaluation, tag invocation).

suggestion.title: ColdFusion C2 Beaconing and Data Exfiltration Post-RCE
suggestion.rationale: Article implies attacker gains code execution. Post-exploitation typically involves C2 communication. Inferred from 'arbitrary code execution' → lateral movement / C2 phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of legitimate outbound connections from ColdFusion instances (license validation, data source queries, Windows updates). Flag unexpected outbound connections to non-standard ports, rare/anonymous ASNs, known malware C2 domains/IPs, or large data transfers from ColdFusion context. Correlate against timing of exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48282 Vulnerability Scanner Match
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies CISA KEV status with federal patch due date 2026-07-10. Any vulnerability scanner result for this CVE must trigger SOC alert given active exploitation confirmation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert whenever CVE-2026-48282 appears in vulnerability scan results. Cross-reference asset inventory to identify unpatched ColdFusion installations. Escalate all detections as critical due to CISA KEV active-exploitation status.

suggestion.title: HTTP Path Traversal Attempts on ColdFusion
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'path traversal vulnerability' as the attack vector. Quote: 'ColdFusion contains a path traversal vulnerability.' Monitor web logs for traversal sequences targeting ColdFusion administrative endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search HTTP request logs for path traversal patterns (../, %2e%2e/, ..\) sent to ColdFusion paths (/cfide/, /administrator/, /cf_scripts/). Alert on POST requests with suspicious payloads to these endpoints, especially from external IPs.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Child Process Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'could lead to arbitrary code execution in the context of the current user.' Successful exploitation manifests as unexpected processes spawned from ColdFusion application context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for child processes spawned from ColdFusion executable (cfusion.exe, java.exe running ColdFusion). Alert on cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash, or sh execution from ColdFusion context, especially with unusual command-line arguments or immediate network connections.

suggestion.title: Exposed ColdFusion Administrative Interfaces
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'public-facing application' as the attack target. Enumerate and monitor externally-reachable ColdFusion admin panels.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Conduct external scan for ColdFusion administrative endpoints reachable from the internet (/cfide/, /CFIDE/, /cfadmin/, /Administrator/). Alert if ColdFusion services respond on standard ports (80, 443, 8500, 8501) to external queries. Track changes weekly.

suggestion.title: Suspicious File Writes Within ColdFusion Directories
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'arbitrary code execution' implies attacker write-capability to filesystem. Monitor ColdFusion application and temp directories for unexpected file creation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected file creation or modification in ColdFusion installation paths and web-accessible directories. Flag creation of .cfm, .cfml, .jar, .exe, or .dll files in ColdFusion class paths. Correlate with ColdFusion process activity.

suggestion.title: CISA KEV Remediation Tracking
suggestion.rationale: Article enforces federal deadline: 'Federal patch due: 2026-07-10.' Continuous inventory and compliance audit is mandatory for federal and regulated environments.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Maintain real-time inventory of ColdFusion versions and patch status. Generate weekly remediation reports. Flag any unpatched instances after federal deadline as compliance violation. Track exception justifications for instances that cannot be patched by deadline.

suggestion.title: Vulnerability Scanner Detection: CVE-2026-48282
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'CVE-2026-48282 — match against your vulnerability scanner' and directs template substitution. Pipeline generated zero scanning-based detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag all instances of Adobe ColdFusion with CVE-2026-48282 vulnerability in scanner output. Cross-correlate with asset inventory to confirm exposure date and confirm patch deployment by federal due-date 2026-07-10.

suggestion.title: Public-Facing ColdFusion Instance Discovery
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'exploit public-facing application' and T1190 mapping. Pipeline missed discovery/inventory detection despite this being a foundational hunt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify externally-accessible ColdFusion endpoints via ingress logs. Cross-match against vulnerability scanner to flag unpatched instances as high-priority targets for exploitation.

suggestion.title: Path Traversal Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'path traversal vulnerability' as the core mechanism. Pipeline failed to generate detections for traversal patterns in application logs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor ColdFusion access logs for path traversal sequences (../, ..\, unicode encoding of traversal patterns). Flag requests with high directory-depth or attempts to access system directories (windows, etc, system32).

suggestion.title: Arbitrary Code Execution from ColdFusion Context
suggestion.rationale: Article states exploitation 'could lead to arbitrary code execution in the context of the current user.' Pipeline generated no process-execution detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline ColdFusion process execution chains. Alert on child processes spawned from ColdFusion (cfusion.exe, java.exe) that are anomalous or run system commands (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, sh) with no corresponding administrative action.

suggestion.title: Outbound Connections from Compromised ColdFusion
suggestion.rationale: Arbitrary code execution typically leads to C2 or lateral movement. Article implies compromise risk but pipeline generated no network-based post-exploitation detection.
