suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor ColdFusion application and web-server access logs for path traversal patterns (../, ..\, %2e%2e, unicode variants) in request URLs or parameters targeting ColdFusion file paths. Alert on attempts to traverse outside intended directories or access system-level resources.

suggestion.title: Unexpected ColdFusion Code Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability 'could lead to arbitrary code execution'. No post-exploitation execution detection offered.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected process spawning, file modifications, or network connectivity initiated from ColdFusion worker processes (cfusion.exe, java.exe under ColdFusion context). Baseline normal ColdFusion behavior and alert on deviations correlated with path-traversal indicators from same host in prior 5-minute window.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion HTTP Request — Path Traversal Pattern Matching
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'path traversal vulnerability' as the attack vector. No detection hypothesis provided despite article explicitly recommending 'asset-exposure hunt' with template substitution. Traversal payloads (../, %2e%2e/, encoded variants, backslash sequences) are observable in HTTP request logs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor ColdFusion-destined HTTP requests for path traversal indicators: encoded dot-segments (%2e%2e), consecutive slashes, backslash sequences, and parent-directory references. Baseline known-benign paths and alert on sequences consistent with CVE-2026-48282 exploitation payloads, particularly from non-internal source IPs.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Process Unexpected Child — Code Execution Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'could lead to arbitrary code execution in the context of the current user.' Exploitation transitions from path traversal (initial access) to process execution (execution phase). No detection for child process spawning post-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag unexpected child processes spawned by ColdFusion application processes (cfexe.exe, java.exe when running ColdFusion). Baseline normal children; alert on cmd.exe, powershell.exe, curl, wget, or temporary-directory scripts spawned in same timestamp cluster as path-traversal HTTP requests.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion File Access — Out-of-Bounds Traversal Targets
suggestion.rationale: Path traversal exploits read/write files outside normal application directory. Article does not recommend file-access monitoring despite describing file-access attack mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor ColdFusion process file I/O for access to system-sensitive paths (Windows\System32, /etc/passwd, parent-directory patterns). Correlate file-access timestamps and paths with HTTP request logs to confirm traversal exploitation chain: request → file access → execution.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Outbound Connection — Post-Exploitation C2
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV indicates 'currently being exploited in the wild'; successful RCE frequently precedes C2 callback. Article addresses exploitation but not post-compromise activity detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unexpected outbound network connections initiated by ColdFusion processes post-exploitation: non-business IPs, high-entropy domains, standard C2 ports (4444, 5555, 8080, 443 to rare external hosts), or DNS queries for dynamic-DNS services.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Application Error — Path Traversal Failure Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Failed and successful path traversal attempts generate ColdFusion-specific exceptions and security events. Article does not recommend application-log monitoring despite providing specific attack mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Parse ColdFusion application logs for path-access violations, file-not-found errors on traversal attempts, or security exceptions during request processing. Correlate exception timestamps and stack traces with external HTTP requests to confirm exploitation attempts and success indicators.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Vulnerable Asset Inventory (CVE-2026-48282)
suggestion.rationale: Article mandates 'standard asset-exposure hunt' and emphasizes 'patch lag is the silent killer' with federal due-date 2026-07-10; detection must inventory ColdFusion versions to identify unpatched instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner or web server version strings to identify ColdFusion instances running vulnerable versions prior to CVE-2026-48282 patch. Correlate asset inventory with CISA KEV due-date to flag remediation gaps.

suggestion.title: Path Traversal Exploitation Attempts (ColdFusion CFIDE)
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'path traversal vulnerability'; exploitation would manifest as directory traversal sequences (../, %2e%2e, etc.) in HTTP requests targeting ColdFusion admin/CFIDE endpoints or configuration paths.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to ColdFusion paths (/CFIDE/, /cfusion, /Administrator) for path traversal encoding patterns and parent directory references. Correlate with public CVE-2026-48282 exploit POCs for exact malicious URI signatures.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Code Execution (ColdFusion Service Account)
suggestion.rationale: Article warns exploitation 'could lead to arbitrary code execution in the context of the current user'; successful exploitation would spawn processes or write CFML files as the ColdFusion service account following path traversal access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process creation (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, csc.exe) or file writes by ColdFusion service accounts within 60s post-exploitation window. Flag anomalous CFML file creation in system temp directories or web root outside deployment processes.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Web Access Anomalies Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article implies active exploitation occurring; successful path traversal would enable attackers to read arbitrary files or execute remote code, leaving traces of unusual file access or web request patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for HTTP requests to ColdFusion admin consoles, CFML file paths, or sensitive configuration endpoints (datasources, extensions) following path traversal attempts. Correlate with error logs indicating unauthorized file or directory access.

suggestion.title: BusySnake Stealer Process Execution & DLL Load
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'BusySnake Stealer' as the malware used by Armored Likho. Pipeline extracted zero use cases despite this. Should detect process creation and module loading patterns associated with known stealer samples.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process execution of known BusySnake Stealer samples or variants by file hash, name pattern, or parent process anomalies. Flag unsigned DLL loads from temp or roaming directories into explorer.exe, outlook.exe, or chrome.exe.

suggestion.title: Information Stealer Credential Access—Screen Capture & Clipboard Exfil
suggestion.rationale: Article references credential theft via 'BusySnake Stealer'—a family designed for data harvesting. Pipeline identified no credential-access detection. Stealers universally perform screenshot and clipboard operations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process events creating or accessing screenshot/clipboard capture APIs (Windows.Graphics.Capture, GetClipboardData, CreateDC). Flag unusual child processes of stealer-suspect parents accessing %TEMP% or %APPDATA% for staged data.

suggestion.title: C2 Beaconing—Stealer Exfiltration to Known Armored Likho Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article states stealer used by Armored Likho for targeting gov/power sector. Pipeline output includes no IOCs, domains, or IP indicators. Should hunt C2 callbacks on protocol/pattern basis when infrastructure IOCs surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Once C2 domains/IPs are confirmed for BusySnake, alert on connections from non-EDR, non-proxy-aware processes to those addresses. Flag encrypted HTTP/HTTPS POST requests from processes in Program Files or temp directories.

suggestion.title: Armored Likho Campaign—Government & Power Sector Lateral Movement Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Article specifically mentions targeting government agencies and power sector operators. Pipeline extracted no tactical patterns for these verticals. Should detect reconnaissance/lateral movement common in critical-infrastructure campaigns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: In gov/energy networks, monitor for enumeration of network shares (net view, dir \\host\c$), group policy updates, and lateral RDP/WinRM connections from single-user workstations or service accounts post-stealer compromise.

suggestion.title: Defense Evasion—Armored Likho Obfuscation & Code Armoring
suggestion.rationale: Actor name 'Armored Likho' implies code obfuscation/packing. Article should discuss evasion techniques. Pipeline extracted zero defense-evasion techniques despite this naming convention.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag process hollowing, import table erasure, or high entropy sections in PE binaries associated with BusySnake. Alert on reflective DLL injection or VirtualAlloc→WriteProcessMemory→CreateRemoteThread sequences.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Vulnerable Instance Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly recommends 'asset-exposure hunt' for 'Adobe ColdFusion Path Traversal' but pipeline generated zero UCs. Baseline detection of ColdFusion services running vulnerable versions is mandatory for a CISA KEV asset-exposure response.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify HTTP/HTTPS services on ColdFusion ports (8500, 8501, 80, 443) returning ColdFusion signature strings (Server headers, CFID/CFTOKEN cookies, /cfusion or /CFIDE paths). Cross-reference with vulnerability scanner for versions below CVE-2026-48282 patch date.

suggestion.title: Path Traversal Exploitation Against ColdFusion
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'path traversal vulnerability...could lead to arbitrary code execution' but pipeline did not generate HTTP anomaly UCs for exploitation attempts. Traversal pattern matching is critical given active KEV exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP requests to ColdFusion endpoints containing path traversal encodings (../, %2e%2e, %252e, ..../, unicode escapes, backslash variants) attempting to escape application context and access sensitive files.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Process Execution from ColdFusion
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability leads to 'arbitrary code execution in the context of the current user'—a clear RCE outcome—but pipeline did not surface process-execution detection rules. Post-exploitation process spawn is the highest-fidelity signal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when parent process is ColdFusion JVM (cfusion.exe, jrun.exe, java.exe with ColdFusion args) spawning shell interpreters (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, /bin/bash, /bin/sh) or network utilities, especially with outbound connections or file write operations.

suggestion.title: External Reconnaissance of ColdFusion Admin Interfaces
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'public-facing application' exploitation and CISA KEV context implies external threat actors. Pipeline missed UC for detecting external HTTP requests probing ColdFusion admin/management paths.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP requests from non-corporate IP ranges targeting ColdFusion admin endpoints (/cfusionmx/, /administrator/, /CFIDE/, /webtop/) or known probe URIs with 401/403/500 responses indicating discovery or vulnerability scanning.

suggestion.title: Anomalous File Access from ColdFusion Process
suggestion.rationale: Path traversal necessarily involves file enumeration and unauthorized file access; article does not mention file-system hunts but RCE exploitation implies out-of-scope file reads. File-access detection is a post-exploitation signal pipeline omitted.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor file-access events from ColdFusion processes reading files outside the application directory (e.g., C:\Windows\system32, /etc/passwd, web-root parent directories, registry hives).

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48282 Asset Exposure Scan
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly directs 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' using template substitution with CVE-2026-48282. Pipeline ignored this instruction entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner and asset inventory for Adobe ColdFusion instances matching CVE-2026-48282 vulnerable version ranges. Cross-reference patch status against federal due date 2026-07-10. Flag unpatched public-facing ColdFusion instances as highest priority.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Path Traversal Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'path traversal vulnerability…could lead to arbitrary code execution.' Web and firewall logs are the primary detection surface for exploitation attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt HTTP requests to ColdFusion endpoints (*.cfm, *.cfml, *.cfc) for path traversal payloads: ../, ..\, %2e%2e, Unicode encodings, and requests targeting system paths (/windows/, /etc/, /system32/). Correlation with HTTP 200 after prior 403 responses indicates successful traversal.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Unexpected Child Process Creation
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'could lead to arbitrary code execution in the context of the current user.' Post-exploitation, ColdFusion runtime spawns cmd.exe, PowerShell, bash, or system utilities.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on ColdFusion service or cfml.exe process spawning cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash, sh, or system utilities (net.exe, whoami, ipconfig). Baseline known-good child processes (cfexecute tasks). High-severity if spawned with SYSTEM token or low-integrity execution context.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion File System Reconnaissance Post-Traversal
suggestion.rationale: Path traversal combined with code execution enables attackers to enumerate sensitive file systems. File audit and host integrity monitoring detect this discovery phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor ColdFusion process reading system-sensitive paths: /etc/passwd, /etc/shadow, /windows/system32/config, Program Files directories, credential stores. Flag reads outside configured web root or application sandbox. Correlate read+write patterns to detect persistence attempts.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Outbound Connection to Suspicious Destination
suggestion.rationale: Successful exploitation leads to reverse shells, C2 callbacks, or data exfiltration. Article emphasizes active wild exploitation; network egress is canonical post-compromise signal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline ColdFusion's legitimate external connections (vendor updates, licensed services, databases). Alert on connections to RFC1918 IPs not in your network, non-standard ports (4444, 5555, 8443, 9999), or known malicious/suspicious external IPs. High-severity if combined with process creation anomalies.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Path Traversal Pattern Detection (Access Logs)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'path traversal vulnerability' as attack vector. Path traversal is detected via ../../../ and encoded URL sequences in access logs—no UC generated despite this being primary exploitation fingerprint.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor ColdFusion web server access logs for HTTP requests containing ../ sequences or URL-encoded equivalents (%2e%2e, %252e). Flag sustained attempts against ColdFusion endpoints; establish baseline deviation alerting per application context.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Process Code Execution (Post-Exploitation)
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'could lead to arbitrary code execution in the context of the current user'—explicit RCE outcome. No UC for detection of spawned processes despite this being stated exploitation consequence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on child processes spawned by ColdFusion runtime (cf*.exe, java.exe w/ ColdFusion classpath). RCE typically manifests as cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or script interpreters executing with web service account permissions from non-standard parent process chain.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion File System Access Anomaly (Traversal to Unauthorized Paths)
suggestion.rationale: Path traversal to RCE requires reading/writing files outside application root. Article mentions this vector but no file-level UC generated for detecting unauthorized directory access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline legitimate file paths accessed by ColdFusion process; alert when cf*.exe or associated java process accesses System32, Program Files, sensitive config directories, or user home directories outside normal application operation.

suggestion.title: Vulnerability Scanner Match: CVE-2026-48282 (CISA KEV Asset Exposure)
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV catalog entry with federal patch deadline 2026-07-10 (published 2026-07-07). No asset-exposure UC generated despite this being the canonical hunt template referenced in article body.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner and asset management for instances of ColdFusion running vulnerable versions (cross-reference CVE-2026-48282 affected versions). Prioritize internet-facing instances. Cross-check patch dates to identify remediation lag past 2026-07-10 federal deadline.

suggestion.title: HTTP Error Spike (Exploitation Enumeration Fingerprint)
suggestion.rationale: Path traversal attempts produce characteristic 404/500 error patterns during reconnaissance/exploitation. Standard exploitation signature omitted from pipeline despite being deterministic outcome of stated attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline HTTP response code distribution per ColdFusion endpoint. Alert on sustained elevation of 4xx/5xx responses, particularly clustered around /admin, /cfusion, or parameter fuzzing indicators. Correlate with path traversal patterns (../../) for confidence.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Configuration/Credential File Access (Post-Exploitation Persistence)
suggestion.rationale: Path traversal to RCE often leads to reading ColdFusion configuration files (datasources, credentials) for lateral movement. Article does not exclude this attack phase but pipeline generated zero persistence/credential-access UCs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for ColdFusion process reading .cfm config files, neo-security.xml, datasources, or password hash files. Correlate with process execution timeline post-vulnerability window to identify post-exploitation reconnaissance.

suggestion.title: Detect ColdFusion Path Traversal Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'could lead to arbitrary code execution' via path traversal; this is the initial attack vector that should be detected at the application/web server layer.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP requests to ColdFusion endpoints containing path traversal sequences (../, ..\, URL-encoded variants) or suspicious file paths in query strings/POST bodies. Focus on public-facing ColdFusion instances. Alert on patterns attempting to access system directories or configuration files.

suggestion.title: Detect Arbitrary Code Execution from ColdFusion Process
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability leads to 'arbitrary code execution in the context of the current user'; monitor process execution spawned by the ColdFusion service.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected child processes spawned from ColdFusion application server processes (cfusion.exe, cfserver.exe variants). Establish baseline of normal ColdFusion-spawned processes and detect deviations, particularly shells or scripting interpreters (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash).

suggestion.title: Inventory and Monitor ColdFusion Asset Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article describes vulnerability in 'public-facing application' context; CISA KEV status means active exploitation is occurring against exposed instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan internal network for ColdFusion instances (fingerprint via server headers, known ports 8500/8501, ColdFusion error pages). Cross-reference against patch inventory for CVE-2026-48282 vulnerable versions. Identify any externally routable instances as immediate remediation priority given federal deadline of 2026-07-10.

suggestion.title: Monitor ColdFusion Application Logs for Path Traversal Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Article documents CVE-2026-48282 actively exploited in CISA KEV; ColdFusion application logs should be monitored for error patterns consistent with path traversal attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Parse ColdFusion application logs for file-not-found errors (404s) on unusual path attempts, security manager exceptions, or template errors involving directory traversal. Monitor for repeated 400/403 errors on ColdFusion-specific paths which may indicate reconnaissance or exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: Detect Lateral Movement via ColdFusion RCE Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Path traversal leading to arbitrary code execution typically serves as a foothold for further compromise; monitor for secondary exploitation patterns following initial ColdFusion compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: If a ColdFusion process is compromised via CVE-2026-48282, look for subsequent network connections to internal resources from the ColdFusion service account, credential harvesting, or new service installations. Correlate ColdFusion compromise indicators with downstream lateral movement events.

suggestion.title: Verify ColdFusion Patch Status Against CVE-2026-48282
suggestion.rationale: Article's federal remediation deadline is 2026-07-10; patch verification is the control that closes the vulnerability window for active exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query software inventory for Adobe ColdFusion installations; determine version and compare against Adobe security bulletin for CVE-2026-48282 patched versions. Flag any instance below minimum patched version as non-compliant. Cross-reference internet-facing assets for priority remediation.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Path Traversal Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'path traversal vulnerability' and KEV implies active exploitation; pipeline generated zero UCs despite explicit T1190 mapping in source material. Need detection for `../` and `..%2F` sequences in HTTP requests targeting `.cfm` endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to ColdFusion web servers for path traversal payloads (../../../, ..%2F patterns) in URI paths and parameters. Baseline normal directory traversal in legitimate application logic; flag requests attempting escape from expected directory trees.

suggestion.title: Exposed Adobe ColdFusion Asset Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' and 'patch lag is the silent killer'. Pipeline generated zero discovery/inventory UCs. Federal agencies required to remediate by 2026-07-10; enterprise SOCs need baseline inventory of ColdFusion instances before exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate vulnerability scanner results (Software: Adobe ColdFusion, any version) with network baselines to identify exposed instances. Flag instances running versions known vulnerable to CVE-2026-48282. Cross-correlate with web server logs showing HTTP traffic to ColdFusion endpoints.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Arbitrary Code Execution Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'could lead to arbitrary code execution in the context of the current user'. Pipeline mapped T1190 but generated zero execution-phase detections for what happens after path traversal succeeds.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor ColdFusion process (cfusion.exe, java.exe with ColdFusion parameters) for unexpected child processes, inline script execution (powershell.exe, cmd.exe), or file creation in unexpected directories. Alert on execution initiated from ColdFusion user context outside normal application behavior.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48282 Vulnerability Scanner Findings Correlation
suggestion.rationale: Article warns 'patch lag is the silent killer' and recommends correlating scanners with actual exploitation. Pipeline found zero IOCs linking scanner detections to active traffic or exploit signatures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify systems flagged by vulnerability scanners as running vulnerable ColdFusion versions (CVE-2026-48282). Correlate with HTTP logs to detect any inbound requests matching path traversal patterns. Prior to federal patch deadline 2026-07-10, flag all unpatched systems for immediate remediation.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Directory Traversal File Access
suggestion.rationale: Path traversal specifically targets file system access escape; article emphasizes 'arbitrary code execution' implying file reads/writes outside intended scope. Pipeline generated no file-system detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor ColdFusion process file access attempts outside legitimate application directories. Flag reads from sensitive system paths (/etc/, /var/, /windows/system32) or writes to unexpected executable locations initiated through web requests.

suggestion.title: YesWiki Formula Injection: Malicious eval() patterns in Bazar CalcField requests
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'unsafe execution vulnerability...before passing [formula] to PHP eval()' and cites 'Bazar form field calculator (CalcField.php)'. Pipeline failed to detect the actual formula injection vector; current UCs focus on post-RCE recon only.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Bazar/CalcField endpoints for payloads containing eval(), system(), passthru(), shell_exec(), exec() functions embedded in formula parameters. Inspect both GET/POST for parameter names like 'formula=', 'calc=', or 'expression='. High-fidelity pattern: formula parameter contains unbalanced parentheses, function calls, or PHP keywords.

suggestion.title: YesWiki ReDoS Attack: Regular Expression Denial of Service via formula crafting
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability is 'vulnerable to Regular Expression Denial of Service (ReDoS)' and pipeline's UC_1_5 attempts URL pattern matching but misses actual ReDoS indicators: excessive nested parentheses '((((((' and engine CPU spike correlation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on web server requests containing deeply nested parentheses (>8 levels) to YesWiki Bazar endpoints, correlated with CPU spikes or regex engine timeouts in PHP error logs. Look for patterns like '(((((((()))))))))' or repeated '.*' in formula parameters. Typical ReDoS payloads trigger 100%+ CPU for 5-30 seconds.

suggestion.title: YesWiki CalcField RCE: PHP eval() error patterns in error logs or syslog
suggestion.rationale: Article describes vulnerable eval() function but no detection leverages PHP error logs or system logs for parsing/eval/syntax errors that indicate exploitation attempts. Web logs miss failed exploit attempts; error logs capture them.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PHP error logs for 'Parse error', 'Syntax error', or 'Fatal error' messages originating from CalcField.php or yesw.php files. Correlate timing with web requests to Bazar endpoints. Successful RCE attempts may show no errors; failed/tuning attempts will. Also check for 'undefined function' errors referencing system(), passthru(), etc.

suggestion.title: YesWiki Webroot Reconnaissance: Directory enumeration targeting Bazar and tools/ paths
suggestion.rationale: Article describes post-RCE persistence writing .php to Bazar/tools directories (UC_1_4), but no detection for the reconnaissance phase that would precede it. Attackers must first discover writable directories. Article mentions 'Bazar webroot' specifically.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests with reconnaissance patterns: multiple 404s to paths like '/Bazar/', '/tools/', '/plugins/', '/images/bazar/' in short timeframes, or successful probes (200 responses) to uncommon YesWiki directories. Detect with-curl or with-python user agents scanning. PHP-FPM spawning 'find' or 'ls' to discover writable directories.

suggestion.title: YesWiki wakka.config.php Credential Exfiltration: Sensitive file read post-RCE
suggestion.rationale: Article lists 'Unsecured Credentials' (T1552.001) but UC_1_3 generic credential hunt misses YesWiki-specific config. Article mentions '.env' and config files; wakka.config.php is the canonical YesWiki config. Attackers reading this file indicates advanced understanding of the target.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any process spawned by php-fpm/apache reading wakka.config.php or calling file_get_contents('...wakka.config.php'), or HTTP requests retrieving config.php with response codes 200 or 500 (misconfigured exposure). Detect cat/grep/curl targeting the file. Also monitor for exfiltration: base64 encoding or compression of config data followed by DNS/HTTP egress.

suggestion.title: YesWiki Plugin or Extension Abuse: Bazar files writing unexpected PHP mime types
suggestion.rationale: UC_1_4 detects .php writes to Bazar, but article describes CalcField as part of 'Bazar form field' subsystem. Attackers may disguise payloads as legitimate .jpg/.txt then rename or upload .phtml/.phar to bypass simple extension checks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for files written to Bazar directories with executable or dangerous MIME types (.phtml, .phar, .php3, .php4, .php5, .inc) even if extension bypasses simple checks. Also detect file renames/moves where a benign file (e.g., image.jpg) is moved into Bazar/tools and then renamed to .php. Correlate with web requests to newly written files to confirm execution.

suggestion.title: YesWiki erasespamedcomments bulk page deletion – single POST with suppr[] array
suggestion.rationale: Article states action 'accepts a `suppr[]` array from `POST` and deletes every wiki page whose tag appears in that array' — implies attacker can delete many pages in one request. Pipeline detects individual POSTs but not the array cardinality or bulk deletion behavior.
log_sources: Web application logs with POST body inspection
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect POST requests to erasespamedcomments with suppr[] parameter containing more than 5 array elements. Correlate with HTTP 200 response followed by high-frequency page deletion events in wiki audit logs within 5 minutes. Flag if performed by non-admin user account.

suggestion.title: YesWiki page deletion by low-privilege write-access user
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'any user who has page write access' can trigger this — implies privilege escalation from write to delete. Pipeline detects the HTTP POST but not the authorization context (user privilege level).
log_sources: Web application firewall logs with user context
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate POST requests to erasespamedcomments with authentication logs showing the user account has only 'write' permission, not 'admin' or 'delete'. Flag if a write-access-only user performs page deletion operations, indicating unauthorized privilege escalation.

suggestion.title: YesWiki page deletion confirmation – HTTP POST followed by backend page-removed events
suggestion.rationale: Pipeline detects the HTTP exploit attempt but cannot confirm actual impact (pages deleted) without backend correlation. Article promises 'arbitrary page deletion' but detection should verify it occurred.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: For each POST to erasespamedcomments returning 200, check wiki backend logs within 30 seconds for page-deleted or page-removed events matching the suppr[] array tags. A successful exploit should show N pages deleted corresponding to array cardinality. Absence of backend deletion events suggests mitigation (e.g., authorization check) is in place.

suggestion.title: YesWiki erasespamedcomments exploitation from multiple sources (coordinated attack)
suggestion.rationale: Article describes a vulnerability; coordinated multi-source exploitation would indicate organized attack vs. isolated opportunism. Pipeline detects single-source POSTs but not distributed patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect erasespamedcomments POST requests with clean=yes + suppr[] from 3+ distinct source IPs or user accounts within a 10-minute window targeting the same wiki. Flag if requests originate from different geographic regions or ASNs, indicating coordinated exploitation.

suggestion.title: Malicious npm Package Installation - @injectivelabs/sdk-ts v1.20.21
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names compromised package version 1.20.21 published to npm; developers installing this version had systems compromised. Pipeline extracted zero IOCs despite this being the primary attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect installation or presence of @injectivelabs/sdk-ts package versions 1.20.21 in npm cache, lock files, or process runtime. Monitor package.json dependencies and npm install logs for this specific version range between June 8–9, 2026.

suggestion.title: SDK Wallet Key Generation Function Call - Credential Exfiltration Trigger
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'malware activates when developers use SDK functions that generate or import wallet keys'; this is the execution trigger. Pipeline missed detection of this behavioral pivot.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor JavaScript runtime for calls to @injectivelabs/sdk-ts key generation and import methods. Flag execution contexts where these functions are called, especially if followed by encoding or network I/O operations.

suggestion.title: Base64-Encoded Wallet Data Exfiltration via HTTP POST
suggestion.rationale: Article states malware 'encodes the data in base64' and sends via 'HTTP POST request to an Injective Labs public infrastructure endpoint'. Pipeline extracted no exfiltration detection use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP POST requests from developer workstations to Injective Labs infrastructure endpoints with base64-encoded payloads in request headers or body. Correlate with cryptocurrency wallet or private key generation activity in the same timeframe.

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify packages with direct dependencies on @injectivelabs/sdk-ts v1.20.21. Cross-reference npm lock files, shrinkwrap files, and dependency manifests to enumerate transitive exposure. Flag installations of dependent packages published between June 8–10, 2026.

suggestion.title: Wallet Mnemonic and Private Key Capture in Memory
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies malware captures 'full mnemonic seed phrase and private key'; article does not name memory-dump techniques but the data exfiltration implies in-memory extraction. Pipeline generated no credential-access detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor JavaScript runtime memory for patterns of mnemonic phrase strings (typically 12–24 English words) and private key hex strings (64-character sequences). Correlate memory reads with @injectivelabs/sdk-ts function execution and subsequent base64 encoding.

suggestion.title: Queued Exfiltration with Delayed Multi-Key Bundling
suggestion.rationale: Article states malware 'queued multiple keys and mnemonics for two seconds, bundled them in the HTTP request header, and sent them'; describes a batching evasion technique. Pipeline generated no behavioral detection for this distinct pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests originating from cryptocurrency wallet or trading applications with multiple base64 payloads bundled in a single POST request header. Flag timing patterns showing ~2-second batching delays between key capture and transmission.

suggestion.title: UAT-7810 Ruckus/ASUS Router Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'The group exploits known vulnerabilities in unpatched Ruckus and ASUS routers to deploy new tools' — clear attack vector that requires n-day monitoring.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ruckus and ASUS routers for HTTP requests to known vulnerability endpoints (CVEs for these models). Baseline: routers should have stable patch versions. Alert on unexpected POST requests or admin panel access from new source IPs.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Proxying Behavior on Edge Network Devices
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'ORB networks create a massive blind spot' and 'Monitor network traffic for unusual proxying behavior or unauthorized connections on devices that typically lack complex services.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag routers (Ruckus, ASUS, other edge devices) establishing tunneling connections to unusual external IPs, especially multi-hop patterns or high throughput on ports associated with proxy protocols (3128, 8080, 9090). Correlate with absence of corresponding user-initiated requests.

suggestion.title: LONGLEASH/DOGLEASH Backdoor Installation on Network Devices
suggestion.rationale: Article names 'the upgraded LONGLEASH and DOGLEASH backdoors' as the malware deployed post-exploitation. These are signatures for persistence detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for file paths/process names matching LONGLEASH or DOGLEASH patterns on routers and edge devices. Monitor firmware modification timestamps on Ruckus/ASUS devices post-exploitation. Correlate suspicious process execution with n-day exploit activity in the same window.

suggestion.title: Secondary APT Command-and-Control Routing Through ORB Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article states UAT-7810 'builds these covert networks to provide infrastructure for other APT groups to launch attacks.' Detection needed for downstream APT activity routed through compromised routers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline for router C2 patterns and test for known malware C2 domains/IPs being accessed *through* routers that have been identified as compromised or unpatched. Multi-hop routing to known APT infrastructure is the signal.

suggestion.title: Unpatched Router Inventory and Firmware Version Monitoring
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'defenders must ensure all edge devices, particularly Ruckus and ASUS routers, are fully patched' — foundational detection is knowing what's running.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate all Ruckus and ASUS routers on network via SNMP/HTTP admin panel polling and extract firmware versions. Flag any version matching known-vulnerable CVEs (article does not list specific CVEs in excerpt, but cross-reference vendor security bulletins). Alert on version drift or unexpected downgrades.

suggestion.title: Avalon Malware Framework Execution Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly names 'Avalon Malware Framework' as primary threat—pipeline should surface baseline detection for known loader/framework binaries or command-line signatures
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process execution with Avalon-associated filenames, command-line patterns, or unusual parent processes launching framework components. Detect process spawning chains consistent with loader-to-payload delivery.

suggestion.title: CrownX Ransomware Encryption Impact
suggestion.rationale: Article states framework 'packs CrownX Ransomware Capabilities'—detection must identify file encryption behavior and mass file modifications characteristic of ransomware payload
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for rapid, widespread file modification events with .crownx or similar extension markers. Detect encryption-pattern file access (high write volume, sequential directory traversal) across user home drives and network shares.

suggestion.title: Malware Framework C2 Beaconing
suggestion.rationale: Malware frameworks require command & control infrastructure—article describes Avalon framework capabilities implying active C2 operations not extracted in empty kill chain
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound connections to known Avalon/CrownX C2 endpoints. Detect periodic beaconing patterns, DNS queries for infrastructure, and connection attempts to ports/domains associated with ransomware command infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Pre-Encryption File System Discovery
suggestion.rationale: Ransomware frameworks enumerate filesystems before encryption to identify targets—foundational attack step absent from empty pipeline kill chain and use-case output
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid directory traversals and mass file/directory listing operations from suspicious process parents. Alert on discovery patterns followed shortly by write-heavy encryption activity across drives and network shares.

suggestion.title: Obfuscated PowerShell Payload Delivery
suggestion.rationale: Malware loaders typically obfuscate PowerShell for evasion during execution—expected defense-evasion technique not surfaced in empty kill-chain phases
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PowerShell processes with -EncodedCommand, Base64-encoded script blocks, or suspicious concatenation patterns. Alert on PowerShell spawning child processes with uncommon parent-child relationships or unusual working directories.

suggestion.title: Registry Persistence or Defense Bypass Configuration
suggestion.rationale: Malware frameworks establish persistence and disable mitigations via registry keys—persistence and privilege-escalation techniques not extracted from article
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor registry writes to Run/RunOnce keys, WinLogon hives, or UAC-bypass targets (Accessibility, AppInit_DLLs) from non-system processes. Alert on modifications to Windows Defender or security-software registry paths.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48282 Vulnerability Scanner Match
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes CVE-2026-48282 as the primary indicator and recommends substituting it into standard asset-exposure hunts. Pipeline failed to generate baseline vulnerability detection UC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any vulnerability scanner result flagging CVE-2026-48282 on ColdFusion instances. Cross-reference against patch management records to identify unpatched systems within the federal due-date window (2026-07-10).

suggestion.title: HTTP Path Traversal Attempts Against ColdFusion
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'path traversal vulnerability' as root cause. Pipeline failed to map this to HTTP request-level detection for ../ sequences in ColdFusion application paths.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests to ColdFusion endpoints containing path traversal sequences (../, ..\ or URL-encoded equivalents %2e%2e) in URI parameters or POST body. Correlate with 4xx/5xx responses or error messages indicating directory/file access outside intended scope.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Process Arbitrary Code Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'could lead to arbitrary code execution in the context of the current user.' Pipeline failed to generate post-exploitation detection for code execution within ColdFusion process context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag child processes spawned by ColdFusion executable (cfusion.exe, jrunx.exe) with unexpected parent-child relationships or anomalous command lines. Monitor for command shells (cmd.exe, powershell.exe) or reconnaissance tools invoked from ColdFusion process context.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Anomalous File Access Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Path traversal leading to RCE implies attacker gains file system access. Pipeline ignored file-level IOCs that would indicate successful post-exploitation activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect access to files/directories outside normal ColdFusion application paths from the ColdFusion process. Alert on creation/modification of .cfm or executable files in web-root or system directories by the ColdFusion process ID.

suggestion.title: Public-Facing ColdFusion Asset Discovery
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'exploit public-facing application' as the attack vector. Pipeline provided no asset-inventory UC to identify ColdFusion instances exposed to the internet.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory, WAF, DNS, and network scans for ColdFusion servers (ports 8500, 8501, 80, 443) with public internet exposure. Correlate with patch management to identify unpatched instances; prioritize for immediate remediation per CISA federal due-date (2026-07-10).

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Public-Facing Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Exploit Public-Facing Application' (T1190) and federal requirement to hunt for exposed assets. Article phrase: 'KEV implies active exploitation against exposed assets'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify ColdFusion instances listening on public-facing ports (8500, 8501, 8502, standard CF admin/debug ports). Baseline DCFM connectivity patterns, alert on externally-accessible CF admin consoles or non-hardened instances.

suggestion.title: Path Traversal Exploitation Attempts Against ColdFusion
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies 'path traversal vulnerability.' Article phrase: 'ColdFusion contains a path traversal vulnerability that could lead to arbitrary code execution'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP GET/POST requests to ColdFusion endpoints containing path traversal sequences: ../, ..\ , %2e%2e, unicode/double-encoded variants. Correlate with known ColdFusion CGI paths (e.g., /cfusion/*, /CFIDE/*, /admin*). Alert on successful responses (200/302) from admin/config endpoints via traversal payloads.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Process Execution Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article states exploitation results in 'arbitrary code execution in the context of the current user.' This describes command execution phase. Article phrase: 'arbitrary code execution in the context of the current user'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor child processes spawned from ColdFusion service accounts (SYSTEM, cfusion, jrun). Baseline normal CF runtime processes (cfusion.exe, jrun32.exe) and alert on anomalous children: cmd.exe, powershell.exe, whoami, net commands, or unexpected network tools (curl, wget, certutil) invoked by CF process.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Configuration/Sensitive Directory Access via Path Traversal
suggestion.rationale: Path traversal typically targets configuration files (CF Admin password hash, datasources.xml, db credentials). Article phrase: 'path traversal vulnerability' combined with severity (CRIT) implies credential/config theft risk.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on filesystem access to known-sensitive ColdFusion paths (cfusion-install-root/lib/neo-datasource.xml, registry HKLM\\Software\\Adobe\\ColdFusion, administrator password hash files) when accessed via web server logs containing traversal sequences. Monitor for repeated 404s transitioning to 200s on config paths.

Article phrase: 'Federal due-date dates also frequently match the timing your organisation will be asked about by auditors / regulators.' Patch lag detection is explicit recommendation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner for ColdFusion instances matching CVE-2026-48282 (affected versions pre-2026-Q3 security update). Verify patch installation date vs. federal due-date (2026-07-10). Alert on any unpatched or unscanned ColdFusion assets. Cross-reference with network exposure scans to identify instances reachable from internet.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Uninitialized Variable/Memory Errors (Path Traversal Exploitation Indicator)
suggestion.rationale: Path traversal vulnerabilities often generate 'file not found' or memory reference errors in application logs when exploit probes occur. Early detection before successful exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor ColdFusion exception logs for patterns: FileNotFoundException, PathTraversalException, or AccessDeniedException when triggered by HTTP requests with ../ or encoded traversal sequences. Spike in 400/403 errors from single source preceded by 200 on restricted paths indicates active probing.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48282: ColdFusion Path Traversal Exploitation Attempts

Alert on requests to known ColdFusion servlets combined with directory traversal syntax. Correlate with failed/successful access to sensitive files outside web root.

Alert on any scanning activity targeting ColdFusion before deadline passes.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48282: Path Traversal Access to Sensitive Files

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor ColdFusion application logs and web server logs for successful HTTP 200/206 responses following path traversal requests. Detect access patterns traversing outside intended directories (e.g., accessing web-inf, metadata files). Alert on file I/O events showing ColdFusion process accessing system files outside application directory.

suggestion.title: CISA KEV CVE-2026-48282: Vendor Update & Mitigation Check

Use advisory date (2026-07-07) as pivot: any exploitation attempts post-publication indicate unpatched systems or 0-day variant. Generate alert if exploitation detected on systems claiming to be patched.

suggestion.title: Detect arbitrary code execution in ColdFusion service context

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process creation by the ColdFusion service account (typically NETWORK SERVICE, LOCAL SYSTEM, or named cfusion user) spawning command shells (cmd.exe, powershell.exe) or scripting interpreters (cscript.exe, wscript.exe) with suspicious parent-child relationships. Baseline legitimate ColdFusion process trees to distinguish post-exploitation activity.

suggestion.title: Alert on ColdFusion vulnerable version detection or patch status

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate CVE-2026-48282 detections from vulnerability scanners against exposed ColdFusion instances. Query patch management systems for patch status by server/date. Generate compliance alerts for servers past the 2026-07-10 federal due date. Cross-reference with asset inventory to identify internet-facing ColdFusion deployments.

suggestion.title: Monitor for post-exploitation file access in ColdFusion directories
suggestion.rationale: Path traversal + RCE allows reading/writing arbitrary files 'in the context of the current user'; pipeline omitted file-system behavioral detection despite this being the primary impact vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unusual file operations by ColdFusion process: mass reads of config files (cfusion.ini, datasources.xml), creation of webroot-accessible shell files (.cfm, .jsp, .jspx), or access to system directories (C:\Windows\System32). Establish baseline file access patterns for legitimate ColdFusion operations to minimize false positives.

suggestion.title: Correlate ColdFusion admin console access with exploitation windows
suggestion.rationale: Path traversal may be exploitable via admin interface if exposed; article does not detail attack surface, but standard ColdFusion exploitation often targets admin panel (default port 8500). Pipeline produced no reconnaissance or lateral-movement detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for successful or repeated failed logins to ColdFusion Administrator console, especially from external IP ranges. Correlate with path-traversal IOCs in web logs. Alert if admin accounts are created or modified shortly after exploitation attempts. Require multi-factor authentication for admin access.

suggestion.title: Detect network callbacks from compromised ColdFusion instances

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for outbound HTTP/HTTPS/DNS from ColdFusion-server IPs to known C2 infrastructure, newly registered domains, or suspicious ASNs. Cross-reference with threat intel feeds (abuse.ch, Feodo, Cyber Threat Coalition). Alert on large data exfiltration over HTTP POST requests originating from ColdFusion process.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Process Code Execution (Post-Exploitation)

suggestion.title: Unexpected Process Execution from ColdFusion
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'could lead to arbitrary code execution in the context of the current user.' Post-exploitation detection must monitor process spawning from ColdFusion runtime (java.exe/cfusion.exe).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for child processes spawned by ColdFusion JVM process (parent: java.exe/cfusion.exe) with unusual characteristics: cmd.exe, powershell.exe, /bin/bash, or unexpected system utilities spawned with unusual command-line flags, encoding, or obfuscation. Establish baseline of legitimate ColdFusion subprocesses (e.g., cf_schedule) and alert on deviations.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Configuration File Access Post-Traversal
suggestion.rationale: Path traversal vulnerability enables attackers to read files outside intended scope. ColdFusion configuration files contain database credentials, API keys, and other sensitive data.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor file-read events initiated by ColdFusion process targeting: neo-datasource.xml, coldfusion.xml, registry paths containing CF configuration, or any access to files outside ColdFusion's intended application directory. Correlate failed path-traversal web requests with successful file access events.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Service Account Lateral Movement Post-RCE
suggestion.rationale: Once arbitrary code execution is achieved in ColdFusion service account context, attacker may pivot laterally. Service accounts often have broad network access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor network connections initiated by ColdFusion process to unusual destinations (non-application servers, administrative ports 3389/5985/445, lateral scanning patterns). Flag any outbound SMB, RDP, WinRM, or SSH connections from ColdFusion service account; these are high-probability lateral movement indicators post-RCE.

suggestion.title: Vulnerability Scanner Match — CVE-2026-48282
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly designates CVE-2026-48282 as the active IOC and instructs substitution into asset-exposure hunts: 'Substitute this CVE wherever the template references <CVE>: CVE-2026-48282'. Pipeline generated zero use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any vulnerability scanner detecting CVE-2026-48282 in ColdFusion instances. Flag findings as critical—federated due date is 2026-07-10, enforcing urgency. Verify patch status via direct product interrogation (version/build query) to bypass patch-lag blind spots. Correlate scanner findings with historical patch-failure patterns on same hosts.

suggestion.title: Path Traversal Attack Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'path traversal vulnerability that could lead to arbitrary code execution.' Core attack vector; no web-layer detection generated by pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests with path traversal sequences (../, ..\, %2e%2e%2f, unicode-encoded variants) targeting ColdFusion endpoints (/cfusion/, /administrator/, /CFIDE/). Baseline normal CF access patterns first. Flag 5+ traversal attempts from single source within 1-minute window. Monitor ColdFusion working-directory access logs for suspicious file reads outside normal baselines.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Process Execution Anomaly
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'could lead to arbitrary code execution in the context of the current user.' Execution phase entirely unmapped by pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected child processes spawned from ColdFusion runtime (java.exe, jrun.exe hosting CF engine). Flag spawning of cmd.exe, powershell.exe, wmic.exe, or binary-execution tools. Establish CF baseline first—many deployments legitimately spawn subprocesses. Alert on any execution with file I/O, network calls, or credential-harvesting arguments.

suggestion.title: Public-Facing ColdFusion Asset Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly directs use of asset-exposure hunt template for ColdFusion. Phrase: 'the canonical Splunk SPL and Defender KQL live once in [`../_TEMPLATES.md#asset-exposure`](../_TEMPLATES.md#asset-exposure)'. Pipeline generated zero asset-discovery use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query for ColdFusion HTTP headers (Server: Adobe ColdFusion, X-Powered-By: ColdFusion, CFID/CFTOKEN cookies). Scan for common CF paths (/cfusion/, /CFIDE/, /administrator/, /cf_scripts/). Flag any ColdFusion instances responding to external probes. Cross-reference with patch-status data from scanner to identify unpatched CVE-2026-48282 instances.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Web Server Error & Access Log Analysis
suggestion.rationale: Path traversal attempts generate diagnostic artifacts in web/application error logs (400/403 responses, unusual URI patterns, CF-specific error pages). Pipeline did not generate log-analysis detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for HTTP 400/403/404 clusters paired with path-traversal syntax in URI or User-Agent. Extract ColdFusion error pages (cfusion/cfexplorer.cfm errors, CFEXECUTE tag errors). Correlate timing/source IP with WAF/IDS alerts for path-traversal signatures. Flag temporal clusters suggesting scanning/exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: CISA KEV Patch Compliance — CVE-2026-48282 Due Date Tracking
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes: 'Federal due-date dates also frequently match the timing your organisation will be asked about by auditors / regulators' with federal remediation due 2026-07-10. No compliance-tracking use case generated.

Alert 24–48 hours before due date (2026-07-10) on any vulnerable instances. Maintain immutable audit log of remediation attempts, version changes, and patch validation dates for regulatory reporting.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48282 Path Traversal Exploitation Attempts

suggestion.title: Unpatched ColdFusion Inventory Mismatch

suggestion.title: Suspicious File Write Operations from ColdFusion Service

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48282 ColdFusion Path Traversal HTTP Exploitation

suggestion.title: Exposed ColdFusion Asset Inventory and Patch Gap Analysis

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation ColdFusion Process Execution

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for child processes spawned by ColdFusion JVM (java.exe running as cfusion context) launching cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or scripting interpreters. Baseline: legitimate ColdFusion does not spawn interactive shells. High-confidence RCE indicator.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Configuration File Access Following Path Traversal
suggestion.rationale: Path traversal vulnerability 'could lead to arbitrary code execution'—implies discovery/access to config files. Pipeline missed discovery-phase detection between exploitation and execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect file system access to ColdFusion directories (cfusionconfig/, cfusionruntime/) preceded by HTTP requests containing path traversal patterns. Look for sequential: HTTP 200 response with traversal payload → file read events on config paths → process creation.

suggestion.title: Vulnerability Scanner Confirmation of CVE-2026-48282
suggestion.rationale: Pipeline IOCs completely empty. CVE-2026-48282 is the concrete tracking identifier required for scan correlation and patch verification. Vulnerability manager query missing despite CISA KEV mandate.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability management platform for active findings tagged CVE-2026-48282. Cross-reference with patch management: systems with finding + no patch applied = federal deadline violation (due 2026-07-10). Prioritize external-facing assets.

suggestion.title: Adobe ColdFusion Path Traversal Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'path traversal vulnerability that could lead to arbitrary code execution.' Standard asset-exposure hunt is the intended detection per article's template reference; must detect HTTP requests with traversal patterns (../, ..\ , encoded variants) targeting known ColdFusion paths.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect inbound HTTP requests to ColdFusion endpoints (e.g., /admin, /cfusion, /CFIDE) containing path traversal payloads or known vulnerable parameter names. Correlate with vulnerability scanner UA strings to separate scans from true exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Process Spawning Shells Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'arbitrary code execution in the context of the current user'—successful path-traversal exploitation results in shell spawning or reverse shells. Detection for abnormal child processes from ColdFusion service accounts (cfusion.exe, java.exe with ColdFusion classpath).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or bash spawned from ColdFusion application processes, especially with suspicious command-line flags (e.g., -nop, -enc, curl/wget for staging). Flag connections to external IPs immediately after process spawn.

suggestion.title: Vulnerability Scanner Probing vs. Exploitation Triage
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'patch lag is the silent killer' and CISA KEV entry means active scanning will spike. Differentiate Nessus/Qualys/Rapid7 fingerprinting (expect 404 or service-banner responses) from actual exploitation (200 OKs with response bodies, successful file/directory enumeration).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate HTTP status codes and response sizes for ColdFusion path-traversal probes. Scanners fail gracefully (403/404); exploitation attempts succeed and exfil file contents or environment. Alert on HTTP 200 + file-read indicators (e.g., web.config, cfusion.ini contents in response body).

suggestion.title: ColdFusion File Write / Webshell Deployment
suggestion.rationale: Path traversal often chains into arbitrary file write; article's 'arbitrary code execution' implication includes uploading JSP/CFML webshells to accessible directories. Detect post-exploitation file operations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor ColdFusion application directories (wwwroot, CFIDE) for new or modified .jsp, .cfml, .cfm, .jspx files with recent timestamps. Correlate with HTTP POST/PUT requests to path-traversal-vulnerable endpoints within ±5 minutes.

suggestion.title: npm Package Installation with Typosquatted Rollup-Like Name
suggestion.rationale: Article states packages 'mimic Rollup Polyfills'—classic name-confusion supply-chain attack where malicious packages use names similar to legitimate libraries (@rollup/*, rollup-polyfill-*, etc.) to trick installation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on npm installs for package names that are character-adjacent to high-popularity bundler/polyfill packages (rollup, webpack, babel, etc.). Flag installations from newly-created publishers or accounts with no GitHub presence. Cross-reference against known typosquatting feeds.

suggestion.title: Process Spawned from node_modules Directory with Immediate External Network Connection
suggestion.rationale: Malicious npm code executes during installation or build to 'steal developer secrets'—requires spawned child processes that connect outbound to exfil data.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect processes spawned from paths matching */node_modules/* that establish TCP/UDP connections to external IPs within 5 seconds of process start. Flag connections to non-whitelisted or newly-registered IP blocks, especially those geolocalizing to APAC.

suggestion.title: Credential Storage Access from npm-Installed Process (SSH Keys, AWS Creds, NPM Tokens)
suggestion.rationale: Objective explicitly to 'steal developer secrets'—attacker targets ~/.ssh, ~/.aws, ~/.npmrc, .env, .git/config storage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor file-open and read operations targeting credential storage paths from processes under node_modules or invoked via npm scripts. Alert on any read of ~/.ssh/id_*, ~/.aws/credentials, ~/.npmrc, .git/config, or *.env files by unknown/unsigned npm packages within 30 seconds of installation.

suggestion.title: Data Exfiltration from Build Host to External C2 (Post-npm Install)
suggestion.rationale: Stolen secrets must reach attacker—expect outbound HTTP/DNS/encrypted traffic carrying source code, credentials, or environment data minutes after malicious npm package execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate suspicious npm package installation with elevated outbound traffic volume (>100 KB) to external IPs within 10 minutes. Flag DNS queries for newly-registered domains, subdomains of known C2 providers, or IPs registered within 30 days. Inspect DNS query names for base64/hex encoding patterns.

suggestion.title: npm Package Metadata Anomalies: Low-Reputation Publisher Uploading Rollup-Variant Package
suggestion.rationale: Attack vector requires publishing malicious code to npm registry—early-stage detection targets suspicious publisher accounts and package metadata inconsistencies with legitimate Rollup ecosystem.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on packages with names matching regex (rollup|@rollup).*[polyfill|plugin|bundler].* published by accounts with: <10 prior packages, no GitHub presence, registration within 7 days, or WHOIS infrastructure overlap with known DPRK C2 ranges.

suggestion.title: npm postinstall/preinstall Script Execution with Credential Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Article indicates code execution via 'npm packages'—attackers abuse lifecycle scripts (preinstall, postinstall, prepare) to enumerate and steal secrets before developers detect malware.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm lifecycle script execution (npm run postinstall, npm run preinstall) for child processes that invoke credential enumeration commands: find ~/.ssh, find ~/.aws, cat ~/.npmrc, env, printenv, or grep secrets. Flag any execution that reads .git/config or searches for *.env files.

suggestion.rationale: Article indicates targeting of government agencies and power sector—characteristic of spear-phishing or watering-hole campaigns. No UC for detecting delivery of BusySnake via malicious links/attachments to critical-sector organizations.
