suggestion.title: Detect exposed ColdFusion applications on internet-facing endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability exists on public-facing applications; 'even if scanners say not vulnerable because of patches, check across your fleet' implies reconnaissance for ColdFusion instances exposed to internet.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for HTTP/HTTPS traffic to port 80, 443, 8500 (ColdFusion default admin) with responses indicating ColdFusion (CFML error pages, CFID/CFTOKEN cookies, CF headers). Look for publicly routable IPs hosting ColdFusion via HTTP Client fingerprinting or certificate scanning.

suggestion.title: Detect path traversal attempts against ColdFusion web services
suggestion.rationale: The vulnerability is explicitly described as 'path traversal'; need detection for exploitation attempts. Article states CVE-2026-48282 should be matched against vulnerability scanner, implying active scanning/exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests containing path traversal payloads ('../', '..\\', '%2e%2e', encoded variants) or directory traversal attempts against known ColdFusion endpoints (.cfm, .cfc files). Check for requests probing for web-root, system directories, or configuration files (e.g., '../../../etc/passwd', '..\\windows\\win.ini').

suggestion.title: Detect arbitrary code execution via ColdFusion process spawning
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'could lead to arbitrary code execution in the context of the current user'; need to detect when this occurs post-exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor ColdFusion process (cfusion.exe, coldfusion.exe, cfmx) spawning child processes with suspicious attributes: system shells (cmd.exe, powershell.exe), network tools (curl, wget, certutil), or LOLBin execution. Flag execution outside ColdFusion's expected execution context, especially with unusual parent-child relationships.

suggestion.title: Vulnerability scanner confirmation of CVE-2026-48282 unpatched instances
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'CVE-2026-48282 — match against your vulnerability scanner' and emphasizes patch verification even if systems appear protected due to lag.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Aggregate vulnerability scanner output for CVE-2026-48282 findings. Flag any unpatched instances of Adobe ColdFusion (all versions; patch version TBD) reachable from network boundary. Cross-correlate with asset inventory to identify systems missing patches by federal deadline 2026-07-10.

suggestion.title: Detect post-exploitation discovery phase from ColdFusion execution context
suggestion.rationale: After arbitrary code execution, attacker will enumerate environment, files, services; need detections for lateral-movement reconnaissance from ColdFusion process lineage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After ColdFusion-spawned child process execution, detect follow-on commands: dir/ls, net view, tasklist, systeminfo, whoami, registry enumeration, or file-system discovery. Specifically monitor for commands accessing %SYSTEMROOT%, Program Files, or network shares executed from ColdFusion child processes.

suggestion.title: Monitor ColdFusion web server logs for POST to dynamic template processing endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Path traversal exploitation often involves uploading or injecting payloads into ColdFusion .cfm processing; web logs will show suspicious POST patterns before execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: In ColdFusion web logs, detect POST requests to .cfm or .cfc endpoints with unusual payload sizes, binary content, or encoded strings. Flag requests containing CFEXECUTE, cfhttp, cfobject tags or Java reflection patterns (java.lang.Runtime.exec) in query/form parameters; these indicate code-injection attempts.

suggestion.title: Detect installation of malicious Injective SDK package versions
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names @injectivelabs/sdk-ts v1.20.21 as malicious and v1.20.23 as clean remediation. Detection must distinguish compromised versions from legitimate. 'The attacker also published version 1.20.21 for another 17 packages associated with the project.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm install/yarn add/pnpm install commands or package-lock.json entries for @injectivelabs/sdk-ts versions <= 1.20.21 or version pinning of any of the 17 downstream compromised packages. Alert on presence of malicious versions in node_modules directory or dependency resolution logs.

suggestion.title: Detect cryptocurrency wallet private key and mnemonic exfiltration via HTTP
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies exact exfiltration behavior: 'captures the full mnemonic seed phrase and private key and encodes the data in base64' and 'exfiltrated via an HTTP POST request.' 'The malware did not immediately transmit stolen secrets, but instead queued multiple keys and mnemonics for two seconds, bundled them in the HTTP request header.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for HTTP POST requests from Node.js processes to Injective Labs infrastructure with base64-encoded patterns in request headers matching cryptographic key length/structure. Correlate with SDK wallet-key-generation function calls in source code or memory patterns. Alert on suspicious 2-second batch timing between key capture and transmission.

suggestion.title: Detect supply-chain repository compromise via unauthorized npm package publication
suggestion.rationale: Article describes GitHub account compromise: 'The attacker compromised a GitHub account belonging to a legitimate project contributor and made the first suspicious commits on June 8, publishing the malicious version of the package shortly afterward.' This is T1195.001 (Supply Chain: Compromise Software Repository).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub account activity for anomalous commits or releases from legitimate contributors during off-hours or unusual geolocation. Correlate with npm publish events within minutes of Git commits. Alert when a single contributor account publishes updates to 17+ related packages in a short window (article: '17 packages associated with the project').

suggestion.title: Detect SDK function calls that trigger wallet key exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article notes conditional malware activation: 'The malware activates when the developers use SDK functions that generate or import wallet keys, rather than upon installation.' This runtime trigger is key to detection. 'Once those functions are called, the malware captures the full mnemonic seed phrase and private key.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Node.js runtime for Injective SDK function calls (generateWallet, importPrivateKey, getMnemonic) followed within milliseconds by credential data (regex: mnemonic phrases 12-24 words, private keys hex format) being read from memory or process handles. Correlate with HTTP exfiltration events to flag as malware activation.

suggestion.title: Detect transitive dependency chain injection of compromised npm packages
suggestion.rationale: Article highlights cascading supply-chain exposure: 'The package has 87 direct dependencies on npm and very likely multiple additional transitive dependencies. A report from Ox Security warns that the 87 dependent packages had a cumulative download count of a little over 112,000.' Downstream packages inherit the malware without direct installation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Analyze dependency trees for any package that directly or transitively requires @injectivelabs/sdk-ts v1.20.21. Flag projects using any of the 87 direct dependents (or their consumers) as potentially compromised even if they did not explicitly install the malicious SDK. Cross-reference with npm audit and lockfile package versions.

suggestion.title: Detect deprecated but still-available malicious npm package artifacts
suggestion.rationale: Article notes incomplete remediation: 'Socket says the malicious version of the package was downloaded 310 times before it was deprecated, not removed, and the malicious GitHub release artifacts are still available.' This allows continued exploitation post-disclosure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm registry for packages marked 'deprecated' but still downloadable, and correlate with historical malicious version numbers. Alert on npm install attempts of deprecated malicious versions or on cached installs from old lockfiles. Scan GitHub releases for artifacts still hosted after version revert/revoke.

suggestion.title: Ruckus/ASUS Router Exploitation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states UAT-7810 'exploits known vulnerabilities in unpatched Ruckus and ASUS routers' to deploy LONGLEASH/DOGLEASH. Pipeline extracted no initial-access signals despite defenders being told 'ensure all edge devices, particularly Ruckus and ASUS routers, are fully patched.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP POST/GET requests to Ruckus (22.3.x, 22.2.x, etc.) and ASUS router admin panels containing known exploitation payloads or unusual binary uploads. Correlate with failed SSH/Telnet attempts. Baseline: legitimate firmware update traffic from known admin IPs.

suggestion.title: LONGLEASH/DOGLEASH Backdoor Deployment and Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article names 'upgraded LONGLEASH and DOGLEASH backdoors' as the primary persistence mechanism. No detection use case generated. Article states tools are 'multi-platform'—need file-based and network-based signatures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect LONGLEASH/DOGLEASH file writes to /etc or /usr/sbin on Linux; detect process execution spawning outbound TLS connections to non-whitelisted C2 ranges from router processes. Signature: custom malware exhibiting multi-platform binary format (ELF, Mach-O, PE). Note: article states tools are 'sophisticated' and 'highly resilient'—expect encryption and evasion.

suggestion.title: ORB Network Detection via Proxy Chain Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Core attack infrastructure: 'ORB networks create a massive blind spot... allow secondary threat actors to mask their origins and route malicious traffic through seemingly innocuous nodes.' Article specifically states 'Monitor network traffic for unusual proxying behavior or unauthorized connections on devices that typically lack complex services.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify relay patterns: router → router → external. Detect CONNECT tunneling or SOCKS proxy traffic on TCP/443 from devices (Ruckus, ASUS) that never historically initiated outbound proxying. Cross-reference destination IPs against secondary compromised devices in same network. Expected: decentralized, low-volume C2 to evade perimeter sensors.

suggestion.title: Malware Hash Correlation (Talos Telemetry IOCs)
suggestion.rationale: Article provides 4 SHA256 hashes with Talos rep scores and detection names (Win.Worm.Coinminer, Win.Tool.Procpatcher, W32.HEUR:Attribute, PUA.Win.Tool.Kmsactivator). Pipeline extracted zero. These are corroborated telemetry, not speculative.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Block/alert on SHA256 file creations: 9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507, 621c6d42409e8aa423684827b4375a35684c71c600f2dd9101f235e8ec633488, 9896a6fcb9bb5ac1ec5297b4a65be3f647589adf7c37b45f3f7466decd6a4a7f, afc8a00883a4ea07df2dc1d4ed02f8a23b35c9456413b438a2d9ce3ae5076638. Baseline: monitor for name collisions (VID001.exe, SECOH-QAD.exe, sample.exe are masquerade targets).

suggestion.title: UAT-7810 Infrastructure Reconnaissance and Build-Out
suggestion.rationale: Article states UAT-7810 'builds these covert networks to provide infrastructure for other APT groups to launch attacks.' This is infrastructure-as-a-service reconnaissance—requires detection of reconnaissance queries, domain registrations, and IP assignments tied to ORB nodes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for bulk registrations of new domains resolving to router-class IP ranges (RFC 1918 + edge-facing IPs). Detect ASN/BGP changes for known UAT-7810 infrastructure. Correlate with historical C2 sinkhole/takedown data to identify resurrected infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Avalon Framework Malware Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly names Avalon as a malware framework; pipeline generated zero execution-stage detections despite critical severity
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect execution chains for Avalon loader/dropper: monitor for suspicious process spawning (PowerShell, CMD, msiexec, regsvcs) with encoded payloads or file-less execution patterns. Baseline: unsigned binaries, parent-child anomalies (explorer→powershell→calc), or processes from temp/AppData directories executing with network activity.

suggestion.title: CrownX Ransomware Encryption and File Destruction
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'CrownX Ransomware Capabilities' in title but pipeline extracted zero use cases for mass encryption activity—core impact behavior of ransomware
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag rapid, high-volume file modification events across user directories (.docx, .xlsx, .pdf, .jpg → .encrypted, .locked, etc.). Correlate with vssadmin/wbadmin execution (shadow copy deletion) and service stop commands. Alert on spikes in file I/O from suspicious processes and simultaneous ransom note (.txt, .html) creation.

suggestion.title: Avalon Persistence via Scheduled Tasks or Registry
suggestion.rationale: Framework architecture implies multi-stage payload with persistence; article lacks detail but no detection use cases were generated for persistence phase
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for scheduled task creation (Task Scheduler, schtasks.exe) with suspicious binary paths, system privilege execution, or boot-time triggers. Flag registry Run/RunOnce key modifications in HKLM and HKCU. Detect WMI event consumer subscriptions and startup folder modifications by non-admin processes.

suggestion.title: Defense Evasion: Security Tool Disablement
suggestion.rationale: Typical ransomware frameworks disable antivirus and backup utilities before encryption; article title emphasizes framework but zero defense-evasion detections exist
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect disabling of Windows Defender via registry (DisableRealtimeMonitoring, DisableBehaviorMonitoring), firewall rule deletion (netsh advfirewall reset), or Group Policy modification. Flag execution of sc.exe/net.exe to stop security services (WinDefend, MsSense, MsMpEngine). Monitor for deletion of event logs or tampering with audit policies.

suggestion.title: CrownX Ransomware Note Deployment
suggestion.rationale: Ransomware payload creates victim-facing ransom notes; article does not detail but is standard final-stage behavior absent from pipeline use cases
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for file creation events with ransom-note naming patterns (RESTORE_FILES.txt, RECOVERY_KEY.html, UNLOCK_YOUR_FILES.bmp, RANSOM.txt) in user directories and root paths. Flag files containing keywords: 'bitcoin', 'wallet', 'decrypt', 'contact us', 'payment', 'recovery key'. Correlate with mass encryption file events.

suggestion.title: Avalon Lateral Movement via Admin Shares or RDP
suggestion.rationale: Ransomware frameworks typically propagate across networks; article framework designation implies lateral capability but pipeline generated no lateral-movement use cases
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect RDP connection spikes, admin share enumeration (\\target\c$), or remote tool execution (psexec, wmic, smbexec, impacket). Flag unusual outbound RDP from non-user machines and lateral movement patterns: single source → multiple internal targets over SMB/RDP with Avalon/CrownX process execution correlation.

suggestion.title: Asset-Exposure Hunt: Vulnerable ColdFusion Instances (CVE-2026-48282)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly prescribes 'Standard asset-exposure hunt — the canonical Splunk SPL and Defender KQL live once in [`../_TEMPLATES.md#asset-exposure`](../_TEMPLATES.md#asset-exposure). Substitute this CVE wherever the template references `<CVE>`: CVE-2026-48282'. Pipeline generated nothing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify unpatched ColdFusion instances vulnerable to CVE-2026-48282 via vulnerability scanner output and network asset inventory. Correlate with web server exposure (public-facing endpoints). Alert if scanner detects CVE match without corresponding remediation ticket.

suggestion.title: Path Traversal Attack Attempts Against ColdFusion Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'path traversal vulnerability' without detailing exploitation patterns. Standard exploitation attempts should be hunted in web access logs before code execution occurs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for path traversal payloads (../, ..\, %2e%2e, unicode variants) in HTTP requests targeting known ColdFusion endpoints. Focus on access logs for CFM/CFML script execution. Flag requests with non-200/302 responses indicating handler errors or successful traversal.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Code Execution from ColdFusion Process Context
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'could lead to arbitrary code execution in the context of the current user'—execution phase missing from empty kill chain. Detection should cover spawned child processes from ColdFusion runtime.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unusual child process spawns from ColdFusion runtime (cfusion.exe, coldfusion.exe) especially cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or unusual binaries. Correlate with web request timestamps and path traversal attempts. Flag network connections from ColdFusion process to external C2.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Web Shell Creation Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Path traversal + code execution enables web shell placement; article implies execution capability but pipeline missed detection for post-exploit persistence via file writes to web directories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for suspicious file creation in ColdFusion web root (CF_ROOT, wwwroot) with CFM/CFML extensions following path traversal attempts. Alert on .cfm/.cfml/.cfmx files created from non-standard paths or by ColdFusion process writing unexpected file types to web-accessible directories.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48282 Patch Compliance Baseline
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'patch lag is the silent killer' and federal due-date 2026-07-10; compliance drift hunting is essential for CISA KEV entries but absent from pipeline output.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of all ColdFusion deployments and their patch status post-due-date. Alert on instances still missing patch or security update for CVE-2026-48282 after 2026-07-10. Cross-reference with exposure scan to prioritize instances reachable from internet.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion CVE-2026-48282 Asset-Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'Standard asset-exposure hunt — the canonical Splunk SPL and Defender KQL live once in [`../_TEMPLATES.md#asset-exposure`]. Substitute this CVE wherever the template references `<CVE>`: CVE-2026-48282'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate exposed ColdFusion instances reachable from untrusted networks; prioritize instances with patch lag vs. CVE-2026-48282 remediation deadline 2026-07-10 (coincident with CISA federal enforcement date).

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Path Traversal Exploitation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'path traversal vulnerability' as exploitation vector. Detection should identify malicious path-traversal payloads (%2e%2e, ../, encoded variants) before code execution succeeds.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP requests to ColdFusion endpoints containing directory traversal sequences targeting sensitive paths (cfusion config, source templates, OS directories).

suggestion.title: ColdFusion CVE-2026-48282 Arbitrary Code Execution Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability 'could lead to arbitrary code execution in the context of the current user'. Post-exploitation detection critical for incident response.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected process spawning by ColdFusion/CFML service accounts (cfusion.exe, cfserver.exe children), particularly cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or other execution engines spawned mid-request.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion CVE-2026-48282 Scanner Match
suggestion.rationale: Article mandates: 'CVE: `CVE-2026-48282` — match against your vulnerability scanner.' Pipeline extracted no IOCs and generated no scanner-based detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on vulnerability scanner reports identifying CVE-2026-48282 on any ColdFusion instance. Correlate with patch inventory; prioritize remediation by federal deadline 2026-07-10.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Public-Facing Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'T1190 — Exploit Public-Facing Application (KEV implies active exploitation against exposed assets)'. Pipeline did not generate asset-exposure use case despite template guidance in article body.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate all ColdFusion instances with external IP binding or published DNS. Verify patching status. Cross-reference with exploitation attempts in proxy/WAF logs to identify probable targets.

suggestion.title: HTTP Path Traversal Against ColdFusion
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies core vulnerability: 'path traversal vulnerability that could lead to arbitrary code execution'. Pipeline did not map exploitation technique to HTTP request patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect GET/POST requests to ColdFusion with path traversal sequences (../, %2e%2e/, ..\). Flag attempts to escape web root toward system directories (../../etc/passwd, ../../../windows/system32).

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Arbitrary Code Execution Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerability 'could lead to arbitrary code execution in the context of the current user'. Pipeline did not generate execution-phase detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor ColdFusion process context (cfusion.exe, jvm.exe with CF identity) for unexpected child processes: cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or suspicious scripts. Alert on file writes to system/privileged directories from CF user.

suggestion.title: Patch Status Compliance for Federal Deadline
suggestion.rationale: Article warns 'patch lag is the silent killer' and sets mandatory federal due date 2026-07-10. Pipeline did not flag remediation deadline tracking.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inventory unpatched ColdFusion instances by remediation window (critical: before 2026-07-10). Cross-verify scanner findings against patch records; identify deployment lag or scan blind spots.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Asset Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'KEV implies active exploitation against exposed assets.' First-order detection is locating ColdFusion instances reachable from untrusted networks, per the asset-exposure template referenced in the article body.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify inbound connections to ColdFusion default ports (8500, 8501) or HTTP/HTTPS traffic to .cfm endpoints from external subnets. Cross-reference with asset inventory to prioritize exposed instances for immediate CVE-2026-48282 patch validation.

suggestion.title: Path Traversal HTTP Payloads (ColdFusion)
suggestion.rationale: Article specifically names 'path traversal vulnerability.' Detection hypothesis must hunt for exploitation attempts: encoded traversal sequences (../, .., %2e%2e) in HTTP requests to ColdFusion handlers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP requests to ColdFusion endpoints containing path-traversal patterns: multiple ../ or ..\ sequences, encoded dot-slash variants (%2e%2e), or requests targeting WEB-INF, system paths (/windows, /etc). Correlate with timestamp and source IP to identify attack campaigns.

suggestion.title: Code Execution from ColdFusion Context
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'could lead to arbitrary code execution in the context of the current user.' Post-exploitation detection must monitor process spawn from ColdFusion process after successful exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on cmd.exe, powershell.exe, wscript.exe, or reverse-shell processes spawned by cfusion.exe or Java ColdFusion runtime. Correlate with preceding HTTP path-traversal requests. Monitor for unusual privilege elevation or network connections from ColdFusion process context.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Patch Lag vs. Scan Results (Deadline: 2026-07-10)
suggestion.rationale: Article warns 'patch lag is the silent killer' and specifies federal due date 2026-07-10. Detection must identify systems claiming patch coverage but flagged as vulnerable by scanners, or systems still unpatched past deadline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference CVE-2026-48282 scanner detections against patch-management records. Identify systems past 2026-07-10 deadline still showing as vulnerable. Flag mismatch scenarios (patch deployed but vulnerability persists—indicates bypassable patch or configuration drift).

suggestion.title: Anomalous File Access from ColdFusion Process
suggestion.rationale: Path traversal exploits inherently perform file I/O outside the application root. Detection should surface file-access attempts from ColdFusion process to system-sensitive paths (e.g., /etc/passwd, C:\Windows\System32 configs).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor file open/read events from ColdFusion application processes accessing paths outside the application directory tree. Correlate with HTTP requests containing traversal payloads. Flag sequences suggesting enumeration of sensitive configuration or system files.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48282 Exploitation via Path Traversal
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'path traversal vulnerability that could lead to arbitrary code execution' against ColdFusion, with active exploitation confirmed by CISA KEV status. Pipeline omitted any detection for malicious path traversal patterns or file access anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor ColdFusion application logs and reverse-proxy access logs for path traversal payloads (../, ..\, encoded variants) targeting administrative or configuration endpoints. Flag requests with 200/201 responses following path traversal patterns indicating successful exploitation.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Process Code Execution Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'could lead to arbitrary code execution in the context of the current user.' Pipeline failed to create detection for child processes spawned by ColdFusion engines following successful path traversal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on child processes spawned by ColdFusion service accounts (cfusion.exe, java.exe running ColdFusion runtime) where parent initiated within 5 seconds of a path traversal web request. Focus on non-standard interpreters (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash) spawned from application context.

suggestion.title: Unpatched ColdFusion Asset Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article prescribes 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' using template substitution with CVE-2026-48282 and federal remediation deadline 2026-07-10. Pipeline did not materialize any asset inventory query despite explicit guidance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset database or vulnerability scanner for ColdFusion installations with versions prior to patch date. Cross-reference with network exposure (public IPs, WAF logs) to identify which vulnerable instances face internet-facing exploitation risk; generate remediation priority by patch urgency (federal due-date 2026-07-10).

suggestion.title: ColdFusion File Traversal & Discovery Activity
suggestion.rationale: Path traversal inherently involves traversing directory trees; article does not mention defensive file-access telemetry. Detection gap for T1083 (File and Directory Discovery) phase of exploitation chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on rapid, non-sequential file-access attempts by ColdFusion processes reading outside standard application root (../../../, etc.). Baseline normal activity (scheduled jobs, legitimate admin access) and flag statistical anomalies in directory enumeration depth or frequency.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Public-Facing Application Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'asset-exposure hunt' and 'public-facing application' exploitation; detection should baseline internet-routable ColdFusion instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify ColdFusion servers listening on public IPs (TCP 80, 443, 8500) without firewall restriction. Correlate against vulnerability scan results for CVE-2026-48282.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Path Traversal Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'path traversal vulnerability'; detection should look for path-traversal payloads in HTTP requests to ColdFusion endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests containing path-traversal patterns (../, ..\, encoded variants) targeting ColdFusion administration or CF file paths (cfusion, cfide, wwwroot).

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Arbitrary Code Execution Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes vulnerability outcome as 'arbitrary code execution in context of current user'; detection should monitor for unexpected process execution or file write activity from ColdFusion process context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor ColdFusion process (cfusion.exe, jrun.exe) for spawning child processes, executing shell commands, or writing suspicious files outside normal application directories.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48282 Vulnerability Scanner Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'match against your vulnerability scanner' as the canonical hunt; detection integrates patch-compliance data.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any asset flagged as vulnerable to CVE-2026-48282 by Nessus, Qualys, or Tenable; prioritize 'not patched' status given federal due date (2026-07-10) and active KEV exploitation.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Administration Console Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Path traversal in ColdFusion typically targets admin endpoints; article context implies administrative access is the exploitation goal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect requests to ColdFusion admin URLs (/cfide/administrator, /CFIDE/componentutils/*, /cfusionportal) from untrusted sources or with path-traversal payloads.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion path traversal exploitation in web logs
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'path traversal vulnerability that could lead to arbitrary code execution'—this is the core attack vector and should trigger web application log inspection for traversal patterns (../, path encoding, etc.) targeting ColdFusion endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor web application and proxy logs for HTTP requests containing path traversal sequences (../, ..\, URL encoding variants) targeting ColdFusion installations or known vulnerable endpoints. Alert on 40x status codes followed by successful requests (probing → exploitation).

suggestion.title: Abnormal process spawning following ColdFusion HTTP requests
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'arbitrary code execution in the context of the current user' post-exploitation; detection must correlate suspicious web requests with unexpected child processes launched by the ColdFusion service.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal child processes spawned by ColdFusion (cfusion.exe, java.exe with known args). Alert on anomalous process creation immediately following HTTP requests identified as traversal attempts, especially cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or script interpreters.

suggestion.title: Public-facing ColdFusion asset discovery
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes this targets 'public-facing' applications; effective defense requires inventory of exposed ColdFusion instances before attackers enumerate them. Federal due date (2026-07-10) creates urgency.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan external-facing assets for ColdFusion services (port 8500, 8501, HTTP headers, .cfm/.cfc extensions). Cross-reference with patching records to identify unpatched instances. Flag as critical until patched or isolated.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48282 exploitation signature detection

suggestion.title: Post-exploitation data exfiltration from ColdFusion context

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate ColdFusion process file reads of sensitive paths (config files, database credentials, application source) with anomalous outbound connections or large data transfers post-exploitation. Baseline normal file access by ColdFusion service.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion configuration and admin access attempts post-exploitation

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP requests to /CFIDE/administrator, /admin, or other known ColdFusion admin paths following exploitation attempts. Alert on successful authentication to admin panel from new IP addresses or service accounts.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Vulnerable Instance Discovery
suggestion.rationale: Article references 'canonical Splunk SPL and Defender KQL live once in `../_TEMPLATES.md#asset-exposure`' and vulnerability scanner matching as primary hunt. Pipeline produced no use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner and asset management databases for ColdFusion instances matching CVE-2026-48282 severity/affected versions. Cross-correlate against web server access logs and network flows to identify externally-routable instances, then prioritize by last-patched date to surface patch-lag risk.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary Code Execution Post-Traversal
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'could lead to arbitrary code execution in the context of the current user.' Pipeline missed execution-phase detection despite clear impact statement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After path traversal attempt detected, hunt for process creation or code execution spawned by the ColdFusion application process (cf.exe, cfserver). Look for child processes with suspicious cmdline (cmd.exe, powershell, certutil) or file writes to unexpected locations, indicating post-exploitation command injection.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48282 Vulnerability Scanner Match
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly advises: 'Check against your vulnerability scanner' and 'patch lag is the silent killer.' Pipeline should generate basic scanner-matching use case for ColdFusion product inventory + version comparison.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query Tenable/Qualys/etc. for Adobe ColdFusion instances. Cross-reference installed version against Adobe CVE-2026-48282 patch baseline. Flag all unpatched or version-unknown instances. Escalate non-compliance past 2026-07-10 federal deadline.

suggestion.title: Adobe ColdFusion Internet-Exposed Asset Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Path traversal exploit only viable on 'public-facing application' (article phrase). Hunt must identify ColdFusion admin/runtime endpoints reachable from internet (certificate scanning, HTTP probes, reverse-DNS, shodan/censys patterns).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan external address space for ColdFusion signatures: SSL certs with cfusion/coldfusion strings, HTTP Server headers matching 'Adobe ColdFusion', JRun/ColdFusion admin panels on 8500/8501/80/443, cfusion/ URI patterns in webcrawl data. Cross-reference with internal asset inventory to identify over-exposed instances.

suggestion.title: Post-ColdFusion RCE Child Process Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'could lead to arbitrary code execution.' Execution phase must detect cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or bash spawned from ColdFusion runtime (cfusion.exe, java.exe/jrunX) with suspicious cmdline arguments.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on child processes spawned by cfusion.exe, java.exe (JRun process), or coldfusion.exe with shell interpreters + encoded/obfuscated command arguments. Baseline known ColdFusion process trees; any cmdline containing download/execution/reverse-shell indicators flagged as exploitation artifact.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Path Traversal Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Attack vector is path traversal (article phrase: 'path traversal vulnerability'). Hunt detects exploit attempts in HTTP logs—URL-encoded or literal ../ sequences targeting ColdFusion paths.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor web server/WAF logs for requests to *.cfm, *.cfc, /cfusion/, /cfadmin/ containing ../ (or %2e%2e, ..%5c, etc.) attempting to traverse to sensitive paths (/etc/passwd, windows/system32, source code directories). Alert on 200 responses to traversal attempts.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Admin/Debug Port Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: ColdFusion admin consoles (ports 8500/8501) are common RCE targets post-traversal. Hunt for port scans, connection attempts, or successful auth attempts to known vulnerable ports from untrusted networks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on failed/successful TCP connections to 8500, 8501, or cfusion admin URIs from external/untrusted sources. Correlate with 200 HTTP responses or admin-panel login attempts (authentication events in ColdFusion audit logs).

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Public Asset Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'public-facing application'—requires identification of exposed ColdFusion instances before exploitation can occur. Article recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' using template.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan public-facing infrastructure for HTTP Server response headers identifying Adobe ColdFusion version or default ColdFusion application paths (/cfusion, /CFIDE, .cfm file extensions). Correlate with asset inventory to find unpatched instances due by 2026-07-10.

suggestion.title: Path Traversal Attack Pattern Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'path traversal vulnerability' as the attack vector—requires detection of traversal payloads in HTTP requests targeting ColdFusion. This is the actual exploitation step.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor ColdFusion application HTTP request logs for path traversal patterns: ../, ..\ backslash escapes, %2e%2e URL encoding, or variations. Flag requests to ColdFusion endpoints (.cfm, .cfc) with traversal indicators in query parameters or POST bodies.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Process Execution from ColdFusion Service
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'arbitrary code execution in the context of the current user'—post-exploitation detection for code execution once path traversal is achieved. Directly maps to T1059 execution techniques.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unexpected child processes spawned by ColdFusion service account (typically IUSR, NETWORK SERVICE, or local CF service account). Baseline normal ColdFusion child processes and alert on anomalies: cmd.exe, powershell.exe, whoami, net.exe, or other reconnaissance/execution tools spawned post-exploitation.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion File Access via Path Traversal
suggestion.rationale: Path traversal enables access to files outside intended directory—detection of successful file reads to sensitive locations (web root parent directories, system files, config files with credentials).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor file access events from ColdFusion process accessing files outside its configured web root or accessing sensitive paths (../../../windows/win.ini, ../../../../etc/passwd, configuration files). Alert on successful reads of system files or config containing credentials.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion CVE-2026-48282 Vulnerability Scanner Match
suggestion.rationale: Article recommends 'CVE: CVE-2026-48282 — match against your vulnerability scanner' as primary detection mechanism. Scanners should flag vulnerable versions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate vulnerability scanner results for CVE-2026-48282 against public-facing assets. Identify ColdFusion instances (by version, application indicators, or banner grabbing) that match vulnerable version ranges. Prioritize by exposure and network location (DMZ, public-facing).

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Path Traversal Request Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'path traversal vulnerability'—must detect suspicious directory traversal patterns in ColdFusion application logs and HTTP requests.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor ColdFusion web requests for path traversal signatures (../, %2e%2e, directory escape sequences) in URL parameters and POST bodies. Flag requests with HTTP 40x responses following traversal attempts as exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable ColdFusion Instance Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article implies active exploitation—need to detect and inventory ColdFusion services and versions against CVE-2026-48282 to identify exposure before compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate asset inventory/vulnerability scan data to flag any ColdFusion instances. Monitor network for ColdFusion service fingerprints (port 8500, 8501, characteristic HTTP headers) and cross-reference against known vulnerable versions.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary Code Execution via ColdFusion Path Traversal
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'could lead to arbitrary code execution in the context of the current user'—must detect actual code execution post-exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor ColdFusion parent process (javaw.exe, java.exe) for unexpected child process spawning, script execution events, or command-line activity correlated with preceding path traversal HTTP requests.

suggestion.title: Web Server Access Log Exploitation Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Path traversal attempts will generate recognizable patterns in web server logs—'../config.xml' and similar filesystem navigation signatures indicate active exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Parse web server access logs for GET/POST requests containing encoded or literal path traversal sequences. Flag sequences of requests with 40x status codes followed by successful (200/302) responses as suspicious exploitation chains.

suggestion.title: Outbound Callback Detection Post-ColdFusion Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Arbitrary code execution context implies attacker can establish callbacks; article severity (critical, active wild exploitation) suggests C2 communication risk.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected outbound connections from ColdFusion process (java.exe parent) to non-whitelisted external IPs/domains. Alert on DNS queries from ColdFusion context or HTTP/HTTPS callbacks to unusual ports.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion CVE-2026-48282 Vulnerability Detection
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entry with known exploitation; article states federal patch due 2026-07-10 and emphasizes vulnerability scanner match. Pipeline must surface this as asset-exposure hunt substituting CVE ID.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on vulnerability scanner detections for CVE-2026-48282, or query asset inventory for ColdFusion product instances with version < patched release. Cross-reference against federal remediation due-date (2026-07-10) for compliance reporting.

suggestion.title: HTTP Path Traversal Attack Attempts Against ColdFusion
suggestion.rationale: Article core: 'path traversal vulnerability.' Web server logs should capture exploitation attempts via directory-traversal patterns targeting ColdFusion paths (e.g., /cfusion/, /../, ..\).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for HTTP requests containing path-traversal sequences (../, ..\ unicode variants) or directory escaping patterns in User-Agent or request path to known ColdFusion application directories. Correlate 400/403 responses with subsequent successful 200 responses indicating successful exploitation.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Process Anomalies Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'arbitrary code execution in the context of the current user.' After path traversal succeeds, RCE spawns unexpected child processes; look for jrun.exe or cfusion.exe parent spawning cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or file-write operations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when ColdFusion JVM process (jrun.exe, jrun32.exe, cfusion.exe) spawns interactive shells (cmd.exe, powershell.exe) or suspicious child processes (net.exe, whoami.exe). Baseline normal ColdFusion child processes (java compiler, update processes) to reduce noise.

suggestion.title: Suspicious File Operations in ColdFusion Web Directories
suggestion.rationale: Path traversal + RCE typically leads to file writes into web-accessible paths. Article's 'arbitrary code execution' implies ability to write web shells (.jsp, .cfml, .cfm) into webroot for persistence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for unexpected file creation in ColdFusion webroot (wwwroot, web-inf) with suspicious extensions (.jsp, .cfml, .cfm) created outside of normal deployment windows. Track file-write events from cfusion.exe or child processes into %PROGRAMFILES%\Adobe\Coldfusion\... or equivalent linux paths.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion HTTP 4xx/5xx Error Spike Detection
suggestion.rationale: Path traversal exploits often trigger 400/403 errors during reconnaissance; successful exploitation may follow with 200-status requests to non-existent resources. Article mentions 'public-facing application,' implying external attack surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline HTTP error rates for known ColdFusion servers. Alert on elevated 4xx/5xx error rates followed by successful 200 responses from same source IP within short time window, especially if requests contain path-traversal sequences or unusual query strings.

suggestion.title: Compliance: Federal Patch Due-Date Tracking for CVE-2026-48282
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Federal patch due: 2026-07-10.' CISA KEV items carry federal remediation mandates; SOC must track remediation status and compliance posture by due-date. Pipeline should have flagged the urgency.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query patch-management and asset-inventory systems for ColdFusion instances. Generate compliance report showing: (1) patched vs. unpatched counts, (2) systems remediated before federal due-date (2026-07-10), (3) any systems still vulnerable after due-date for escalation to compliance/legal teams.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary Code Execution in ColdFusion Process Context

Look for process command lines containing shell interpreters, script interpreters, or suspicious network calls originating from ColdFusion context post-exploitation.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48282 Exploitation Signature Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article references specific CVE. IDS/WAF/EDR rules for known payload patterns should exist in vendor advisories. Pipeline must map to signature-based detection for immediate exploitation alerts.

Cross-reference with network exposure scanning. Create alerting rule: if exposed + unpatched for CVE-2026-48282, escalate to critical priority.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48282 Vulnerability Detection

Alert on any systems matching this CVE signature, even if marked patched—patch lag is common in KEV exploits.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary Code Execution in ColdFusion Process Context

Flag unexpected interpreters (cmd.exe, PowerShell, bash) or network utilities (curl, wget, nc) launched from ColdFusion context with low-confidence parents.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Application Directory Traversal via File Access Logs
suggestion.rationale: Path traversal exploitation necessitates filesystem access outside intended application directories; no detection covers anomalous file access patterns from ColdFusion service account.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for file access events from ColdFusion service account (typically SYSTEM or named service account) accessing files outside the ColdFusion install directory or application root. Focus on access to sensitive directories (Windows\System32, program files outside ColdFusion, web root parent directories).

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Path Traversal Exploitation Attempts

suggestion.title: Arbitrary Code Execution from ColdFusion Service Context

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process creation where parent is ColdFusion service (cfusion.exe, java.exe running CF) spawning cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash, or uncommon binaries. Establish baseline of legitimate spawned processes (cf-scheduled tasks, file operations); flag deviations.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Instance Exposure Inventory

Correlate NetFlow/Zeek for internet-facing traffic to ColdFusion ports (8500, custom admin ports). Flag exposed CFML application roots or admin interfaces without network segmentation.

suggestion.title: Encoded/Obfuscated Path Traversal Variants in HTTP Requests
suggestion.rationale: Path traversal exploits use encoding to bypass WAF/IDS signatures. Article mentions 'path traversal' without specifying encoding; double-encoding, Unicode, and case variants are common evasions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for double-encoded traversal (%252e, %252f), mixed-case variants (..%252F), UTF-8 encoding (..%c0%ae), and null-byte injection (..%00). Correlate with file-access attempts (/etc/passwd, /windows/win.ini, web.config, ColdFusion registry hives).

suggestion.title: ColdFusion File Access Outside Application Directory
suggestion.rationale: Path traversal's end-goal is reading/writing files outside intended scope. File I/O from CF service to /etc, /windows/system32, or parent directories signals successful traversal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor file read/write initiated by cfusion.exe/java.exe processes to sensitive paths (../../../, /etc, /windows/system32, /boot, configuration files outside application root). Baseline legitimate CF file ops (library paths, temp dirs). Alert on anomalous access patterns.

suggestion.title: Compliance Audit: CVE-2026-48282 Patch Status by 2026-07-10
suggestion.rationale: Article mandates 'Federal patch due: 2026-07-10' + CISA KEV context = regulatory deadline. Patch-lag hunting is essential for compliance and reduces exploitability window.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query configuration management and patch-tracking systems for any ColdFusion instances below the patched version for CVE-2026-48282. Cross-reference scanner results against installed versions (scanners lag; reconcile). Report unpatched assets by location/owner/risk, prioritizing internet-facing instances. Tie to compliance audit trail for federal/regulatory response.

suggestion.title: Suspicious npm Postinstall Script Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article describes malicious npm packages mimicking legitimate polyfills; npm relies heavily on postinstall hooks for code execution during package installation. Phrase: 'npm Packages Mimic Rollup Polyfills to Steal Developer Secrets' implies code execution at install time.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect npm install operations that spawn child processes with suspicious command-line patterns (encoded payloads, curl/wget to external hosts, env-var exfiltration). Alert on postinstall scripts that reference unknown domains or pipe output to /dev/tcp.

suggestion.title: Environment Variable Exfiltration During Package Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article states packages target 'developer secrets'—API keys, tokens, and credentials typically stored in .env files or environment. Detection should focus on npm processes reading env vars.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect npm or node processes accessing .env files, env vars (process.env enumeration), or credential storage (SSH keys, .aws/credentials). Correlate with outbound network connections or file writes to suspicious locations.

suggestion.title: Typosquatted npm Package Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies packages 'mimic' legitimate Rollup polyfills—classic typosquatting. Detection should identify installs of packages with names similar to popular libraries but installed via exact or near-exact name matches.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference installed packages against a curated list of legitimate npm packages; flag installs of packages with Levenshtein distance ≤2 from known polyfills (rollup, polyfill, babel-*). Alert on first-time-seen package names with zero GitHub stars or recent creation dates.

suggestion.title: Minified/Obfuscated Code in npm Package Distributions
suggestion.rationale: Malicious npm packages typically hide malicious code. Article implies sophisticated obfuscation ('mimic' suggests code disguise). Detection should identify packages with obfuscated payloads during installation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inspect node_modules for scripts with high entropy, single-line encoding (base64, hex), or cryptographic operations in package.json scripts. Correlate with low code readability metrics (cyclomatic complexity, variable naming patterns).

suggestion.title: npm Package Network Egress to Suspicious Domains
suggestion.rationale: Stolen secrets must exfiltrate. Article implies C2 callback infrastructure for credential theft.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate npm install processes with outbound network connections (HTTP/HTTPS/DNS) to newly-registered or reputation-low domains. Alert on POST requests with encoded payloads or suspicious User-Agent strings during package installation windows.

suggestion.title: npm Registry Authentication Token Theft
suggestion.rationale: Developers often store npm auth tokens in .npmrc; stealing these allows attacker to publish malicious versions to legitimate packages or access private registries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect file reads of ~/.npmrc or environment variable access to NPM_TOKEN/NPM_AUTH_TOKEN during unexpected process execution. Monitor for subsequent npm publish or registry login commands from unusual IP/machine contexts.
