suggestion.title: SiYuan Renderer Process JavaScript Engine Spike Post-Panel Open
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'runs arbitrary JavaScript in the renderer when the victim opens the block-attribute panel' — the XSS payload execution in JavaScript engine is the critical execution phase. Detection of abnormal CPU/memory during this phase could catch exploitation before shell spawning.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate opening of SiYuan attribute-view panels (detected via window title tracking or user action events) with sudden CPU spike in SiYuan renderer process (sustained >50% single-thread or >200% multi-core for >2sec). XSS payloads with setTimeout/fetch loops will show measurable engine load. Requires event log injection of panel-open signal or behavioral profiling of benign panel interactions.

suggestion.title: SiYuan Process Accessing Local File System Post-Renderer XSS
suggestion.rationale: Article truncates at 'On Electron desktop the renderer …' but implies nodeIntegration-enabled code execution can access fs module. Detect file/registry access patterns unusual for normal SiYuan operation, occurring after activity on attribute-view panels.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag file or registry access initiated by SiYuan process (or its child processes) to unexpected locations: Program Files/Windows/System32, browser cache dirs, credential storage, after no file/registry access occurred in prior 60sec. Benign SiYuan operations are read-only against app directory; suspicious access is write-or-delete to OS-critical or credential paths.

suggestion.title: SiYuan Database Shared or Synchronized to Untrusted Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Attack requires victim to have malicious database open. Article does not specify if attacker compromises existing shared database or socially engineers victim to download one; detection of suspicious database sharing/sync events could block propagation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor SiYuan workspace directories (\data\, typically in AppData\Roaming or cloud sync roots) for file transfers to/from external cloud storage (OneDrive, Google Drive, Dropbox outside managed tenants), or for databases sent via email/messaging. Correlate with downloads of .sy or database backup files from external sources.

suggestion.title: Malicious Crate Code Execution via Download and Execute
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'A method within the exploration crate attempted to download and execute a payload from a remote site.' Direct evidence of T1059 + T1105; should generate detection for suspicious child processes spawning from Rust/Cargo toolchain with outbound network.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process creation where parent is Rust compiler, Cargo, or build-related process, with command line containing download utilities (curl, wget, powershell -Command) or execution patterns pointing to %TEMP% or /tmp staged files. Correlate with outbound network to non-package-registry hosts.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Compromise Detection - Malicious Crate Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes crate 'removed from crates.io for malicious code' — textbook T1195.001 (Compromised Software Dependencies). Pipeline missed supply chain as kill-chain phase entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cargo.toml modifications and crate installations for suspicious patterns: crates with zero prior version history, rapid publication-to-removal cycles, or crates flagged by security advisories. Cross-reference against known GHSA/Rustsec advisories within 24 hours of advisory publication.

suggestion.title: Outbound Network from Cargo/Build Process to Suspicious Domains
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'attempted to download...payload from a remote site' — explicitly describes C2 or payload fetch. Pipeline generated no execution/C2 detections despite this clear behavioral indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag outbound DNS/HTTP/HTTPS connections initiated by Rust toolchain processes (rustc, cargo, build scripts) to destinations outside known registries (crates.io, github.com, registry.rust-lang.org). Correlate with file creation in build cache directories.

suggestion.title: Temp Directory Staging and Execution from Package Build
suggestion.rationale: Download → execute pattern implies staging in temp. Article mentions crate has 'no evidence of actual usage' yet code was malicious, suggesting payload execution happened during install/build phase targeting developers' machines.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate file creation in %APPDATA%\cargo, .cargo/registry/cache, or /tmp with rapid subsequent process spawning from those paths. Flag if file timestamps and execution are within seconds and parent process chain includes Cargo.

suggestion.title: Registry Abuse - Rapid Crate Removal Signal
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'published on 2026-06-02, approximately 1 hour before removal' — extremely short crate lifespan combined with 'malicious code' reason is a registry abuse pattern T1195.001.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor package registry APIs (crates.io, cargo-index) for crates published then yanked/removed within 2 hours, especially if removal reason contains 'malicious', 'security', or 'suspicious'. Correlate with any downstream installations on monitored assets during the live window.

suggestion.title: Browser extension calling SiYuan admin API (127.0.0.1:6806 with /api/admin/ path)
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker extension 'can make fully authenticated admin API calls.' Specific API paths like /api/admin/*, /api/setting/*, /api/system/* should be monitored. No existing UC captures the actual exploit: extension-to-admin-endpoint. UC_8_4 only detects port 6806 connectivity, not the admin path traversal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor localhost:6806 HTTP requests from chrome/edge/brave processes for /api/admin*, /api/setting*, /api/system* URIs. Log the Referer/Origin header to detect chrome-extension:// schemes. Flag as suspicious if request succeeds (HTTP 200) without prior auth token setup.

suggestion.title: Extension probing localhost for SiYuan kernel service (port 6806 scanner)
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions extensions can 'discover' SiYuan running locally. Malicious or legitimate-compromised extensions may scan 127.0.0.1 for open ports. 'Combined with the default empty AccessAuthCode on desktop installs' suggests scanning for vulnerable config. No UC addresses reconnaissance phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect browser process (chrome, edge, brave) performing rapid sequential connections to 127.0.0.1 on different ports (e.g., 6806, 6805, 6807) or known app ports (5432, 3306, 27017). Baseline expected browser loopback connections; flag anomalies as service discovery attempts.

suggestion.title: SiYuan empty AccessAuthCode deployment (default unsafe config)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'default empty AccessAuthCode on desktop installs' enables the vulnerability. No UC detects config exposure. Should inventory SiYuan installations with disabled/empty auth. Phrase: 'unconditionally trusts all chrome-extension://'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate SiYuan config files (Linux: ~/.config/siyuan/, Windows: %APPDATA%/SiYuan/) for conf.json or settings with empty or absent AccessAuthCode field. Flag as misconfigured if kernel listens on 6806 and AccessAuthCode is null/empty/default.

suggestion.title: Extension reading/exfiltrating browser credentials via hijacked SiYuan API
suggestion.rationale: T1539 (Steal Web Session Cookie) and T1555.003 (Credentials from Web Browsers) are listed techniques, but no UC specifically detects an extension calling SiYuan API to *then* extract credentials. Article: extension gets admin access, implying it can invoke credential-gathering endpoints. This is execution of the actual exploit, not generic cookie-stealer.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate: (1) browser making requests to 127.0.0.1:6806 + admin API paths, followed by (2) file access to browser credential stores (Chrome User Data/Login Data, Edge, Firefox logins.sqlite). Timestamp correlation within minutes. Flag as credential exfil chain.

suggestion.title: Browser extension manifest declaring unsafe permissions (localhost, broad API scopes)
suggestion.rationale: Malicious extension must request permissions for local network access or run with broad scripting scope. Article mentions 'compromised legitimate extension via supply chain' — supply-chain indicators include suspicious permission escalation in manifest update. No UC monitors extension manifest changes or high-risk permissions.
log_sources: Browser extension manifests (registry or profile storage)
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor installed extension manifests for permissions like 'webRequest', 'webRequestBlocking', 'http://127.0.0.1/*', '<all_urls>', 'background', or 'nativeMessaging'. Flag manifest updates that add localhost-targeting permissions. Cross-reference with extension publisher reputation.

suggestion.title: Access tokens in HTTP 302 redirect Location header (CVE-2026-54072 exfiltration)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'appends access_token, id_token, and refresh_token as query parameters and issues a 302 redirect'. Pipeline missed the exfiltration mechanism — tokens in Location header is the smoking gun.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for HTTP 302 responses from /authorize endpoint where Location header contains URL-encoded or plaintext access_token, id_token, or refresh_token parameters. Token format: typically JWT (~500+ chars) or opaque strings. Correlate redirect_uri to threat-intel domain lists.

suggestion.title: Redirect URI validation bypass — wildcard or mismatch against AllowedOrigins (CVE-2026-54072 precursor)
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'accepts any redirect_uri without validating it against AllowedOrigins'. Root-cause detection should capture requests with redirect_uri that don't match registered origins. Requires application-level logging or WAF rules.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for /authorize requests where redirect_uri domain deviates from AllowedOrigins configuration. Flag mismatches, wildcard (*) patterns, or localhost/127.0.0.1 if not explicitly allowed. Escalate if combined with implicit-flow response_type.

suggestion.title: Attacker-controlled domain in redirect_uri — reputation & passive DNS check
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'attacker-controlled URL'. Requires domain reputation check against known malware/phishing domains. Pipeline produced no IOC output; reputation check is standard threat-intel enrichment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Extract redirect_uri domain from /authorize requests. Query against domain reputation services. Flag if domain has no WHOIS history, recent registration, no SSL cert, or known in phishing/malware databases. Correlate with source IP geolocation.

suggestion.title: Client_id enumeration via GraphQL introspection (CVE-2026-54072 reconnaissance)
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated attacker can obtain the required client_id from the public /graphql'. Reconnaissance phase where attacker discovers client_id needed for exploit. Pipeline's UC_9_3 is too vague; should detect repeated failed or successful meta queries from single source.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for repeated /graphql queries (threshold: >5 in 5min window) from same src targeting introspection or client metadata fields. Flag if src IP is not on internal allowlist and queries are unauthenticated. Correlate with follow-up /authorize requests to same dest from same src within 10 minutes.

suggestion.title: ALWAYS_PROTECTED JWT/CLI token validation bypass attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability requires 'JWT or CLI token' validation; attackers would probe for missing/invalid credentials. Article phrase: 'only validates JWT or CLI token.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Look for requests to /api/settings/database missing Authorization header or with malformed/expired JWT tokens. Correlate with subsequent successful requests from same source (possible retry after credential compromise). Baseline acceptable-token failure rate to surface anomalies.

suggestion.title: Database export response pattern matching (credentials/tokens in payload)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states export contains 'all credentials, API keys, OAuth tokens, and settings.' Detection should match response content not just endpoint. Article phrase: 'containing all credentials, API keys, OAuth tokens, and settings.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag GET responses to /api/settings/database with response body containing JSON keys matching credential patterns (password, oauth_token, api_key, bearer, secret, private_key). Correlate with bytes_out threshold to identify large exfiltration vs. small operational requests.

suggestion.title: Database configuration/auth endpoint modification post-import
suggestion.rationale: Successful POST import could overwrite authentication config, user permissions, or auth endpoints. Should detect downstream configuration changes. Article phrase: 'full database import (complete overwrite).'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate POST to /api/settings/database with subsequent config changes (OAuth endpoint redirection, user role changes, credential resets). Look for authentication service errors or config reload events within 5 minutes post-import.

suggestion.title: Export-then-import pattern (lateral movement / backup poisoning)
suggestion.rationale: Sophisticated attackers would export, modify locally, then reimport to inject malicious configs or steal credentials while avoiding detection. Article phrase: 'full database export' and 'import (complete overwrite).'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect same source with GET followed by POST to /api/settings/database within 10–300 second window. Anomalous pattern suggests export-modify-reimport workflow. Baseline normal backup/restore cycles to reduce FP.

suggestion.title: Out-of-band database file manipulation (SQLite/.db file access)
suggestion.rationale: 9routers likely uses a file-based database (SQLite). Attacker could bypass API by directly manipulating database file if filesystem access compromised. Article mentions database but not schema.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file-system access to 9routers database files (.db, .sqlite, etc.) outside of the application process. Look for copy/read/modify of DB files via cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or file explorer from non-standard user contexts.

suggestion.title: iCagenda CVE-2026-48939 Vulnerability Scan
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly lists CVE-2026-48939 as CISA KEV (actively exploited), Federal patch due 2026-07-13. No vulnerability detection rule generated despite this being primary initial-access detection vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query for iCagenda HTTP signatures (Joomla component paths, version fingerprinting responses). Asset inventory query for CVE-2026-48939 patches across exposed web-facing instances. Given active KEV exploitation, prioritize against 2026-07-13 deadline.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Upload to iCagenda Attachment Handler
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'upload of arbitrary files in the file attachment feature' as exploitation mechanism. Zero detection rules for upload anomalies despite explicit attack description.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor POST requests to iCagenda upload endpoints for file-type anomalies: PHP/PHTML/PHAR extensions in attachment submissions. Alert on Content-Type mismatches (e.g., PHP file masqueraded as image). Correlate upload success (HTTP 200/301) with subsequent access to uploaded path.

suggestion.title: PHP Code Execution from Web Upload Directory
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'PHP code upload and execution' as outcome. This is the post-exploitation persistence mechanism but pipeline generated zero web-shell detection rules.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PHP interpreter execution spawning child processes (shell, cmd.exe) from web-accessible upload directories (/media/, /temp/, /attachments/). Correlate: new .php file in upload path + HTTP GET/POST to that file + process spawn with network egress.

suggestion.title: Web Shell Persistence Post-iCagenda Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation path 'ultimately resulting in PHP code upload and execution' implies attacker persistence infrastructure. Article provides no IOC signatures but web-shell activity is detectable via behavioral anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt PHP processes from web-serving user accounts making unexpected outbound connections or spawning command shells. Check upload directories for recently-created .php files with suspicious execution patterns (high entropy, base64 strings, eval() calls).

suggestion.title: iCagenda Instance Exposure Inventory
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV status means 'currently being exploited in the wild.' Article emphasizes Federal remediation deadline 2026-07-13. Asset discovery is prerequisite for any mitigation workflow but pipeline generated no scanning rules.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query proxy/firewall logs for all outbound HTTPS traffic to port 443 containing iCagenda admin paths (/administrator/, /component/com_icagenda/). Correlate with asset database; flag unpatched instances, prioritize immediate remediation.

suggestion.title: iCagenda Dangerous File Type Upload Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unrestricted upload of file with dangerous type' and 'arbitrary files in the file attachment feature'—should detect POST requests to iCagenda upload endpoints with dangerous extensions (.php, .phtml, .php3) or MIME-type mismatches.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor iCagenda upload endpoints (commonly /upload, /attachment, /media, /files) for POST requests where file extension or MIME type indicates executable code. Flag uploads of .php, .phtml, .php3, .php5, or binaries with image MIME types.

suggestion.title: PHP Code Execution from iCagenda Upload Directory
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'PHP code upload and execution'—requires detection of process execution or file-access patterns from known iCagenda upload directories, establishing the execution phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PHP interpreter (php.exe, php-cgi.exe, or web-server PHP handlers) executing scripts from iCagenda upload directories. Flag child processes spawned by web-server process with working directory or file-access paths rooted in upload locations.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Child Process Spawning from iCagenda Web Server
suggestion.rationale: Article describes RCE via file attachment exploitation—web-server process should not spawn cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or bash under normal operation. This flags execution post-exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of iCagenda web-server process (w3wp.exe, httpd.exe, php-fpm) behavior. Alert on child-process creation of shells (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, /bin/bash) or system-modification tools (reg.exe, sc.exe) originating from web-server context.

suggestion.title: Vulnerability Scanner Match for CVE-2026-48939
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly recommends scanning: 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' with 'match against your vulnerability scanner'—operationalize CVE-2026-48939 plugin/signature detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference vulnerability scan results for CVE-2026-48939 matches against asset inventory. Escalate if vulnerable iCagenda instance is internet-facing or unpatched beyond federal due date 2026-07-13.

suggestion.title: Detect Unrestricted File Upload to iCagenda Attachment Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unrestricted upload of file with dangerous type' and 'arbitrary files in the file attachment feature'—this is the exploitation vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor POST/PUT requests to iCagenda upload paths (/upload, /attachment, /media) for executable or script-type file extensions (php, phtml, php3-php8, pht, phar). Alert on successful 200-201 responses followed by HTTP requests to those uploaded file paths from external or unexpected sources.

suggestion.title: Detect PHP Script Execution from Upload Directories
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'PHP code upload and execution' as the exploitation outcome, requiring post-upload execution detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP GET/POST requests to PHP files located in non-standard directories (/uploads/, /attachments/, /tmp/, /media/). Correlate with preceding POST requests to upload endpoints within a short time window. Flag access patterns consistent with web shell invocation (query parameters, high request volume, non-browser user agents).

suggestion.title: Asset Inventory: Identify Public-Facing iCagenda Instances
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV indicates active exploitation of exposed instances; article states 'publicly-facing application' context implies internet-accessible iCagenda deployments require immediate patch verification.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory and vulnerability scanner output for iCagenda instances. Cross-reference with external DNS records and certificate logs to identify internet-facing deployments. Verify patch status against CVE-2026-48939 remediation due date (2026-07-13). Alert on any unpatched or unscanned instances.

suggestion.title: Detect Suspicious File Extension Obfuscation in Uploads
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies unrestricted dangerous-type uploads; detection should cover filename evasion patterns (double extensions, null bytes, unicode) common in bypass attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor iCagenda attachment upload requests for obfuscated filenames: .php.jpg, .php%00.jpg, .phtml, files with trailing dots/spaces, or unicode-encoded extensions. Validate Content-Type headers against actual file signatures (magic bytes). Alert if MIME type declaration conflicts with file content analysis.

suggestion.title: Detect Web Shell Backdoor Commands Post-Upload
suggestion.rationale: Successful PHP upload enables persistent code execution; detection should identify command-execution patterns consistent with web shell operation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate successful file uploads with subsequent HTTP requests containing shell command signatures: system(), exec(), passthru(), shell_exec(), backtick execution, or encoded base64 payloads in query/POST parameters. Flag requests from non-browser user agents or with suspicious query string patterns (cmd=, execute=, id=, os=).

suggestion.title: Monitor Web Root File Modifications Following Upload Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article describes PHP code execution from uploaded files; file integrity monitoring on web-accessible directories provides post-exploitation forensics.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enable file change monitoring on iCagenda web root and upload directories. Alert on new .php files created outside normal deployment windows, or on modifications to existing .php files with unusual content signatures (base64-encoded blocks, eval() calls, obfuscated variable names). Correlate with preceding HTTP upload activity.

suggestion.title: iCagenda Internet-Facing Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes vulnerability is actively exploited (CISA KEV status) against exposed instances. Phrase: 'CISA KEV entry. The U.S. federal "Known Exploited Vulnerabilities" catalog only adds CVEs that have been **observed exploited in the wild**.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inventory internet-facing iCagenda instances via port scanning for web server signatures, checking HTTP response headers for component disclosure, and probing default admin paths. Correlate with proxy logs for repeated requests to /com_icagenda/ paths pre-exploitation.

suggestion.title: Unrestricted File Upload to Attachment Feature
suggestion.rationale: Article core vulnerability: 'allows the upload of arbitrary files in the file attachment feature'. Must detect upload operations prior to execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP POST/PUT to iCagenda upload endpoints (/components/com_icagenda/upload*, /attachments/*) containing executable MIME types (.php, .phtml, .phps, .phar, .phpt) or polyglot files. Establish per-user baseline upload frequency to detect weaponized campaigns.

suggestion.title: PHP Execution from Uploaded Attachment
suggestion.rationale: Article states compromise results in 'PHP code upload and execution'; distinguishes exploitation from mere file write. Phrase: 'ultimately resulting in PHP code upload and execution'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for child processes spawned from web server daemon (apache2, php-fpm, nginx) with command-line arguments indicating reconnaissance or persistence. Correlate timing with suspicious file creation in web-accessible upload directories to confirm post-exploitation activity.

suggestion.title: Suspicious File in iCagenda Attachment Directory
suggestion.rationale: Detection of written payload on disk. Phrase: 'allows the upload of arbitrary files in the file attachment feature'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file creation events in iCagenda component directories (typically */components/com_icagenda/uploads/*) with non-standard extensions or ownership inconsistent with legitimate uploads. Establish whitelist of expected files and ownership patterns.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Network Activity from Web Server
suggestion.rationale: Uploaded PHP code enabling secondary objectives; article's KEV status implies live actor campaigns beyond initial exploitation. Phrase: 'PHP code upload and execution' without limiting to single interaction.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound TCP/UDP initiated from web server process context (apache2, php-fpm) to non-RFC1918 destinations on non-standard ports (excluding 80/443). Correlate with DNS queries from web daemon and suspicious child process creation to establish C2 chain.

suggestion.title: iCagenda Arbitrary File Upload — PHP in Attachments
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'upload of arbitrary files in the file attachment feature, ultimately resulting in PHP code upload and execution.' Pipeline generated zero use cases despite explicit execution vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor iCagenda file attachment endpoints for POST requests containing .php files or double-extension payloads (e.g., shell.php.jpg). Track PHP process spawning from web root directories following upload requests. Alert on suspicious child processes launched by PHP interpreters in web-accessible folders.

suggestion.title: iCagenda Asset Exposure — Internet-Facing Instances
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes T1190 (Exploit Public-Facing Application) and CISA KEV context ('observed exploited in the wild'). Detecting exposed iCagenda instances is the canonical initial hunt before looking for exploit payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify iCagenda instances on the internet by fingerprinting characteristic web paths (e.g., /administrator/index.php, /components/com_icagenda). Cross-reference with internal asset inventory; flag any exposure. Correlate with proxy logs for inbound access to iCagenda services.

suggestion.title: iCagenda Upload Endpoint — File Type Validation Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Core vulnerability is 'unrestricted upload'—no file-type validation. Pipeline should detect attempts to upload executable or script files where filtering should block them.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful file uploads with executable MIME types (.php, .php5, .phtml, .exe, .jsp, .asp) to iCagenda attachment directories. Monitor for files appearing in upload directories that do not match the original request Content-Type header (MIME-type mismatch).

suggestion.title: PHP Code Execution in Web-Accessible Upload Directory
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'PHP code upload and execution.' Detection should trigger on any evidence that uploaded PHP was executed, not just uploaded.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect php.exe or php-cgi.exe spawning unusual child processes (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash) from web-accessible directories. Correlate PHP process creation timestamps with prior file upload requests to the same iCagenda instance via web logs.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48939 Vulnerability Scanner Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article is a CISA KEV entry stating 'patch due 2026-07-13'—vulnerability scanners must flag iCagenda instances that have not been patched. Pipeline should generate a scanner-focused hunt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan all internet-facing iCagenda instances for CVE-2026-48939 presence. Cross-reference vulnerability scanner results with patch management database to identify systems missing updates. Prioritize remediation by federal deadline (2026-07-13) and exposure vector.

suggestion.title: Orchard Action proof validation bypasses (soundness violation)

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Zcash node logs for Orchard Action proofs that pass validation despite missing or zero-valued base-point constraints. Alert on proofs validated faster than baseline (indicating skipped constraint checks) or accepted with malformed diversified-address fields.

suggestion.title: Zcash ledger consensus divergence (patched vs. unpatched nodes)
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'breaking Orchard Action circuit soundness.' Mixed patch levels cause patched nodes to reject transactions unpatched nodes accept, leading to chain divergence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect consensus failures where transaction acceptance rates diverge between Zcash nodes, or where nodes report different chain tips. Flag reorg events and ledger divergence correlated with node version mismatches.

suggestion.title: Forged Orchard note double-spend via soundness violation
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'under-constrained base' allows crafting multiple valid proofs for the same commitment. Hunt for duplicate nullifiers or multiple proofs claiming the same note.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan Zcash blockchain for Orchard transactions with identical nullifiers (note commitments) but different proofs or timestamps. Flag anomalies: multiple valid proofs for a single shielded note within a short time window.

suggestion.title: halo2_gadgets vulnerable-version supply-chain exposure

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate all codebases and deployed artifacts that import halo2_gadgets with version < 0.5.0. Identify both direct and transitive dependencies across internal Zcash ecosystem, cryptocurrency projects, and privacy libraries.

suggestion.title: Orchard Action circuit constraint-check omission patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'missing copy constraint in halo2_gadgets variable-base scalar multiplication.' Root cause is an omitted constraint enforcement. Hunt for similar patterns in other circuits or gadgets.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor halo2_gadgets circuits for execution paths where copy constraints are skipped or conditional checks are bypassed. Flag provers that succeed without satisfying all expected constraints, or variable-base multiplications that don't enforce base-point properties.

suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unrestricted upload of file with dangerous type' and 'PHP code upload' via attachment feature. Zero detection use cases generated for upload-based initial access despite explicit threat.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48939 Vulnerable iCagenda Inventory

suggestion.title: iCagenda Upload Endpoint Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes file attachment feature as sole attack vector. Pipeline failed to generate WAF/proxy-based detections for common upload bypass techniques (null bytes, case variation, MIME spoofing).

suggestion.title: iCagenda CVE-2026-48939 Unrestricted File Upload Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unrestricted upload of file with dangerous type vulnerability that allows the upload of arbitrary files in the file attachment feature'—direct detection gap for malicious uploads to iCagenda instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP POST requests to iCagenda file attachment endpoints for uploads of executable file types (.php, .phtml, .exe, .sh). Alert on Content-Type mismatches (e.g., .php uploaded as image/jpeg). Correlate with application error logs showing upload acceptance.

suggestion.title: PHP Code Execution Post-iCagenda Upload
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'ultimately resulting in PHP code upload and execution'—execution phase must detect PHP interpreter invocation triggered by user-controlled uploads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PHP interpreter (php.exe, php-cgi) spawning from or with working directory pointing to iCagenda upload folder. Monitor for HTTP requests to uploaded files (e.g., /uploads/*.php) followed by spawned child processes. Alert on web server worker process executing unregistered PHP scripts.

suggestion.title: Dangerous File Type Attachment Filtering Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Article describes vulnerability allows 'arbitrary files' uploads despite dangerous type restrictions—indicates filtering evasion or complete lack of validation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect iCagenda requests with double extensions (.php.jpg), null-byte injections, or MIME type mismatches on file attachments. Monitor for requests uploading polyglot files or appending PHP content to image files. Alert on any file type reaching the filesystem that wasn't explicitly whitelisted.

suggestion.title: iCagenda Asset Inventory & Federal Patch Compliance (CVE-2026-48939)
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'Federal patch due: 2026-07-13'—critical for compliance hunt and inventory. Pipeline should detect deployed iCagenda instances and check patch status against deadline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner for CVE-2026-48939 matches and iCagenda version detection. Cross-reference asset inventory for unpatched instances. Generate compliance report showing remediation status and days remaining until 2026-07-13 deadline. Flag any instances still running vulnerable versions.

suggestion.title: Web Shell Persistence via iCagenda Upload
suggestion.rationale: Article's 'PHP code upload and execution' implies web shell placement risk—attackers gain persistent access via uploaded backdoor scripts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for PHP files created in iCagenda upload directories matching known web shell signatures or containing eval/system/exec functions. Alert on recurring HTTP requests to freshly-created PHP files with parameter passing (e.g., /uploads/shell.php?cmd=...). Correlate with absence of legitimate file management activity.

suggestion.title: iCagenda Dangerous File Type Upload Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'unrestricted upload of file with dangerous type vulnerability that allows the upload of arbitrary files…ultimately resulting in PHP code upload and execution.' No detection logic was generated for file extension validation bypass or suspicious MIME type mismatches in upload traffic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor iCagenda upload endpoints (e.g., `/index.php?view=upload`, file attachment features) for POST requests with .php, .phtml, .jsp, .asp, .aspx extensions or PHP MIME type mismatches. Flag requests where Content-Type header contradicts file extension (e.g., image/jpeg with .php name).

suggestion.title: PHP Execution in Web Upload Directory
suggestion.rationale: The attack results in 'PHP code upload and execution'—implying files are written to a web-accessible directory and executed. No UC for detecting newly-written PHP files or executable access patterns in upload folders.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on PHP files written to common web upload directories (/uploads, /attachments, /files, /tmp with web access). Cross-correlate file-creation events with subsequent HTTP requests to those file paths, especially with query strings or POST payloads that suggest parameter passing.

suggestion.title: iCagenda Vulnerability Scanner Evasion via File Rename
suggestion.rationale: Phrase 'upload of arbitrary files' suggests polyglot or double-extension bypass (e.g., .php.jpg, .phtml) to evade upload filters. No detection for obfuscated file extensions in upload traffic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect upload POST requests with suspicious file extensions (.php.*, .phtml.*, .shtml.*, .jhtml.*) or null-byte injection attempts (.php%00.jpg). Flag uploads with filename/MIME-type mismatches where attacker may be attempting double-extension or encoding tricks.

suggestion.title: iCagenda Service Reconnaissance for CVE-2026-48939
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entry implies active exploitation—defenders need to know which systems are running iCagenda. No IOC or hunt for product identification before patch windows close (due 2026-07-13).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query web server logs and network traffic for iCagenda version strings, known endpoint patterns (e.g., `index.php?view=`, iCagenda-specific User-Agent strings, or X-Powered-By headers). Identify all instances in your environment for rapid patching and segmentation.

suggestion.title: POST to iCagenda Upload Endpoint with Content-Disposition Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Article confirms attack vector is 'file attachment feature'—likely multipart/form-data uploads. No UC for detecting anomalous Content-Disposition headers or multi-stage uploads that bypass server-side validation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor multipart/form-data POST requests to iCagenda file attachment endpoints for oversized payloads, missing Content-Disposition headers, or mismatched field names. Alert on repeated failed uploads followed by successful binary write—signature of validation-bypass attempts.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48939 Asset Exposure Scan Match
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly directs: 'Standard asset-exposure hunt — the canonical Splunk SPL and Defender KQL live once in [...TEMPLATES.md#asset-exposure].' Pipeline generated zero use cases despite this guidance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate vulnerability scanner detections for CVE-2026-48939 against iCagenda installations. Flag assets not patched by federal due date 2026-07-13. Cross-check patch status in WSUS, Qualys, or equivalent and validate applied patches.

suggestion.title: Suspicious File Upload to iCagenda Attachment Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article states core attack: 'upload of arbitrary files in the file attachment feature.' Pipeline generated no file-write detection UC despite explicit description of upload vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on uploads of non-document file types (.php, .phtml, .php3, .php4, .php5, .phar, .phps, .exe, .bat, .com, .scr) to known iCagenda attachment directories. Baseline legitimate upload patterns and file sizes first to reduce FP.

suggestion.title: PHP Code Execution Following File Upload
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes attack outcome: 'PHP code upload and execution.' Pipeline failed to generate execution-phase detection despite clear attack chain establishing code-execution goal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for PHP interpreter (php.exe, php-cgi) spawning unexpected child processes or executing suspicious commands immediately after suspicious file writes to web-accessible directories. Correlate upload timestamps with execution timestamps.

suggestion.title: iCagenda Installation Discovery and Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article references remediation deadline implying asset inventory requirement. Product 'iCagenda' is the primary IOC the pipeline should have extracted but did not. No inventory detection generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify iCagenda instances via HTTP header analysis, HTTP Server banners, DNS records, network protocol signatures, application discovery tools, and package manager logs. Establish baseline of deployments and cross-reference against patch registry.

suggestion.title: Exploitation Attempts Against iCagenda File Upload Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV status signals active in-the-wild exploitation. Article states vulnerability is in public-facing 'file attachment feature.' Pipeline generated zero IOCs or web-layer detection UCs despite this being the initial-access vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor POST/PUT requests to iCagenda file upload endpoints for null bytes, path-traversal sequences, double extensions, known payload signatures, or rejected file-type attempts. Establish baseline of legitimate upload volume and file types; alert on deviations.

suggestion.title: Unrestricted File Upload to iCagenda Attachment Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'allows the upload of arbitrary files in the file attachment feature' — baseline detection for executable file types (PHP, PHTML, JSP, ASPX) in upload requests.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP POST/PUT to iCagenda file attachment endpoints containing PHP/executable extensions in multipart payloads. Establish baseline of legitimate attachment MIME types and alert on deviations, particularly double-extensions or null-byte bypass patterns.

suggestion.title: PHP Code Execution from iCagenda Upload Directory
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'PHP code upload and execution' — direct gap in pipeline's kill-chain. Execution phase must correlate upload with subprocess spawning.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate HTTP POST to iCagenda upload endpoints with PHP interpreter execution (php.exe, php-cgi, or child processes from w3wp.exe, apache2, etc.) within 30 seconds. Alert on execution of recently-created files in web-accessible upload or temp directories.

suggestion.title: Webshell Command & Control via iCagenda Upload
suggestion.rationale: Article enables PHP execution capability; attackers will pivot to C2 via webshell POST requests, which pipeline did not model as persistent threat.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for sustained HTTP activity to iCagenda upload directories with C2 patterns: encoded query parameters, command-like payloads, base64/hex encoding in POST body, consistent User-Agent anomalies, or responses with system output characteristics.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48939 Vulnerable Asset Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes CISA KEV status ('currently exploited') and federal remediation deadline of 2026-07-13 — pipeline omitted vulnerability scanning IOC and patch-gap identification.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan all internet-facing assets for iCagenda product identification and version signatures vulnerable to CVE-2026-48939. Cross-reference patch deployment logs to identify unpatched instances. Prioritize by external exposure and time-to-deadline.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Process Spawning from Web Application Pool
suggestion.rationale: Article's PHP execution implies attacker code execution within web server context — need behavioral detection for shell spawning (cmd.exe, powershell.exe) from w3wp.exe or apache2.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when w3wp.exe, apache2, nginx, or other web server processes spawn command shells (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, /bin/bash, /bin/sh) or tools commonly used in post-exploitation (curl, wget, whoami, net.exe). Establish baseline of legitimate application behavior and treat deviations as high-fidelity.

suggestion.title: Unrestricted File Upload to iCagenda Instance
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'unrestricted upload of file with dangerous type vulnerability that allows the upload of arbitrary files in the file attachment feature.' Pipeline missed detection for upload POST/PUT to iCagenda endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor web server logs and network events for POST/PUT requests to iCagenda file upload endpoints (typically `/upload`, `/attachment`, or component-specific paths) with file extensions not in whitelist or content-type mismatches. Correlate with iCagenda process or IIS/Apache logs.

suggestion.title: PHP Code Execution in Web Application Directory
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'PHP code upload and execution'—detection needed for execution of uploaded PHP within web root. Pipeline failed to suggest hunting for PHP process spawns or script execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for php.exe or php-cgi.exe child processes spawned by web server (w3wp.exe, apache2, nginx) and detect file writes of .php, .php5, .phtml files to web-accessible directories. Cross-reference timing with upload logs.

suggestion.title: iCagenda Instance Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article references 'exposed assets' and includes asset-exposure hunt template; pipeline produced no use case for discovering internet-facing iCagenda instances vulnerable to this exploit.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query passive DNS, shodan/censys, or active web scanner results for iCagenda fingerprints (HTTP headers, default paths `/index.php?option=com_icagenda`, `/components/com_icagenda/). Cross-reference against CVE-2026-48939 vulnerability scanners.

suggestion.title: Dangerous File Type Upload Bypass Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifically mentions 'unrestricted upload of file with dangerous type'—but pipeline missed UC for detecting upload validation bypass (double-extension, null-byte, MIME-type mismatch).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on uploads with Content-Type mismatches (e.g., Content-Type: image/jpeg but filename ends .php), double extensions (.php.jpg), or null-byte injection attempts to iCagenda upload endpoints. Flag requests that bypass expected MIME validation.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Upload to iCagenda Attachment Feature
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'allows the upload of arbitrary files in the file attachment feature' but pipeline generated zero file-upload detection rules despite this being the primary attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor POST requests to iCagenda attachment endpoints for multipart form-data containing executable file extensions (.php, .phtml, .shtml, .exe) regardless of declared Content-Type header. Correlate HTTP 2xx responses with file-creation events in web-accessible upload directories within 10 seconds.

suggestion.title: PHP Interpreter Spawning from Web-Writable Upload Paths
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'PHP code upload and execution' as attack outcome but pipeline generated no execution-phase detection for PHP subprocess spawning from iCagenda uploads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect web server processes (httpd, nginx, IIS) spawning php.exe, php-cgi, or php-fpm child processes with command-line arguments referencing iCagenda upload or attachment directories. Flag execution events correlating with recent multipart form submissions or containing base64-encoded/obfuscated payloads.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48939 iCagenda Vulnerability Presence Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' via template substitution and specifies CISA KEV status with federal patch deadline 2026-07-13, but pipeline generated zero vulnerability-scanner or patch-compliance detection logic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scan results for iCagenda instances (any version pre-2026-07-13) flagged with CVE-2026-48939. Prioritize internet-facing assets. Cross-reference with network telemetry for anomalous outbound connections or service probing post-disclosure date (2026-07-10).

suggestion.title: Cypher syntax keywords in Langroid prompts and LLM inputs
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'query text is influenceable by prompt injection (direct user input or indirect content the agent reads back via RAG).' The injection vector is the prompt itself. Detection should identify prompts/inputs containing Cypher keywords before Neo4j execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for HTTP requests or application log entries where Langroid receives prompts containing Cypher syntax (DETACH DELETE, LOAD CSV, CALL apoc, CALL dbms). Correlate timestamps with subsequent Neo4j query.log entries containing same keywords to confirm prompt-to-query injection succeeded. Baseline normal prompts and alert on anomalies.

suggestion.title: APOC library enabled or loaded in Neo4j runtime/config
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies APOC/dbms procedures as the RCE landing pad ('APOC/dbms Cypher-to-RCE landing'). APOC must be explicitly enabled. Detection should identify when APOC procedures become available in the database.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for: (1) neo4j.conf edits enabling APOC (dbms.security.procedures.unrestricted patterns), (2) Neo4j startup logs showing APOC jar/plugin loading, (3) Queries invoking apoc.* or dbms.* procedures from non-admin sessions. Flag first-time APOC invocations by service accounts.

suggestion.title: Langroid service account permission escalation in Neo4j
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes unvalidated queries with no allowlist. If Langroid service account runs read-only, injection of DETACH DELETE or APOC.execute fails at permission level—detection should flag when service account queries attempt forbidden operations or exceed assigned role.
log_sources: Neo4j query execution logs with permission context
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track Langroid service account's baseline role and assigned Cypher privileges. Flag queries attempting WRITE, ADMIN, or APOC operations from that account. Flag new service accounts created for Langroid access. Flag sudden permission changes to existing Langroid accounts.

suggestion.title: Langroid Neo4jChatAgent config disabling validation or allowlist
suggestion.rationale: Title notes 'config-conditional RCE'—security is config-dependent. Detection should identify deployments where query validation is explicitly disabled or statement allowlists are absent/empty.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan Langroid configs for Neo4jChatAgent sections where: (1) `query_validation_enabled=false`, (2) `allow_list` or `statement_allowlist` is empty/null, (3) `disable_cypher_validation=true` or similar. Flag configs merging defaults that disable guardrails. Correlate with vulnerability scanner results and breach timelines.

suggestion.title: Mass graph data destruction via DETACH DELETE operations
suggestion.rationale: Article lists T1485 (Data Destruction). DETACH DELETE can obliterate nodes/relationships at scale. Detection should flag mass deletion operations deviating from baseline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline DETACH DELETE volume and scope per authenticated session. Alert on: (1) single DETACH DELETE removing >1000 nodes/relationships, (2) DETACH DELETE without WHERE clauses, (3) mass deletions outside scheduled maintenance windows. Correlate timing with observed prompt injection attempts or Cypher syntax keywords in logs.

suggestion.title: APOC export operations exfiltrating data to external hosts
suggestion.rationale: Article lists T1567 (Exfiltration Over Web Service). apoc.export.* can write graph data to remote URLs. Detection should identify APOC export procedures with external destinations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for Cypher queries calling apoc.export.* functions with remote URLs (http://, https://, ftp://) in parameters. Correlate with outbound network traffic from Neo4j JVM. Establish baseline of legitimate APOC exports and alert on: new destinations, high-volume transfers, export calls outside administrative sessions, or exports occurring after suspicious Cypher activity detected.

suggestion.title: iCagenda Unrestricted File Upload Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'allows the upload of arbitrary files in the file attachment feature'—the core attack vector. Pipeline missed any detection for file upload attempts to iCagenda endpoints, which is the initial exploitation step.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP POST/PUT requests to iCagenda upload endpoints (e.g., /upload, /attachment, /files). Alert on requests with file extensions matching dangerous types (.php, .phtml, .php7, .exe, .jsp) or Content-Type mismatches (e.g., application/x-php in multipart form). Correlate against iCagenda version scanning to map vulnerable instances.

suggestion.title: PHP Code Execution from Web Upload Directory
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly says 'PHP code upload and execution'—yet no detection for the execution phase. Post-upload, attackers will execute the malicious PHP file, typically through web server process (apache/nginx/IIS) spawning PHP interpreter.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on php.exe, php-cgi.exe, or php-fpm process creation where parent is a web server (httpd, nginx, apache, w3wp) and command line references files in known upload directories (/var/www/uploads, /iCagenda/uploads, etc.). Correlate with recent file creation events in those directories.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Executable File Creation in Web-Accessible Directory
suggestion.rationale: Article describes file upload leading to PHP execution—detection must cover file-system indicator of successful upload. No UC suggested for monitoring .php file creation in web directories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on creation of executable file types (.php, .phtml, .php7, .phar, .jsp, .aspx) within web-accessible directories, especially those associated with iCagenda installations (/var/www/html/iCagenda/*, /opt/iCagenda/uploads/*). Filter out legitimate updates/patches by excluding known file hashes and maintenance windows.

suggestion.title: iCagenda Asset Inventory & Vulnerable Instance Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt'—pipeline should generate asset-discovery UC to identify iCagenda instances before they are exploited. No inventory or scanning detection provided.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner results for CVE-2026-48939 matches. Search web server logs and HTTP traffic for User-Agent or X-Header patterns matching iCagenda (e.g., 'iCagenda/*'). Correlate DNS queries and reverse-DNS lookups for common iCagenda paths (/index.php?view=agenda, /administrator). Flag any exposures with public internet accessibility.

suggestion.title: Suspicious HTTP Requests to iCagenda Upload Endpoints with Dangerous MIME Types
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'unrestricted upload of file with dangerous type'—no detection for MIME-type mismatches or content validation bypass attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor multipart/form-data POST requests to iCagenda upload endpoints. Alert on Content-Type header mismatches (e.g., claiming image/jpeg but containing PHP markers like '<?php'). Flag requests where declared file extension doesn't match body content (magic bytes check). Include baseline of legitimate uploads from known administrative IPs.

suggestion.title: iCagenda Process Anomaly & Remote Command Execution Post-Upload
suggestion.rationale: After PHP upload and execution, attackers will invoke system commands (whoami, id, nc, curl for reverse shell). Article does not discuss post-exploitation, but standard practice for file-upload-to-RCE requires detection of suspicious child processes spawned by PHP.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected child process creation under php.exe (or web server process) with parent initiated from remote HTTP request. Monitor command-line arguments for indicators: shell invocation (sh, bash, cmd.exe), network tools (curl, wget, nc, nslookup), or process spawning (exec, system, passthru). Correlate with suspicious file creation in uploads within last 5 minutes.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure: CVE-2026-48939 iCagenda Vulnerability Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly directs: 'Substitute this CVE wherever the template references <CVE>' for asset-exposure hunt. This is the foundational detection for any CISA KEV entry. No use case generated despite clear instruction.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan external-facing assets for iCagenda installations matching CVE-2026-48939. Prioritize by federal due-date (2026-07-13). Correlate vulnerability scanner results with web server fingerprinting to confirm product version and exposure.

suggestion.title: Malicious File Upload to iCagenda Attachment Feature
suggestion.rationale: Article describes core attack vector: 'allows the upload of arbitrary files in the file attachment feature.' No detection for this primary exploitation step exists despite being explicitly described.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor iCagenda file attachment endpoints for POST requests uploading executable file types (.php, .phtml, .php3, .php4, .php5, .phar, .phps) or MIME-type mismatches (e.g., image/jpeg with .php extension). Flag polyglot files and double-extension uploads.

suggestion.title: PHP Code Execution from iCagenda Upload Directory
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'ultimately resulting in PHP code upload and execution.' Execution-phase detection absent despite being the terminal attack step.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on php.exe, php-cgi, or CLI spawning from iCagenda web directories (/media/com_icagenda/, /components/com_icagenda/). Monitor for system command execution (cmd.exe, powershell, bash) invoked by web server processes. Flag base64-encoded payloads or eval/exec patterns in HTTP requests to these directories.

suggestion.title: Web Shell Persistence Post-iCagenda Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article implies malicious PHP upload establishes code execution capability. Persistence detection (detecting attacker-placed web shells, backdoors) is missing but critical for post-compromise hunting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor iCagenda directories for newly created or recently modified .php files outside deployment windows. Cross-reference file timestamps with upload logs. Alert on web shell signatures (<?php system($_GET), passthru, exec, proc_open) in uploaded files.

suggestion.title: iCagenda File Upload to Web Root
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'upload of arbitrary files in the file attachment feature, ultimately resulting in PHP code upload and execution'—need detection for files being written to web-accessible directory post-upload.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor web server file system writes to iCagenda upload directories for files with PHP, phtml, php3, php4, php5, phar extensions immediately following HTTP POST to /upload or /attachment endpoints. Correlate with subsequent process spawning (php.exe, php-cgi) in child processes of web server.

suggestion.title: iCagenda Public Exposure Discovery
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'Recommended hunts: Standard asset-exposure hunt' and CISA KEV status means active exploitation in wild—need asset inventory for internet-facing iCagenda instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan network for listening services on ports 80, 443, 8080 responding with iCagenda headers (Server: Apache/Nginx + iCagenda theme in HTTP response). Cross-reference against asset inventory for patches applied post 2026-07-13 deadline.

suggestion.title: Suspicious PHP Execution Post-Upload
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability 'resulting in PHP code upload and execution'—need process-level detection for unexpected PHP interpreters spawning under web server context post-file-upload.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on php.exe, php-cgi.exe, or php command execution spawned by apache2, nginx, w3wp parent process within 5 seconds of file write events to attachment/upload directories. Exclude known legitimate PHP scripts; escalate if .php file was written in same window from external IP.

suggestion.title: iCagenda HTTP POST to Upload Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation requires 'file attachment feature'—need HTTP request-level detection for attempts to use iCagenda's upload functionality.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP POST requests to /upload, /attachment, /file, /media endpoints on hosts running iCagenda. Flag requests with Content-Type: application/x-php or multipart/form-data containing .php/.phtml/.phar files. Baseline legitimate uploads by source IP/user-agent, alert on anomalies.

suggestion.title: iCagenda Dangerous File Type Upload
suggestion.rationale: Core vulnerability: 'unrestricted upload of file with dangerous type'—detection for executable/script file types bypassing upload filters.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on uploads where file extension or MIME type mismatch (e.g., .php with image/jpeg MIME), or where Content-Disposition filename contains executable extensions (.exe, .php, .sh, .bat, .ps1). Focus on iCagenda URIs known to handle file attachments.

suggestion.title: Unrestricted File Upload to iCagenda Attachment Feature
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unrestricted upload of file with dangerous type vulnerability that allows the upload of arbitrary files in the file attachment feature'—core attack vector. Needs detection for file type validation bypass or missing MIME-type checks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor web application logs for POST requests to iCagenda file upload endpoints (typically /upload, /attachment, /media) with suspicious file extensions (PHP, JSP, ASP, PHTML, etc.). Correlate with HTTP 200/201 responses indicating successful upload. Alert on rapid sequences of uploads within seconds.

suggestion.title: PHP Code Execution Post-File Upload
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'PHP code upload and execution'—indicates post-upload execution phase. Detection should cover process spawning and web shell activity following upload events.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PHP interpreter spawning child processes from web server context (w3wp.exe, httpd, apache2) immediately following file upload events. Look for unusual command-line arguments, reverse shells, or outbound connections initiated from PHP execution context.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48939 Vulnerability Scanner Match
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entry requires baseline scanning per asset-exposure template. Article specifies CVE identifier and patch deadline (2026-07-13)—needs scanner coverage verification.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan all iCagenda instances in the fleet for CVE-2026-48939 presence. Alert on any detected vulnerabilities. Cross-reference with patch management systems to identify lag between patch availability and deployment.

suggestion.title: Suspicious .PHP File in Web-Accessible Directories
suggestion.rationale: Article details 'arbitrary files' and 'PHP code upload and execution'—new PHP files appearing in web root or attachment directories are strong indicators of successful exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for new .php, .phtml, .php5 file creation in iCagenda web directories (/var/www/html/*, /opt/iCagenda/uploads/*, C:\inetpub\*). Flag files with encoding obfuscation, base64 payloads, or eval/assert calls in content.

suggestion.title: iCagenda Application Exposure Inventory
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV indicates active wild exploitation. Baseline hunt must identify all exposed iCagenda instances accessible from network boundaries—article implies web-facing deployment requirement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for iCagenda banners, version strings, or known path signatures (/index.php?option=com_icagenda) in web proxy logs, DNS queries, or reverse-DNS records. Correlate with firewall rules to confirm internet-facing exposure.

suggestion.title: Multi-Step File Upload Exploitation Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article's attack flow requires upload-then-access sequence. Detection should correlate file POST with subsequent GET/HEAD requests to confirm execution trigger.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate iCagenda file upload POST request (with suspicious extension) followed within 30 seconds by HTTP request to the uploaded file's URL (request for /uploads/shell.php or /attachment/backdoor.php). Flag if HTTP 200 response and response body contains PHP output or error messages.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48939 Asset Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'upload of arbitrary files in the file attachment feature' on public-facing iCagenda apps. Standard asset-exposure hunt mandatory for CISA KEV; federal agencies required to remediate by 2026-07-13.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan for exposed iCagenda instances (port 80/443 HTTP responses, certificate names, index page fingerprints). Cross-reference against vulnerability scanner results for CVE-2026-48939. Urgent: patch lag frequently explains breaches even in organizations believing themselves patched.

suggestion.title: Dangerous File Upload to Web Root
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'upload of arbitrary files' and 'ultimately resulting in PHP code upload and execution.' Monitor for .php/.phtml/.php3/.php4/.php5/.phtml uploaded to iCagenda /uploads or /attachments directories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP POST to iCagenda file-attachment endpoints with PHP/executable MIME types or extensions in multipart form-data. Flag when PHP files appear in web-accessible upload directories post-upload.

suggestion.title: PHP Code Execution from User-Writable Directory
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'PHP code upload and execution.' Post-compromise, attacker executes uploaded PHP via direct URL or include() calls.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP GET/POST to .php files in /uploads, /attachments, or /temp directories. Correlate with process-creation logs (php.exe, php-cgi.exe spawning from web server user context). Successful exploitation produces PHP output in access logs.

suggestion.title: iCagenda Installation Discovery
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies iCagenda as the affected product. Inventory step: locate all iCagenda instances across enterprise before targeted hunt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search DNS logs for iCagenda subdomains, certificate transparency logs for iCagenda hostnames. Network scanner for signature: iCagenda index pages contain 'iCagenda' in HTML title/source. Shodan/Censys queries for iCagenda.

suggestion.title: Exploit Kit / Scanner Traffic to iCagenda
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV indicates 'observed exploited in the wild'—threat actors actively scanning for vulnerable iCagenda instances. Inbound exploit attempts will precede compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests to iCagenda file-attachment endpoints with suspicious query parameters, polyglot payloads, or known exploit signatures. Monitor for repeated scanner probes to /attachments, /uploads from external IPs.
